entries.name: 0bull
entries.description: Control real iPhones rented from 0bull (screenshots, on-screen text, taps, typing, device commands, recorded macros, an on-phone agent) and publish videos to TikTok and YouTube Shorts from them, through the hosted 0bull Streamable HTTP MCP server plus three workflow skills. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Requires a 0bull account with a rented phone and browser OAuth consent (add the server with auth: oauth, then brodification mcp login 0bull); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Posting sends the user's video and caption to TikTok or YouTube through the phone's own apps. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; screenshots, on-screen text, anything typed on the phone (including passwords or codes you hand the agent) and your videos and captions go to 0bull.net; posts publish publicly to TikTok or YouTube; the server also exposes rental tools that spend money, which the skills tell the model never to call but brodification does not block.

entries.name: aave-mcp
entries.title: Aave
entries.description: Aave V3 and V4 through Aave's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.aave.com, no sign-in, no keys in config): live markets and rates on every chain Aave runs on, wallet positions and health factor, rewards, DAO governance, swap quotes, and unsigned transactions for the user's own wallet to sign. Bundles five workflow skills: safe transactions, deleverage, yield analysis, account activity and transaction confirmation. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.aave.com, which records tool usage for analytics and keeps a wallet address only as a keyed hash. The server never holds keys. Every tool is annotated read-only except submit_signed_order and cancel_order, which relay an order or cancellation the user already signed; the package marks the server untrusted, so brodification asks before either runs and refuses them in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: abstract-provider
entries.title: Abstract
entries.description: Abstract model provider (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K3) over the OpenAI Responses API with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); requests go to https://api.abstract.inc/v1 through brodification' own client with ABSTRACT_API_KEY, which brodification reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: accent-picker
entries.title: Accent Picker
entries.description: OKLCH accent colour picker for the brodification Desktop status bar: drag it and the whole theme retints live, with palette commands to reset to the theme default or copy the current colour. A theme-authoring tool; the colour is scratch state and is never persisted. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: account-pool
entries.title: Account Pool
entries.description: Run several accounts of one provider in brodification' credential pool: `brodification account <provider> <action>` adds accounts with email verification, shows live usage per account, keeps the least-used account first (fill_first + a 5-minute balance timer over every provider with accounts), parks accounts for hours or on a weekly schedule, shows which bot is on which account and its tokens at API prices, alerts on dead logins, a full pool or a runaway bot, and can start an idle account's 5-hour window with one tiny request (wake). Adapters for anthropic and openai-codex; generic commands for any pool provider. Optional Accounts page in brodification Desktop. Linux and Windows. Disclosure — logins stay in brodification: park holds an entry out of rotation in brodification' pool (mark_exhausted_and_rotate, reason "parked") and unpark is reset_status; the plugin's park list holds labels, ids and times only; expired tokens are refreshed by brodification (try_refresh_matching); sign-in, in the terminal and on the Desktop page, runs `brodification auth add`; other profiles' accounts are read with read_credential_pool. It uses each account's access token as brodification stores it for live usage and the email check (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /profile, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, with the client headers of brodification' usage fetcher) and for wake (a command, a page button, or the timer after the opt-in `wake auto-on`): one one-word request per account through brodification' Anthropic client or the Codex Responses endpoint, and the account's model list. Telegram alerts through `brodification send -t telegram` to the bot's home channel or a chat id kept in account-pool.json; no telemetry. Its session tracker, a post_api_request hook, runs in every profile and writes labels, ids and token counts only. `setup` writes plugins.enabled of every profile, links the plugin into every profile, removes the retired account-pool-tracker (`brodification plugins remove`) and, with --timer, adds a systemd user timer (Linux) or a Task Scheduler task for the user (Windows, no admin rights). Runs systemctl --user and notify-send (Linux), schtasks, powershell.exe and taskkill (Windows), brodification config set, brodification auth add/remove, brodification send, brodification plugins remove; reads every profile's config.yaml and state.db (read-only), the gateway config (whether the Telegram bot has a home channel) and /proc on Linux. The command registers in the default profile only and provides no tools. Live usage, the email check and wake send each account's own access token from brodification' pool straight to its vendor with Claude Code (anthropic) and Codex CLI (openai-codex) client headers. The session tracker reads the running agent's current pool account (label and id only) by scanning Python thread frames for brodification' private _credential_pool. On the first run after 3.x it moves parked logins from account-pool-parked.json back into brodification' pool and deletes that file.
known_issues: After installing, run `brodification account <provider> setup` (add --timer for the 5-minute balance timer): it lists the plugin in every profile for the Desktop page and links it into every profile for the session tracker. Coming from 3.x it also removes account-pool-tracker.

brodification can let a parked account back into rotation early (`brodification auth reset`, or a Codex quota it sees come back); the next balance run parks it again, and doctor names it until then. A park without --until is held for 30 days, and a balance run renews it once less than 15 days are left, so without the timer it ends after 30 days.

Windows: tested with a stand-in Task Scheduler and, up to 3.13, with Windows' own Python, cmd.exe and wscript.exe under Wine; not yet on a Windows machine. On Windows the timer runs only while the user is signed in.
Built for plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under host, brodification skips plugin CLI commands, so `brodification account` and the timer's balance are unavailable.

Usage comes from undocumented provider endpoints (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage) that can change or rate-limit without notice; bots are unaffected when they do.

The Desktop page's sign-in relays `brodification auth add` and has run in sandbox tests (brodification' real sign-in code, provider calls replaced), not yet with a new account on a real install. The Codex browser sign-in needs the browser on the same computer; when port 1455 is taken, brodification signs in with a device code instead.

entries.name: account-switcher
entries.description: Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local brodification profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of the gateway (and, on brodification before 0.22, of brodification Desktop). Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through brodification's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one brodification-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json. On brodification 0.22 and later it stops and restarts the gateway once brodification's own idle proof and the gateway's drain report idle, and brodification Desktop stays open and reconnects; on earlier brodification it also reads the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment and closes and reopens brodification Desktop (work started in the seconds after the idle check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

entries.name: acedatacloud-media
entries.title: Ace Data Cloud Media
entries.description: Suno music, Seedance video, HappyHorse (Happy Horse) video, GPT Image images and Nano Banana images by Ace Data Cloud; 17 selectable service toolsets and a Nano Banana image_generate backend. Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no brodification approval prompt; the model can choose costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 images), and prompts and reference URLs go to api.acedata.cloud. Prompts, reference URLs and face images go to api.acedata.cloud. The tools are on wherever you enable their toolsets, including gateways.

entries.title: Ace Data Cloud

entries.name: adaption
entries.description: Dataset import, adaptation, augmentation, translation, synthetic generation, and AutoScientist fine-tuning through the hosted Adaption MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with three workflow skills; the MCP server is added separately with OAuth (or an API key for headless use). Disclosure — skill-only, no code; the MCP tools call api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai, and launches spend Adaption credits (the skills request a cost estimate first, brodification does not enforce it). brodification does not prompt before those tools unless the server is configured with trust: untrusted.

entries.name: adspirer
entries.description: Create, analyze, and optimize campaigns across Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Amazon Ads, ChatGPT Ads, and Microsoft Ads through the hosted Adspirer MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with fourteen paid-media workflow skills and approval safeguards; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; confirm-before-spend is enforced by skill instructions, not by brodification.

entries.name: advanced-delegation
entries.title: Advanced Delegation
entries.description: Two extra delegation modes for `delegate_task`, next to the built-in default. Model routes (`delegation.backend: model_map`): the agent picks a named model route per subagent from a list you define (e.g. fast, deep, local). Profile routes (`delegation.backend: profile_routes`): the agent runs a subagent as one of your brodification profiles, with that profile's own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md. Only route names and their one-line descriptions reach the model. Adds `brodification delegation config` (pick the mode and edit its routes; `--show` prints the setup) and the `/delegation` slash command (switch modes for this session, or `--global` to save it). Needs a brodification core with pluggable delegation providers (0.22.5 or newer); on an older core it installs, logs one warning and does nothing. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network or model calls of its own; subagents run through core's `delegate_task` on the routes you configured. Writes only `delegation.backend` and `delegation.backends.*` (model_map / profile_routes) in the active profile's config.yaml, through core's config writer. A model route's optional `api_key` is stored in config.yaml in plain text (`provider:` keeps keys in .env / auth.json). Listing a profile under profile routes lets this profile's subagents use that profile's credentials, SOUL.md and terminal policy.

entries.name: advisor
entries.title: Advisor
entries.description: A persistent second model reviews every agent turn. After each turn the plugin hands the transcript to the model you nominate as advisor and delivers its findings as advice in the same session: [NIT], [CONCERN] or [BLOCKER] notes, held back until a later review raises the same point again, so the primary agent is not interrupted by a one-off remark. It reviews, it does not act: the advisor never edits files, calls tools or changes session state, and only reads the turn transcript. This is the backend counterpart of MoA — one extra model, not a committee: the primary agent does the work and the advisor checks it. Port of pi-omplike-advisor (Petr Baudis / pasky), itself rooted in oh-my-pi (Can Boluk). Runs inside the plugin host with no dependencies beyond brodification itself. Disclosure — once the plugin is enabled, every completed turn costs one extra completion through brodification's ctx.llm to the advisor model (the primary agent's provider unless you allow a provider/model override under plugins.entries.advisor.llm), carrying the user message, the final reply, every tool call and tool result in the session so far (each clipped to 500 characters) and the contents of a WATCHDOG.md in brodification's working directory if one exists; deliverable advice is queued into the CLI session as a user-role message, which starts or interrupts an agent turn; state is kept under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/advisor/ and reviews run on one background thread; no other network, files or credentials.
known_issues: Every reviewed turn costs one extra completion on the advisor model. Reviews run on a single worker in the background after the hook returns (the hook itself never blocks turn finalization), so a long advisor call delays advice, not the agent.

Advice is injected into the live conversation with ctx.inject_message, which the interactive CLI provides. On gateway surfaces (Telegram, Slack, ...) the review still runs and its notes are held, but there is no in-session place to inject them, so delivery is CLI-shaped.

Concerns are only delivered once a later review repeats them (hold-and-reconfirm), so a genuine one-off concern can stay silent by design. /advisor test <severity> <note> injects a synthetic note to see the delivery path.
The cross-provider trust gate is conservative: point the advisor at a provider different from the primary agent's, or accept the default inherit-primary behaviour.

The interactive provider/model picker (/advisor model with no argument) needs PluginContext.request_model_selection, and the status-bar badge needs ctx.register_status_segment. Where a build lacks those newer seams the plugin still loads and the text commands keep working (/advisor provider <name>, /advisor model <name>).
State lives in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/advisor/state.json, per profile.

entries.name: adwhispr
entries.description: Research competitor ads, clone the winners, and run campaigns through the hosted AdWhispr MCP. Finds brands verified to be advertising in a niche right now, their longest-running Meta and TikTok ads, Instagram content and Google keyword data; clones a proven ad into a finished image or AI video for your brand (free script approval before any credit is charged); and launches paused campaigns on Meta, Google, TikTok, X and ChatGPT Ads. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with twenty-four workflow skills; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (always created paused, two-step confirm server-side) and renders videos that use paid credits; the AdWhispr server is marked untrusted, so brodification asks before every write or spend tool and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Sends research queries and your brand assets to adwhispr.com; sign-in is OAuth through npx mcp-remote@0.1.49.

entries.name: afterforge
entries.description: Local-first regression workbench turning agent failures and corrections into reviewed, evidence-backed checks.

entries.name: agent-analytics
entries.description: Dashboard-only read plugin for Agent Analytics inside brodification.

entries.name: agent-batch
entries.description: Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; brodification phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT_BATCH_REPO, AGENT_BATCH_WORKFLOW, AGENT_BATCH_MODEL and AGENT_BATCH_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — brodification can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow_dispatch with your GITHUB_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys.

entries.name: agent-hint
entries.description: Give the inference engine behind each request a standard, machine-readable view of the agent session that produced it. Injects an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON: session identity and call index, lifecycle state, soft priority, a cache-pinning hint, optional measured statistics) on main LLM requests, and can emit session lifecycle events out of band as local ndjson or as POSTs to a URL you configure. Request bodies are never modified, and nothing is added or sent until the plugin is enabled. Lets a scheduler pin a session to the instance already holding its KV cache, or rank a user-blocked session above background work, without teaching the engine anything about the client. Disclosure — when enabled, every main LLM request carries an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON with the session id, call index, lifecycle state, priority and cache hints) to whatever provider is configured, not only hint-aware engines; with status_sink: http the same session events and usage/latency statistics are POSTed to the status_url you set, and ndjson writes them under $BRODIFICATION_HOME.

entries.name: agent-hold-em
entries.description: No-Limit Texas Hold 'Em for brodification Desktop: play with three isolated brodification profile agents using play chips only. Agent decisions use configured models and may consume provider tokens; this is a local game, not gambling software. Disclosure — each opponent is a zero-tool brodification agent run in-process under the local brodification profile you select for it, using that profile's configured provider credentials and spending its tokens; reads every local profile's name, model and avatar for the picker; stores the table (including hole cards) in plugin-data/agent-hold-em/table.json.

entries.name: agent-importers
entries.description: `brodification import-agent`: import an OpenClaw (~/.openclaw, or legacy ~/.clawdbot / ~/.moltbot), Claude Code (~/.claude), Codex CLI (~/.codex) or Cursor (~/.cursor) setup into brodification in one command; always previews first and asks before applying. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: instructions, Cursor rules and memories become memory entries, Bash permission rules become command allow/deny lists, MCP servers land in config.yaml, skills are copied, and `--sync` re-imports sources that changed. OpenClaw (core's former `brodification claw migrate`; the plugin keeps that spelling, `brodification claw cleanup` and the openclaw-migration skill): persona, memories, skills, model and messaging settings, MCP servers and agent behaviour. Formerly built into brodification core; `brodification setup` offers to install it when it finds one of these agents, and profiles with a registered sync source are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies, no network calls and no model calls. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: reads those agents' local config trees (never their credential files; secret-looking MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed) and writes only into the active profile (memories/MEMORY.md with a backup, config.yaml, skills/ and import-sync.json). OpenClaw: reads the OpenClaw dir (openclaw.json, its .env, workspace files such as SOUL.md / MEMORY.md / USER.md, skills); API keys and bot tokens come over only with --migrate-secrets (allowlisted names, shown in the preview). It writes into the active profile (config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, memories/, skills/openclaw-imports/, a migration/openclaw/<time>/ report with item backups, and a backups/pre-migration-*.zip restore point), plus a workspace dir only when --workspace-target names one. It runs local pgrep / systemctl / tasklist checks to warn when OpenClaw or a brodification gateway is still running, and `brodification claw cleanup` renames the OpenClaw dir to *.pre-migration after a confirmation.

entries.name: agent-janitor
entries.description: Process hygiene for agent machines — finds the background processes your agent left behind (dev servers, tunnels, watchers, nohup jobs) using evidence signals (ppid=1 reparent, port listener via /proc/net/tcp{,6}, dev-server traits, TTL exceeded) and attributes them to the originating tool call via agent-ledger's ledger when present. Dry-run by default: nothing is killed until you write policy_mode=enforce; system daemons and host/VM management agents are exempt by name, a user-editable whitelist covers your real infrastructure, and each kill re-reads the cmdline first (SIGTERM, 2s, SIGKILL with PID-reuse check). stdlib-only, fails open. Disclosure — inside brodification it only appends terminal commands that look like they start background work (first 300 characters, which can include inline secrets) to plugin-data/agent-janitor/spawns.jsonl, and reads agent-ledger's ledger.db read-only when present. Killing is a separate CLI you run yourself (janitor_cli.py sweep): after you write "enforce" to plugin-data/agent-janitor/policy_mode it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to every process re-parented to PID 1 for over a minute that is not on its built-in exempt list or your whitelist, whoever started it (for example a tmux server or a nohup'd brodification gateway), including other users' processes when run as root. Dry-run first; the dry-run list is the kill list.

entries.name: agent-ledger
entries.description: Write-ahead ledger for agent side effects, with an OWASP Agentic Top 10 posture scorer. Disclosure — records the arguments (up to 4000 chars: terminal commands, file contents, MCP args) and a 300-char result digest of every state-changing tool call in a local plaintext SQLite ledger under BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/agent-ledger/ that is never pruned; injects a warning listing this session's unconfirmed calls into the next turn's context; an optional policy engine (off by default; you add policy.json and set policy_mode) can refuse matching tool calls before they run; the optional posture_daily.py script, run from your own cron, sends a score summary to Telegram with the bot token you give it.

entries.name: agent-log
entries.description: Readable agent.log viewer in the desktop status bar — a live, colour-coded feed of API calls, tools, turns, fallbacks, warnings and errors, with per-call tokens/latency/cache, stats tables, and a single-dot alert for genuine non-self-healing faults. Follows app theme/language.

entries.name: agent-mail-gateway
entries.description: Email for your agents through a self-hosted Agent Mail Gateway: the agent-mail skill teaches reading, searching, replying and forwarding mail, attachments, sending and answering calendar invitations, how to react when the gateway's pre-send review or the operator's policies stop a message, and prompt-injection rules for email content. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only, no code, no mcp.json): you connect the gateway yourself as a remote MCP server in mcp_servers with your own key; the gateway enforces per-mailbox sender/recipient allow lists.

entries.name: agent-station
entries.description: Read-only brodification Desktop page for the focused chat: the main agent and its subagents, background commands and a Replay of file edits. Disclosure — its local dashboard routes serve the file-edit contents (Replay) and background-command output tails of the chat you view to the Desktop page; reads state.db read-only.
entries.title: Agent Station

entries.name: agent_memory_es
entries.description: Self-owned long-term memory backed by the agent-memory-es service (Elasticsearch). Three agent tools — recall, retain, reflect — over episodic/ semantic/procedural tiers with hybrid BM25+kNN recall and server-enforced private/team/common visibility. Requires a running agent-memory-es instance. Disclosure — each user prompt (as a recall query), each user message and brodification memory writes are sent to the agent-memory-es service at AMES_SERVICE_URL (default localhost:8123) with AMES_SERVICE_KEY; the model may store facts in shared team/common visibility tiers.

entries.name: agentchat
entries.description: AgentChat — peer-to-peer messaging for AI agents. Owns its own WebSocket; pokes the agent on inbound; the agent decides whether to reply. Send is a tool call, never automatic. Bundles the etiquette skill.

entries.name: agentplaybooks-memory
entries.description: Private AgentPlaybooks memory for brodification: native recall, explicit memory-write mirroring, archive and history. Disclosure — each turn's query is sent to agentplaybooks.ai for recall; explicit built-in memory writes are mirrored there. HTTPS endpoints only.

entries.name: agentplaybooks-tools
entries.description: Connect AgentPlaybooks skills and hosted MCP/OpenAPI tools to brodification, with guided authentication and API-key setup. Requires Node.js 20+ and @agentplaybooks/cli@0.5.0; the CLI is installed separately. Disclosure — skill-only; the separately installed apb CLI does the work. `apb connect --target=brodification --apply` and `apb sync --target=brodification --apply` edit the selected brodification profile's config.yaml (adding the hosted playbook MCP endpoint and merged MCP definitions, so that playbook's remote tools become available to the agent); local writes require --apply; hosted operations contact agentplaybooks.ai after `apb login`, and `apb push --apply` uploads your project's configuration (secret references, not values).

entries.name: agentwalletapi
entries.description: OpenClawCash managed EVM and Solana wallets for AI agents — thin bridge to the OpenClawCash agent API. Disclosure — payments plugin for the OpenClawCash custodial wallet service (openclawcash.com); the model can create wallets and send EVM/Solana transfers from wallets reachable by OPENCLAWCASH_AGENT_KEY with no brodification confirmation prompt; tool arguments go to openclawcash.com, and wallet_create also sends OPENCLAWCASH_EXPORT_PASSPHRASE to that API.

entries.name: agora
entries.description: Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real brodification profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through brodification' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an `brodification agora` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit `brodification agora setup`. Disclosure — creates a brodification profile per worker by asking core to provision it (`brodification profile create --clone`, which copies config.yaml and .env into the new profile as owner-only files, never symlinks to the real credentials); spawns `brodification -p <profile> chat -Q -q` subprocesses to speak in discussions and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive `--yolo --accept-hooks` ONLY when the project opted in via `agora_start_project(allow_unattended=True)`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task_comments, task_events, task_runs, task_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in `scheduled` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to BRODIFICATION_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into BRODIFICATION_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the brodification dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned brodification subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials.

entries.name: ai-usage-tracker
entries.description: Live subscription-quota windows for every AI provider brodification can route to, as a desktop page plus a status-bar chip, with a per-profile picker — Codex, Claude, Copilot, OpenCode Go/Zen, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax, Nous, OpenRouter, DeepSeek.

entries.name: aichipmunk
entries.description: Pairs this machine's brodification bots with the AI Chipmunk mobile app from inside brodification Desktop — pick a bot, get the reachable host, profile and API key as a scannable code. Registers a `brodification aichipmunk` CLI command, a desktop page and a dashboard API; no tools or hooks. Disclosure — on an explicit confirmed "Switch to Tailscale" it adds a persistent tailscale serve handler putting the API server's own port (plain HTTP inside the tailnet, API_SERVER_KEY auth) onto the tailnet; on a machine with no Tailscale CLI it instead runs brodification config set platforms.api_server.host <tailnet IP> on the owning profile and restarts that gateway; reads API_SERVER_KEY from every profile's .env on this machine on each status poll (masked in lists, the full key only in the pairing link and QR returned to an authenticated dashboard caller, which may be the phone over a published dashboard); shells out to the tailscale and brodification CLIs and probes only this machine's own /health; no third-party network calls.

entries.title: AI Stupid Level
entries.description: AI Stupid Level Smart Router — OpenAI-compatible; routing modes such as auto-tooling send each request to the model currently scoring best on continuously re-run benchmarks, called with your own provider keys. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool definitions, tool results and ASL_ROUTER_KEY to aistupidlevel.info (S.C. Studio Platforms S.R.L.), which forwards each request to the AI provider it routes to using the provider keys you store on your AI Stupid Level account; model usage is billed to your provider accounts, and prompts are logged only if you enable logging for a key.

entries.name: alans-way-computer
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin: Computer Use
entries.description: Computer-use provider for brodification: the stock computer_use tool drives desktop apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the Alan's Way Plugin's workspace setup. Select it with computer_use.backend: alans-way-computer (the Alan's Way Plugin's setup.sh sets this when it installs the provider; in the catalog flow it prints the command). Disclosure — starts the workspace router from the profile's mcp_servers.workspace_browser block (command and args from config.yaml, with a filtered environment plus BRODIFICATION_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_DESKTOP_ACTIONS=1, which lets this private router child serve desktop input) as a long-running node child per session. The filtered environment passes PATH, HOME, locale and OS basics, plus DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS so the router's VM-desktop fallback finds the X display and session bus; no keys or tokens. It talks to the router over stdio (app lists, element trees, screenshots and input actions). The router reaches the user's computer over SSH on the user's tailnet and falls back to the VM's desktop, where it uses xdotool, a screenshot tool and the AT-SPI accessibility bus if they are installed (the provider installs none of them). The provider never takes the focused window on the user's computer, and every input action still goes through brodification's computer_use approval gate (cua:*:background entries in command_allowlist, which the Alan's Way Plugin's --allow-desktop-actions adds, skip the prompt). The provider itself makes no network calls. On brodification 0.21.5, which has no provider API, it installs and does nothing. Since 0.21.0, captures keep element numbers stable across action replies on Mac and Windows, fold in changed controls and report removed numbers; a truncated list never treats unseen controls as removed. Linux keeps the whole-tree generation guard, so capture again before acting by number after a change. Action replies describe nearby changes and can mark the effect confirmed. Default som captures still fetch a screenshot to measure the window, but omit it from the model when named controls cover at least 35%; mode vision explicitly includes it and mode ax requests no screenshot. Replies identify the coordinate space and explain locked screens, missing permissions, unreadable or cut trees, hung apps and uncertain outcomes before a retry. Element trees, generation, screenshots' geometry and host OS are session memory, with no new persistent provider state, tools, hooks, middleware, required environment variables or direct network destinations. Browser commit approvals are separate from this provider's unchanged computer_use approval gate.
known_issues: Needs a brodification build with the pluggable computer-use API (merged to main after 0.21.5). On older brodification the plugin installs and does nothing. Install alans-way first and run its workspace setup, which writes the workspace_browser block this provider reuses.

brodification asks for approval on every computer_use action type until it is granted. For an unattended Telegram bot, grant them once with Always in Telegram, or add cua:<action>:background entries to command_allowlist (see the README). Takes effect after a gateway restart.
Runs only in the plugin host: it cannot load under plugins.isolation: host, because the provider hands brodification a live router session.

Typing without a target field works only on the VM's own desktop, where it types at the focused window (still approval-gated). On the user's computer the app never takes focus, so the agent uses set_value on a field instead.

The VM desktop path needs xdotool, a screenshot tool (scrot, maim or ImageMagick import), the AT-SPI bus and python3-gi on the VM. Without them those calls fail and the agent reports it; setup.sh warns about what is missing.

A default som capture may fetch the window screenshot even when it is omitted from the model after the 35% coverage check. Use mode vision to request it explicitly, or mode ax for an element-only capture. When a screenshot is omitted, coordinate= and element bounds are screen pixels.

Mac and Windows action replies update the held element list without shifting surviving numbers. On Linux, capture again before acting by number after a tree change; cut replies do not prove an unseen control is gone. A timeout or hung app can leave the action's outcome uncertain: capture before retrying.

Between 0a61eb66894a00bf2e8a8091359ffb9bcf196a70 and f8dcdaf5a4d78573229e34b2c4962b43651e9cd7, alans-way-computer changes only its manifest version from 0.21.6 to 0.21.7; provider code and README are unchanged. It is pinned alongside alans-way because it uses the configured workspace router; remote end-to-end compatibility remains unverified.

entries.name: alans-way
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin
entries.description: Idle check-ins from the primary bot of a brodification gateway on a Linux machine or a macOS guest VM: when the bound Telegram chat has been quiet for two hours, during 08:00-22:00 in the user's timezone, the bot checks in once (does one safe step and reports it, suggests one, or asks one question), backing off when unanswered. The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through brodification's approval-gated computer_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one "safe, reversible" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre_llm_call/post_llm_call hooks see every session's turns and store the bound chat's activity timestamps in plugin state; optional cross-bot export adds the separate storage disclosed below. On first load it reads $BRODIFICATION_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and run setup.sh, which does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units brodification-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit brodification-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (administrators_authorized_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the brodification-gateway unit. brodification refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or brodification gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or brodification gateway restart. (5) For the main profile and every profile with its own Telegram bot, writes a managed mcp_servers.workspace_browser block (removing other entries that run this router, with a backup; a re-run keeps the computer address and OS it already holds, and --mac-ssh none removes them), turns off the built-in browser toolset for Telegram and cron (--keep-browser leaves it on), turns computer_use on for Telegram and cron, and sets computer_use.backend to alans-way-computer when it installed or found that provider (under the skill's --skip-plugin flow it only warns and prints the config command). It reads each profile's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN only to derive the numeric bot id. It warns, and changes nothing, when a copy of the workspace-operations skill in a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's. The workspace router reaches the user's computer over SSH on their tailnet; on the user's computer it calls the local API of Alan's Workspace on 127.0.0.1 with that app's bearer token. The skill's moved-VM checklist has the agent read the app's preferences.json on the user's computer over the same SSH path and tell the human where the VNC password lives without pasting it. The Alan's Workspace setup page has the human run the alans-way connect script from its main branch on their own computer, and the agent may install Tailscale with its official install script. The manual --allow-desktop-actions setup flag, which the skill offers but never adds itself, adds cua:*:background entries to command_allowlist. On a brodification without the computer-use provider API, including 0.21.5, it also exposes workspace_computer_action, which drives the user's desktop, Terminal included, with no approval. The repo also holds bootstrap-orgo.sh and migrate.sh, which the plugin, setup.sh and the skills never run: a user runs them by hand to provision a fresh supervisord Linux computer (it fetches the brodification and Tailscale installers over HTTPS, pipes setup.sh from this repo's main branch into bash unless --repo-ref is given, installs openssh-server if absent, writes supervisord programs, and POSTs the Tailscale login URL with a shared secret to a --callback URL when one is given) or to copy ~/.brodification, including .env, auth.json and state.db, to another host over SSH (it also looks up each profile's bot username at api.telegram.org with that profile's bot token). Since 0.21.0, every enabled profile also gets a default-on Telegram texting voice: an additional pre_llm_call hook reads that profile's voice mode and adds a tone note to Telegram turns, and transform_llm_output can remove a known leading assistant opener from the final Telegram reply. Messages containing backticks, quotes, indentation or silence markers are left unchanged by that polish. /tone texting|default|status and brodification tone store the mode under voice in brodification plugin state; setup.sh --tone applies it to each configured profile. It layers over the user's persona without writing SOUL.md or agent.system_prompt. Check-ins now name one concrete open thread. /proactivity now requests one immediately from the bound chat even when paused or outside active hours, without changing the settings or unanswered-check-in count. Morning briefs are off by default: /proactivity brief on (or the operator CLI) enables one daily internal user-role prompt near active_start, with 0-20 minutes of jitter, at most two hours late and skipped after recent user activity. It asks the model to consult calendar and email read-only if those tools exist. The existing proactivity tool may disable the brief but cannot enable it; settings.morning_brief and last_brief_date are stored in the existing idle plugin state. The workspace router adds a commit object to the existing browser open/action tools for purchases, bookings, sends, posts, submissions, deletions and account changes. It checks control names, selectors, refs, action-looking URLs, batches, scripts, keys and dialogs against page state; missing page knowledge needs a snapshot or explicit commit. Shared commit-name patterns allow benign Buy it again, Book a demo and Subscribe & Save labels without excusing other commit-bearing words. It asks through MCP elicitation (60-second default wait, configurable with BRODIFICATION_ROUTER_APPROVAL_MS), refuses unavailable, declined, timed-out or stale approvals, drops agent-supplied approval receipts and adds a single-use receipt bound to the approved tab and epoch. An approved commit is never replayed after a lost connection or host change. It appends commit decisions to commit-decisions.jsonl beside the mac-watch state file, creating the log with mode 0600: timestamp, bot id, page origin, decision and any supplied kind, summary, amount, currency and counterparty, or the detected target. Page/control/challenge and pending-approval state is held in memory. The same two skills now prefer brodification web_search/web_extract for plain lookups and the user's computer for interactive search, hand CAPTCHAs to the human, poll at most every 30 seconds for up to 30 minutes, and switch sources after two challenges in ten minutes. The router stops remembering challenge pages for failover and reports changed tab ids in result metadata. The operations skill covers the app's automatic takeover after its grace period; CAPTCHA and recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still keep the bot out. It also asks the agent to save durable facts and preferences to memory, never live tab state. The setup skill pins the companion app source to a82f5010248455600acfe275010e3e725355a2a8 and adds a long-chat reference: report effective compression and summary routing read-only, then only with explicit consent for each profile enable compression.proactive_prune_tokens at 48000, with 8000-character eligibility and 4096-token minimum reclaim, using the profile-scoped config CLI and keeping custom values, micro_compact and summary routing. This writes the approved profile's config.yaml and records prior values outside the repo for undo; setup.sh does not run it. A weekly time-saved report is a user-created brodification cron recipe, not an installed job. setup.sh --verify now checks the running service manager, display, SSH ProxyCommand and managed browser's loopback /json/version endpoint, and reports noVNC reachability from its actual bind address. Manual supervisord restart guidance drains with USR1 first. The repo also adds scripts/voice_eval.py, user-run only: it sends fixed fictional scenarios and replies to Anthropic models through the SDK or claude -p for scoring and optionally writes a JSON result; the plugin, setup and skills never run it. Since 0.21.5, the plugin registers two more bundled skills, web-errands and integrations, with no new tools, hooks, commands or required environment variables. web-errands is guidance for shopping, booking, applications, filings, cancellations and claims in the workspace browser: every purchase, booking, send, submission and deletion still goes through the commit approval gate described above, CAPTCHA, sign-in and card-entry walls go back to the human, and card numbers are never stored. It has the agent record each application's company, role, date and posting URL in brodification memory. For a price, restock or status watch the user asks for, it has the agent create a brodification cron job with brodification's cronjob_manage tool (or ask the operator), polling no more often than every 10 minutes and stopping after three consecutive failures; cron runs cannot answer approvals, so a watch that reaches its target stages the result for the user. The integrations skill has the agent check that an account is connected, with a small read, before promising a task that needs it, and reuses brodification's Google Workspace, Himalaya, Home Assistant, Honcho and X routes first. The Google route uses brodification's own setup, whose fixed scope list includes write access; the skill says so and stops if the user declines. Only after the user agrees in chat does it guide an install: a brodification catalog plugin (Home Assistant or Honcho), a separately reviewed Himalaya v1.2.0 binary, rclone v1.75.2 (the release zip from downloads.rclone.org, checked against that release's SHA256SUMS before extraction) or Taskwarrior 3.5.0 (a source build of upstream commit 3419d5ba1e6a780fbbb0a8d68d8fd31e675c1bf8 cloned from GitHub, after checking the CMake and Rust versions and asking before changing any toolchain), the last two into versioned directories under ~/.local/share/alans-tools/. Secrets are entered by the human in a private terminal outside the agent session, never in Telegram; where a recipe needs a secret in the agent's terminal (a mail credential, RCLONE_CONFIG_PASS), it explains the grant and adds only that variable to the profile's terminal.env_passthrough. The recipes keep rclone.conf (mode 0600) and Taskwarrior's taskrc and data under the profile's BRODIFICATION_HOME/integrations. Scheduled reads are read-only cron jobs with a profile-local failure-count file, and pausing goes through the owner conversation or an explicitly authorized brodification cron pause. API writes (send, post, delete, share) need fresh explicit approval in the live conversation, and a declined, timed-out or unavailable browser commit is never completed through another tool. Mastodon is not bundled: its recipe is human-run documentation in this repo (docs/integrations/mastodon.md) that the plugin and skills never run. None of this runs at plugin load or from setup.sh. Telegram replies, check-ins and briefs share one status-first style: concrete status, evidence or caveat, plain limits, and no tool names, file paths, scripts or job and session IDs in user-facing text unless asked. Prices, availability and policies must come from a page read this turn or be labeled unconfirmed. Multi-step browser work runs in short chunks of about two actions with at most one plain progress update per chunk, a new mid-task message is acknowledged and folded in, and brodification's clarify buttons may be used for decisions the user owns, never for approvals; a whole checkout batch still sits under one commit. For a message of 200 characters or fewer that is wholly a recap request, greeting, thanks or acknowledgment, the voice hook appends a three-sentence limit; the check reads only the current message, with no model call, history or network. The check-in menu now ends with asking about a decision the user owns. The operations skill adds tab hygiene: the agent closes finished tabs it owns with the existing close tool, never another bot's or the user's and never one with a pending handback or recording hold. The router adds requestingBotId to tab-list replies and forwards a reply over 4 MiB unchanged, without that decoration, writing a content-free line to stderr. The skill also tells the agent to report installed versions by running brodification --version, reading the plugin's install metadata, running local git describe and rev-parse on the Alan's Tools checkout, and calling the app's existing status tool. setup.sh --bind now also makes the bound DM brodification's Telegram home by running brodification -p PROFILE config set for TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID (30-second limit each; on failure it warns to send /sethome); it loads on gateway restart. setup.sh --verify exits 0 for a complete local audit, 1 for failed required checks and 2 for a partial install (warnings, or skipped browser or services). The setup skill's checkout step now initializes ~/alans-way-agents if absent and fetches the pin (depth 1) from the repo's GitHub origin, or reuses a clean clone there after two read-only local git helpers (5-second limit) confirm one recorded and effective origin URL naming this repo; for file and direct Git installs it uses the installer-recorded revision, and it never falls back to a tag when that record is invalid. Its computer-use API probe separates an absent API from a failed or timed-out probe and ends the probe's process group or tree on timeout. The setup skill also offers, each only after an explicit answer, with readback and a remembered-choice marker in the profile's config: display.busy_input_mode (steer or interrupt, for every platform in that profile; asked once, only when the effective mode is interrupt and no choice is recorded) and one grouped Telegram question covering platforms.telegram.typing_indicator, display.platforms.telegram.interim_assistant_messages, tool_progress, notifications, long_running_notifications and busy_steer_ack_enabled, platforms.telegram.reactions, display.memory_notifications (hides the Memory updated and Self-improvement review notices on every platform in that profile), cron.wrap_response (profile-wide: removes scheduled-message headers, job IDs and footers for all delivery targets) and, as a separate city-confirmed question, timezone. Markers written through the same CLI are skills.config.workspace-setup.busy_input_choice and telegram_feel_choice; a legacy busy_steer_ack_choice marker is only read, never written. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing, and neither setup script writes any of these keys. When the VNC viewer binds loopback only, the skill can, with explicit consent, have the human run a temporary SSH forward to the computer's loopback (local port 16080, ends after 30 minutes) and verify it with curl from that computer. For a manual or file install, SAFE requires no scanner confirmation; setup and dependency consent remain separate. A later CAUTION revision needs review and explicit consent to the exact tree before retrying brodification plugins install with --ref SHA --enable --force; --enable alone does not confirm a warning, and --force confirms CAUTION and can replace an install but cannot override DANGEROUS. brodification's unmodified scanner reports SAFE for this plugin: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the two git helpers in skills/workspace-setup/SKILL.md) and 3 LOW (hardcoded_ip_port: the loopback forward examples in the same file). This pin also extends the existing texting-note and minimal final-opener polish to public session source tags desktop, tui and bot_room, alongside Telegram; CLI, cron, webhook and API-server sources keep their default voice. Routine work is instructed to stay quiet while preserving essential questions, approvals, failures and honest completion. Fixed brodification progress/error/approval messages are unchanged. Scripted tool conversations prove hook delivery; consistent real-model quiet behavior is unverified. Router changes bind approvals to exact observed page targets, reject missing/malformed action success receipts, bound recovery and owned-child shutdown, and project agent-facing replies without exposing internal approval proof. Cross-bot proactivity adds the cross_bot_ask tool and pre_tool_call/on_session_end hooks; no middleware, required secrets or direct network destinations are added. Optional cross-bot proactivity is off by default, configured with the same explicit absolute shared root and designated primary in each participating profile, then enrolled per bot through /proactivity cross on (activation in a running gateway needs a restart). Only completed user/final-assistant exchanges from each enrolled bot's bound owner Telegram DM are exported: at most four recent exchanges and 2 KiB per digest, expiring after 24 hours per exchange. There is no historical backfill or export of groups, other chats, attachments, reasoning, tool history, cron, check-ins, briefs, child or imported turns. Exchanges that appear to contain credentials or payment details, or match operator redact terms, are skipped entirely before truncation; sanitization cannot detect every secret. Only the designated primary receives other enabled profiles' fresh digests during permitted check-ins, including user-requested /proactivity now; its own digest is excluded and exports are JSON-escaped as untrusted observations, bounded to 32 KiB across 16 profiles. Ordinary turns, briefs and cron receive no cross-bot context or dispatch permit. The primary may automatically schedule one read_only or draft_only cross_bot_ask with fresh target evidence per check-in into another enrolled bot's existing bound DM; results stay there with primary attribution. The receiver needs its own gateway-injection permission and verified routing, observes pause/hours/busy settings, and starts no spontaneous secondary check-ins. Queued asks are at most 800 characters, expire after two hours and are deleted before injection; sent means scheduled, not delivered or completed, with no replay, receipt store or result polling. Attempts are limited to four per rolling day gateway-wide, two per target and 60-minute target spacing. The plugin-owned POSIX shared directory uses mode 0700 and files 0600: digests and queued bodies, persistent enrollment/generation and eligibility/heartbeat records, body-free turn/attempt hashes retained for 48 hours, one-use check-in permits and imported-session locks expiring within 30 minutes. Session locks contain the exact session key and ask ID and survive restart until session end, expiry or opt-out. Pruning runs on activated startup, before store access and every 60 seconds while connected; offline expired files can remain until an activated profile prunes them. Dormant profiles do no cross-bot store access. /proactivity cross off immediately stops sharing, receiving and dispatch and purges that profile's digest, permits, locks and pending asks; body-free records remain until expiry and scheduler roles revert on restart. Only the operator can enable or expand sharing; the model may disable it. Launch-gateway profile routing policy is read through public configuration/home-scope APIs; no brodification session DB or credential store is read for export. Imported sessions block terminal/code, desktop actions, delegation, messaging, scheduling, further cross-bot asks and unknown connectors; reviewed reads/drafting and existing gated browser actions remain allowed. Browser approval, CAPTCHA and ownership gates still apply; this is not universal read-only enforcement. Copied context goes through the configured model provider and target Telegram delivery and may remain in brodification history, API-content sidecars, compaction and memory-provider records, including Honcho when configured, and model-provider retention after expiry or opt-out. The instruction not to save other bots' excerpts is model policy, not enforced deletion; the plugin performs no memory-provider writes. No new direct network endpoint or telemetry is introduced. Optional integrations use the user's selected Google Workspace API, IMAP/SMTP mail service, Home Assistant instance, Honcho API, X API or rclone cloud/WebDAV/S3 endpoint; browser errands contact user-selected sites. Honcho can receive conversation turns, derived conclusions, peer/session IDs and version/OS/plugin headers. Native tools retain their own profile-scoped credentials, including Google client/token/pending OAuth files and encrypted rclone provider tokens; the plugin does not create a separate credential store. Setup downloads also reach GitHub/raw.githubusercontent.com, the official Tailscale installer, configured distro package repositories and the npm/Playwright distribution, in addition to Google and rclone downloads already disclosed.
known_issues: Install this on the machine that runs brodification (a Linux host or a macOS guest VM), not on the user's primary computer. Windows guests are new and untested on real hardware. If the plugin is already installed from the catalog, setup leaves it as it is, so this pin stays.

Setup turns off brodification's stock browser toolset for Telegram and cron so the agent uses the workspace browser (pass --keep-browser to leave it on). It never turns off computer_use: on brodification with the computer-use provider API, desktop input goes through the gated computer_use tool and its alans-way-computer provider.
Check-ins need plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection: true and a bound Telegram DM (setup does both). A background thread checks every 60 seconds once the gateway connects Telegram.

Setup may install Chrome, Chromium, Playwright's Chromium or Xvfb with root or passwordless sudo, and may drain-stop and start the profile's gateway to apply a plugin change brodification refuses while it runs. Pass --skip-services to skip the services and their packages.
The computer's SSH key is only accepted from the tailnet (from= restriction). An existing unrestricted line for the same key is rewritten with it.
A copy of the workspace-operations skill under a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's and never gets its updates. Setup only warns; move anything worth keeping out of it, then delete it.

The texting voice is default-on for Telegram, desktop, TUI and bot_room source tags. /tone default disables its note and final-opener polish per profile. CLI, cron, webhook and API-server sources retain the default voice. Check-ins and morning briefs keep their own short style. Fixed brodification progress/error/approval messages, direct sends and cron reports are outside these hooks; interim messages get the tone note but no polish, and streaming can show raw chunks before a final edit. Consistent real-model quiet behavior remains unverified.

Morning briefs are opt-in (/proactivity brief on), use the existing bound DM and gateway-injection permission, and may read calendar/email through tools already available to the model. /proactivity now is user-only from that chat and bypasses pause/hours for one requested check-in.

Telegram browser Approve buttons need brodification v0.21.6 or newer including commit 239740a19e (first in date tag v2026.6.19), despite the generic >=0.21.5 install floor. Without MCP form elicitation support commits fail with approval_unavailable; unattended cron declines them. The gate protects against agent mistakes and malicious pages, not a deliberately hostile bot with same-user terminal/file access.

The router appends approval details and detected targets to commit-decisions.jsonl beside mac-watch state, shared by routers using that path; no retention or rotation is implemented. Keep this local log private. CAPTCHA handback, recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still block takeover. If the router reports human_has_control before a commit approval, wait or claim the tab through the normal app control flow first.

Long-chat pruning is an agent-guided, separately consented config option per profile, not a setup.sh default. It preserves customized values and summary routing, rewrites sent history and can break the prompt-cache prefix; undo affects future pruning and cannot restore tool bodies already pruned from active context.

web-errands and integrations are agent guidance, not setup steps. Any Himalaya, rclone, Taskwarrior, Home Assistant or Honcho install happens only after the user agrees in chat, never from setup.sh or plugin load. Taskwarrior is built from source (CMake >=3.24, Rust >=1.91.1 and several GiB of temporary space). The Google Workspace route requests brodification's fixed scope list, which includes write access.

Guided setup can change a profile's busy-input, Telegram display, notification, reaction, memory-notice, cron-wrapping and timezone settings, but only after explicit answers. Busy mode, memory-notice hiding, cron.wrap_response and timezone reach beyond Telegram within that profile. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing; neither setup script writes these keys.

setup.sh --bind also sets TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL for the bound profile through brodification config set and clears TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID; it loads on gateway restart. If that fails, send /sethome in the primary DM.

Desktop control needs a brodification with tools.computer_use.backend.ComputerUseProvider (commit 63f5e0ea45726c5d8d7d207d140613997730aab3 or newer); a version string alone does not prove it. setup.sh --verify exits 2, not 0, for a partial install.

This pin needs the paired workspace/remote browser host with approval-binding-v1 support for approved browser actions. Older hosts fail closed when that proof is unavailable; update and verify the paired workspace before rollout.

Cross-bot proactivity is off by default and requires operator configuration and per-bot /proactivity cross on; activation needs a gateway restart. It exports bounded completed owner-DM excerpts across enabled profiles on one gateway. /proactivity cross off stops sharing/receiving/dispatch immediately and purges local shared text and permits; body-free hashes remain for 48 hours. Sanitization skips credential/payment-looking exchanges but cannot guarantee secrecy. Digest TTL is 24 hours, queued asks two hours; offline expired files remain until an activated profile prunes them. Copied context in brodification history, sidecars, compaction, memory-provider records and model-provider retention is not erased by expiry or opt-out. The no-memory instruction is model policy. Shared storage requires POSIX owner-only directories/files. Dormant profiles do no store access.

During a permitted primary check-in the model may automatically schedule one read-only/draft-only ask into an enrolled target bot's existing owner DM, with primary attribution. sent means scheduled, not delivered or completed; there is no receipt/result store or replay. Imported-session restrictions last at most 30 minutes and survive restart; terminal/code, desktop input, delegation, messaging, scheduling and unknown connectors are blocked, while existing gated browser calls remain possible. Existing approval/CAPTCHA/ownership gates apply; this is not universal read-only enforcement. Targets require gateway-injection permission and verified same-bot routes; missing permission, routing, busy/pause/hours or expiry can prevent delivery.

entries.name: alice-voice
entries.description: Private Yandex Alice voice input for brodification, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL.
entries.title: Alice Voice Input
known_issues: Default profile and one existing authorized Telegram DM session only; a private Alice skill and operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy are required.
Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram connect factory receives the native Application and is not supported by plugins.isolation: host.
The webhook URL contains a bearer secret. Yandex request signatures are not verified; body skill/account IDs are not cryptographic authentication.
Alice acknowledges asynchronous scheduling, not completion or delivery. Replies are sent to Telegram, not spoken by Alice.
Deduplication is bounded and memory-only; no durable queue, exactly-once guarantee, or built-in global rate limiter.

entries.name: ample
entries.title: Ample
entries.description: Ample (ample.computer) as native tools: deploy the websites and web apps brodification builds to public HTTPS URLs, release changes to the same URLs, read build and runtime logs, list and delete apps; bundled skill ample:web-apps. Disclosure — maintained by Ample, the hosting service it deploys to; talks to Ample's API (https://api.ample.computer); on first use downloads the pinned Ample CLI 0.1.36 from Ample's release server (https://get.ample.computer/releases/0.1.36/, SHA-256 checked, never self-updated; cli_path uses your own binary instead) and runs it as a subprocess with an allowlisted environment and its crash reports off; ample_deploy uploads the folder it is given (home, brodification home and credential directories refused) and writes ample.toml and .ample/ into it; with no AMPLE_CLIENT_ID/AMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET or AMPLE_TOKEN set, the first deploy signs up for a free Ample account (deleted after two days unless claimed) and saves its credential in brodification's .env. A pre_tool_call hook sends every delete (scoped to that app) and the first publish of each folder to brodification's approval gate; only folders the user has published, recorded in plugin state, skip it. No telemetry, no background processes.

entries.name: anatomy-museum
entries.title: Anatomy Museum
entries.description: Native Anatomy community gallery with search, local favorites and explicit sandboxed standalone playback. Disclosure — when opened it fetches gallery metadata and thumbnails from a third-party GitHub repository (wheresryan22/anatomy-community, resolved at runtime from its mutable previews branch via api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com). "Open figure in brodification" downloads that community figure's HTML and runs its JavaScript inside the Desktop SDK sandbox (opaque origin, scripts only), and "Browse Ryan's website" embeds skills.wheresryan.sh the same way. Favorites and filters stay in Desktop-local plugin storage; no credentials or brodification data are sent.
known_issues: Requires the matching native Desktop SDK; tested source-built Desktop reports 0.0.0, not a certified prebuilt release number.
Full embedded website navigation and website-wrapper Play-with-it are unsupported; repository standalone playback and external recovery are separate.
Wankel, Zipper and WebGL Ripple tank were interaction-tested; the other catalog figures were not individually certified.

entries.name: ando-platform
entries.description: Connect a brodification agent through an existing Ando invitation and receive authorized messages. Disclosure — connects outbound to Ando (mcp.ando.so, api.ando.so, realtime.ando.so) with an agent API key stored at $BRODIFICATION_HOME/ando/connection.json (mode 600); Ando messages from the connecting member (or members the operator explicitly allowlists) start brodification turns and the final reply, with any files it attaches, is posted back to Ando; message attachments are uploaded and downloaded through short-lived single-use links Ando issues (up to 20 MB each; received files are cached in the profile's brodification cache); brodification ando connect edits gateway.platforms.ando in config.yaml.

entries.name: android-emulator
entries.description: Control a headless Android emulator from brodification — live sidebar, app management, GPS/battery/network simulation, and ADB tools. Emulator host is Linux. Disclosure — requires a pre-installed Android SDK under ~/Android/Sdk; runs adb, emulator, avdmanager and sdkmanager on the host, and the dashboard's Create AVD action downloads Android system images from Google via sdkmanager. emu_shell runs arbitrary commands inside the emulator; emu_install/emu_push copy host files into it.

entries.name: antenna
entries.description: Signed messaging with paired brodification and OpenClaw agents, with receiver-controlled live and opt-in non-YOLO headless delivery. Disclosure — runs a loopback-only Node receiver when listen_port is set (you expose only its HTTPS receive route); messages from paired peers become agent turns in the sessions you approve and may cause tool use, and opt-in background delivery runs them in non-YOLO sessions only; smart scanning sends message text through your configured provider; ClawReef Public Groups use a plaintext relay that ClawReef can read; identity keys, peer credentials, holds and receipts live in the profile's plugin-data/antenna (0700/0600) and backups contain credentials; policy and storage commands rewrite config.yaml (comments and formatting are lost).
entries.title: Antenna for brodification

entries.name: antigravity-agy
entries.description: Run brodification on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, brodification tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to brodification. Fails closed on any non-brodification tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).

entries.name: antigravity-oauth
entries.description: Sign in to Google Antigravity with `brodification auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx brodification-antigravity-oauth`) and run brodification on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your brodification SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching brodification tool, which then runs under brodification approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full brodification system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).

entries.name: antigravity-subscription-directsdk
entries.description: Run brodification on an Antigravity subscription via the official agy CLI (DirectSDK path). Streams tokens progressively, persists multi-turn trajectories via agy --conversation (up to 239k tokens), discovers models dynamically per account, maps thinking effort, reports quota in /usage, and aborts reported native tools. Disclosure — routes inference and /usage quota reads through Google's official agy CLI under your subscription (usage counts against it); links (symlink, else hardlink/copy) the antigravity-oauth-token into a per-session private temp HOME deleted on close; probes OS keyring presence (Linux Secret Service, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) without reading secrets; on macOS symlinks ~/Library/Keychains for CLI session reuse; never writes to vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking environment variables before spawning agy (name heuristic; ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT for an allow-list). Disclosure — the opt-in ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR env var writes every outgoing prompt (full conversation text) to that directory.

entries.name: anyapi
entries.title: AnyAPI.ai
entries.description: AnyAPI.ai — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool results and ANYAPI_API_KEY to api.anyapi.ai, a third-party relay (AnyAPI Inc.) that forwards them to the upstream vendor serving the chosen model; billed to your AnyAPI account.

entries.name: anyrouter
entries.description: AnyRouter — unified model gateway (OpenAI-compatible); /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes, first-party meta-models like anyrouter/brodification. Disclosure — sends your prompts and ANYROUTER_API_KEY to anyrouter.dev, a third-party relay that forwards to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, …), on some plans through a shared pool of other members' donated free-tier vendor keys; billed in prepaid AnyRouter credits. anyrouter/brodification is AnyRouter's own routing meta-model, not a Nous Research model. Opt-in ANYROUTER_APP_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds brodification attribution headers.

entries.name: anysearch
entries.description: AnySearch web search and extraction plus two real-time fallback chains: when a primary backend fails (Exa quota, Firecrawl timeout), the same call is served by AnySearch (1,000 free requests/day).

entries.name: aphrodite
entries.description: CCR compression plugin - 28-type classifier, 13 tools, opt-in context engine, TOML-driven templates. Disclosure - pre_tool_call auto-backgrounds long terminal/process commands (modify: background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and rewrites chained terminal commands when enabled.
