Disclosure — hook and tool logic runs in prebuilt native binaries (libaphrodite_brodification + aphrodite proxy, v1.6.6) built from the public PlayForm/Aphrodite source and fetched by an explicit download.sh step checked against in-tree SHA-256 sums; register() starts a background proxy on 127.0.0.1:9797/9798 whose management routes are open to local processes unless APHRODITE_MGMT_TOKEN is set; pre_tool_call by default rewrites slow terminal commands (cargo/npm/pip/docker/curl…) to run in the background (background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and splits chained commands when enabled; aphrodite_prefetch reads files the model names into its store (refuses .env, auth.json, ~/.ssh and the brodification home); requires its own APHRODITE_API_KEY for an upstream LLM endpoint (default api.openai.com).

entries.name: apify
entries.description: Apify, the largest marketplace of tools for AI: discover, run, and collect results from thousands of ready-to-run Actors, from the comfort of your agent, plus an Apify backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract tools.
entries.title: Apify

entries.name: approval-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of brodification's approval prompts (dangerous commands, protected writes, MCP consent, smart-mode verdicts): /approval-log shows how often each rule asked, how many prompts were approved, denied or left unanswered, and how long a person took to answer, per rule, per surface or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /approval-log recent lists the newest decisions (ten, or up to 100 with /approval-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes decision metadata (session id, surface, rule label, answer, timings; no command, description or session key) to plugin-data/approval-ledger/approvals.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer or change an approval; no network

entries.name: ard-kit
entries.description: Agentic Resource Discovery — search a local tool catalog by intent and inspect an entry to get its invoke command. Ships the ard-registry skill plus an stdio MCP server (ard_search / ard_inspect / ard_verify); stdlib only, the run stays local. Disclosure — no network egress, no API keys and no environment variables read by the MCP front, which ranks a catalog JSON on disk; no catalog ships in the repo, so the first call returns an explicit error naming the `python -m ard_kit.catalogize` command that builds one.

entries.name: artifact-relay
entries.description: Publish and read private Markdown or HTML reports through your Artifact Relay server.

entries.name: artifacts
entries.title: brodification Artifacts
entries.description: Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to BRODIFICATION_ARTIFACTS_URL with the machine credential BRODIFICATION_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, resolved through brodification secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact_publish reads a resolved local path only after brodification read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact_download checks raw and resolved destinations against brodification write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry.
known_issues: Conflicts with artifact-relay because both register artifact_publish. Enable only one of these plugins.
Needs the brodification Artifacts service running separately (run from source; no package or image yet). Tested with brodification 0.21.x and in Chromium only.

entries.name: aside-browser
entries.description: Use the signed-in Aside browser as brodification's browser when the Aside CLI is installed. Disclosure — runs the local aside CLI to drive your signed-in Aside browser (page text, screenshots, Aside memory, model-written JavaScript via aside_repl) without a brodification approval prompt; Aside's permission level is a user-only setting (default ask) that covers aside_exec only. Optional pre_tool_call hook blocks brodification' built-in browser tools while Aside is ready when browser_policy is always. Reads Aside's settings.json for the model list; no telemetry.
known_issues: Drives the signed-in Aside browser on this machine. Does not install Aside.

entries.name: author-feed
entries.description: Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile_get, author_feed and author_watch. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key, and no program on your machine. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with brodification tools. brodification author-feed schedule creates one cron job, a model turn every hour by default (two or more model requests, no daily cap). Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run brodification author-feed unschedule before removal. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with brodification cron remove <id>. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private brodification parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall.

entries.name: auto-pin
entries.description: Automatically pin every new interactive session (desktop, CLI, TUI) and the branches you fork from them. Cron, one-shot, subagent and messaging sessions are left alone, and unpinning a session sticks. Disclosure — on each new desktop/CLI/TUI session it sets the session's pinned flag in brodification's session database (state.db) through the shared SessionDB handle, and records each automatic pin in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/auto-pin/ledger.txt; no network, no tools.

entries.name: aux-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of brodification's auxiliary LLM calls (titling, compression, vision, approval): /aux shows tokens, time and failures per task, model, provider or day, or lists the newest calls (ten, or up to 100 with /aux recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded. Disclosure — writes auxiliary-call metadata (ids, models, timings, token counts, no prompt or response text) to plugin-data/aux-ledger/calls.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

entries.name: background-review-watch
entries.description: Status-bar chips for the background self-improvement review and batch context compaction: review running/done/stale with live elapsed time, a turn-countdown fill bar to the next nudge, an always-visible compaction chip (compacting/done/failed/stale with committed reduction or failure class), reply-guard recovery and review-overlap diagnostics, and a Settings page that tunes both orphan ceilings. Disclosure — renderer-only; polls filtered read-only tails of agent.log via host.logs to parse lifecycle markers; listens for review.summary/message.start/message.complete events; stores three small plugin-storage records (settings + last compaction + last review); no network calls beyond the local gateway, no credential access, no self-update.

entries.name: beam
entries.title: Beam
entries.description: Move data across cloud storage and exchange end-to-end encrypted messages, files and media between agents with Beam Network (Bittensor SN105).

entries.name: bento
entries.description: Bento (bentonow.com) email marketing: subscribers, tags, fields, events incl. $purchase, stats, draft/scheduled broadcasts and transactional email, with dry-run + human-approval gates on every send. Native Python plugin, no dependencies. Disclosure — sends real email (bento_email_send, bento_broadcast_schedule), and events, purchases and consent changes can trigger Bento Flows that email people; calls only app.bentonow.com (an operator base_url override is limited to https *.bentonow.com or loopback) with the BENTO_* keys from the profile .env; no telemetry, no self-update; T2/T3 calls go to the brodification approval prompt, which asks no human under YOLO, approvals.mode off, or cron/single-query/unattended mode set to approve. T3 sends then still need a dry-run confirm token and hard guards, but T2 writes (events, purchases, consent, bulk upserts) need no token unless safety.tier2 is token_only; T1 writes (tags, tag/field definitions, drafts, upserts up to bulk_threshold) are never gated and still run under environment=disabled; environment=staging does not block sends, only environment=disabled blocks T2/T3.

entries.name: better-session-appearance
entries.description: Set a color for each session and show an idle glyph to make rows easier to scan.

entries.name: betterdb
entries.description: BetterDB long-term memory provider — semantic recall on Valkey / valkey-search via the betterdb-agent-memory SDK. Completed turns are embedded and stored in a vector index; the next turn recalls the most relevant memories with a composite similarity/recency/importance score. Explicit betterdb_remember / betterdb_recall / betterdb_forget tools. Disclosure — turn text and tool-stored facts are embedded through an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint you configure (embeddings_base_url, default api.openai.com) and written to the Valkey instance you point it at; plaintext http:// to a remote host is refused. Opt-in, off by default: a discovery marker (set discovery=true to let BetterDB Monitor enumerate the tier) and SDK usage analytics (set telemetry=true).

entries.name: bharatcode-provider
entries.description: BharatCode (bharatcode.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider — free student tier, native /model integration. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and BHARATCODE_API_KEY go to bharatcode.ai (BharatCode, India), which processes prompts through third-party inference partners, some outside India; outside paid Pro (complimentary or referral Pro included) BharatCode may retain private prompt/response logs for debugging, abuse review and product quality, and even on paid Pro a flagged account can have a time-limited sample of up to 100 prompts and responses captured for security review.

entries.name: bilinc
entries.description: Hosted memory for brodification with a full history: see what your agent remembered, when it changed and why. Recalls relevant memories before each turn, adds bilinc_recall, bilinc_remember, bilinc_revise and bilinc_forget tools, and mirrors brodification built-in memory writes. Maintained by ReARC Labs; free plan available. Disclosure — recall queries (the text of each message, when auto_recall is on), tool arguments, mirrored built-in memory writes, the brodification session id and, only if memory.bilinc.capture_turns is turned on, each turn's user and assistant text are sent over HTTPS to bilinc.space under your BILINC_API_KEY; requests carry User-Agent bilinc-brodification/<version> and X-Bilinc-Client: brodification-plugin headers. Secret-looking strings are redacted before sending. Recall and writes run on background threads inside brodification; no separate process, local database or telemetry.
entries.title: Bilinc

entries.name: billing
entries.description: Nous Portal usage widget for the brodification desktop statusbar — remaining credits plus plan-usage percentage, with portal detail on hover.

entries.name: biomimetic-brain
entries.description: Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read BRODIFICATION_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.

entries.name: birkin-mnemosyne
entries.description: Local Markdown memory provider with multilingual lexical recall and profile-local durable notes. Create-only writes are limited to primary agent contexts. Uses published birkin-mnemosyne 0.7.2 with compatible updates below 1.0; no API key, network service or telemetry. Session handoff capture is opt-in. Native brodification memory files remain separate.

entries.name: blackbox
entries.title: Agent Blackbox
entries.description: Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; `brodification blackbox setup` installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), and joins the DKG peer-to-peer network; package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; `blackbox attach` copies the plugin into the brodification homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set `auto_attach: true`); `brodification blackbox chat` creates an `agent-blackbox` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700.
known_issues: After installing, run `brodification blackbox setup` once: it installs Blackbox's local DKG node (a pinned, checksum-verified OriginTrail release from npm) and its graph store (Blazegraph in Docker, or Oxigraph when Docker is not available), then syncs the verified threat graph. Until setup has run, the built-in rules protect and `brodification blackbox status` says setup is needed.

entries.name: blender
entries.description: Official Blender Lab MCP server over stdio, pinned to upstream v1.0.3, with a Blender workflow skill. Requires Blender 5.1+, its separately installed MCP add-on, Git and uv. First startup downloads Python dependencies; prepare the uv environment before connecting. Disclosure — tools execute arbitrary Python in Blender with your privileges; first start downloads the pinned Blender Lab MCP server and its Python dependencies with uv; at install brodification looks for Blender in the standard install locations (Windows uninstall registry and Program Files, /Applications and the Steam library on macOS, PATH, flatpak, snap and Steam on Linux) and refuses the install when it is missing. Server discovery does not prove scene readiness.
entries.title: Blender

entries.name: blinkenbar
entries.description: Dense, animated supercomputer light banks driven by system telemetry and live agent activity in brodification Desktop.

entries.name: boardstate
entries.title: Boardstate
entries.description: A live board your agent builds for you: tabs of notes, tables, charts, KPI cards and live brodification data, in the dashboard and brodification Desktop. It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Desktop, and the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate_* tools, approval widgets included. Runs a local Node >= 20 sidecar on loopback with a per-spawn nonce; no network access unless you opt in to operator-gated connectors. Disclosure — spawns a local Node.js ≥20 sidecar (from PATH/BRODIFICATION_NODE_BIN, nothing downloaded) on 127.0.0.1 on first use; state under BRODIFICATION_HOME/boardstate-state/. Reads the dashboard's loopback session token from brodification internals (web_server._SESSION_TOKEN) and passes it to the sidecar for live usage/sessions/cron widgets; mounts one token-gated static route for approved widget assets. No outbound network unless you author boardstate.connectors.json (stdio/HTTP MCP connectors); connector actions need operator approval. Ships one plugin skill, boardstate:boardstate-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text.

entries.name: bot-cabinet-v2
entries.title: Cabinet
entries.description: Tell Cabinet the job you need done and it answers with the smallest setup that does it (one chat, a skill, a routine, a Bot or a crew), shows which answers led there, then helps you act: add one of botcabinet.com's 20 Bots (each with its test record shown) as a brodification profile, plan a new Bot line by line, or set up a crew of Bots in a handoff order with blocked Kanban cards. Everything Cabinet makes can be removed again from My Bots, and a Bot that brodification's own Bots catalog carries is handed over to it, never duplicated. Disclosure — fetches its Bot catalog from https://botcabinet.com/catalog.json on open and Refresh (data only, 2 MB cap) and, after you confirm, creates brodification profiles whose instructions (SOUL.md) come from that catalog; can create and archive Kanban cards for a crew; deletes only profiles it created that you have not changed; reads ~/.brodification/profiles and hashes profile files to track what it made; calls private brodification modules (brodification_cli.profiles, kanban_db), so a brodification update can break it; no shell, credentials, telemetry or self-updates.

entries.name: bot-forge
entries.description: Say "make me a <role>" and your agent spawns a complete Bot Mode Bot — name, face, SOUL.md, memory, tools, skills, routines, gateway — tested, with rollback. Then hire a whole crew in one call, ask what is waiting on you, and edit, teach, share and health-check Bots by chatting. Disclosure — spawns the brodification CLI to create and run Bot profiles under BRODIFICATION_HOME/profiles/, and installs its own small companion hook plugin (bot-forge-marks, two hooks, no tools) into each Bot profile it manages, enabling it in that profile's config.yaml; never the root profile. Disclosure — when a Bot journals a blocked/failed entry, the plugin emails its title and summary to your own address via the SMTP account in brodification' EMAIL_* settings (TLS verified; off with notify_blocked or notify_email false); adopt_bots (off by default) installs the companion hook into every profile on load.

entries.name: brain-graph
entries.description: Local Markdown vault for brodification Desktop — notes, wikilinks, search, recycle bin, and an interactive graph.

entries.name: brave-search
entries.description: Brave Search API tools for live web search inside brodification

entries.name: brethof-brain
entries.description: brethof-brain long-term memory provider — the memory's briefing in the system prompt at session start, ambient recall on every turn, every turn archived; one memory shared with the user's other agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more). Sends each turn to the user's own brethof-brain memory (on their machine at 127.0.0.1:8610, or hosted at memory.brethof.cloud). Needs a brethof-brain account. Disclosure — sends every user prompt and each turn's user and assistant text, with your API key, to the brethof-brain server you configure (default a local box at 127.0.0.1:8610; hosted at memory.brethof.cloud), and puts the server's returned briefing and recall text into the system prompt and each turn; reads BRETHOF_BRAIN_* from $BRODIFICATION_HOME/.env and ~/.brethof-brain/config.json.

entries.name: bridge-adapter
entries.description: Generic JSON-file-based bridge adapter. Bridges self-register via a registry/ manifest (presence = registered, rm = unregistered). Polls inbox/ for incoming messages, writes outgoing to outbox/. External services (imsg, Matrix, Telegram, ...) write/read JSON files in a shared directory.

entries.name: brodification-aac
entries.title: brodification AAC
entries.description: Communication boards, explicit speech, switch scanning and reviewed AI proposals for brodification Desktop. Disclosure — Desktop-only page; Speak sends your message text through the brodification gateway to the TTS provider configured in brodification (cloud providers receive it) and the audio plays on the gateway host, which may be remote; the AI helpers open a separate brodification chat session per request and send your topic or message as a normal agent turn on your model provider; saved phrases and approved boards are kept in plaintext in the plugin's Desktop storage.
known_issues: Experimental, nonclinical AAC; requires brodification Desktop and configured services for optional AI and speech.
Screenshots are actual React renders with mocked SDK/native boundaries, not live provider proof.
Saved phrases and approved boards persist locally in plaintext; full config is read-only through SDK.
Speech is submission acknowledgement only; backend-owned audio may play on a remote gateway host.
No speech Stop, request-scoped cancellation, completion or later playback error tracking; Stop scanning remains independent.
No voice catalog or model/provider/settings writes; configure in brodification Settings.
Explicit expression tags require a current ElevenLabs v3 config snapshot, not an atomic guarantee or provider attestation.

entries.name: brodification-activity
entries.title: Activity
entries.description: brodification Desktop session analytics and provider-reported usage: annual heatmaps, token mix, model breakdowns and source-period summaries. Disclosure — reads the selected profile's state.db read-only and, for the Providers tab, an Activity cache under plugin-data/brodification-activity plus the optional Quota quota_cache.json. Fetch provider data runs a local Node.js (22.18+) collector and, only on that explicit click, calls chatgpt.com through brodification's signed-in Codex request route (requires_auth: openai-codex) and api.commandcode.ai, opencode.ai and ollama.com with the optional API keys you configure as plugin secrets; it stores usage aggregates and hashed key identifiers locally. No other credential reads, telemetry or sign-in flow; remote profiles go through the configured gateway.

entries.name: brodification-adaptive-effort
entries.description: Choose a separate scorer to set the reasoning effort of each brodification request. Disclosure — off by default; when a mode is enabled (or on an explicit `/hae probe`), sends the latest user message (or the parent-written subagent goal), truncated to 4000 characters, plus any configured guidance to the scorer you select (TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai by default, or OpenAI Decisions, OpenRouter, Cloudflare Workers AI, Nace at console.nace.ai, or a custom URL) using that service's key; opt-in settings can also send the target model identity, up to 6 earlier user/assistant text messages (1200 characters each) and a separate continuation question to the same scorer; in brodification Desktop it also sets the focused chat's session reasoning selector through the gateway `config.set` API after each applied change, and it keeps a prompt-free effort-change history (64 changes × 64 conversations), per-conversation mode overrides (at most 256 conversations) and per-route cache verdicts built from provider token counters (at most 128 routes) in its plugin data directory.
entries.title: brodification Adaptive Effort
known_issues: Pre-release: live effort acceptance is only partially validated; see the v0.3.0 release notes for the per-route evidence.

0.4.0 removes the custom `chat_completions` scorer format and OpenRouter chat-model scoring; such configurations fail open (effort unchanged) until moved to a `systemone` endpoint or an OpenRouter decision model.

entries.name: brodification-agent-builder
entries.title: brodification Builder
entries.description: Guided Desktop workspace in BOTS: tailored questions, reference files, editable instructions and capabilities, version comparisons, model-only trials, and native Bot Chat handoff. Saves specialists as separate brodification profiles and installs the Builder companion plugin into its own bot profile. Disclosure — "Talk to Builder" auto-creates a brodification-builder profile cloned from the active profile with copied .env/auth.json and copies+enables this plugin there outside the catalog installer (uninstall does not remove that copy); "Save agent" creates new profiles the same way and rewrites their tool/skill selection.
known_issues: Windows Desktop runtime testing remains; the installer and renderer use portable paths and APIs.

entries.name: brodification-agent-mixer
entries.title: Agent Mixer
entries.description: A mixing desk for how much a coding agent may change: four enforced dials (edits, write-scope globs, per-turn line budget, new-dependency policy) with /mixer, live presets, a Desktop dial panel in the composer, a web-dashboard saved-defaults bar and a steering-console page. Also drives Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI through the agent-mixer hook command. Disclosure — enforces edit/scope/line-budget/new-dependency dials in pre_tool_call (blocks, or escalates "ask" to brodification approval, which /yolo skips) and adds a one-line rules context via pre_llm_call when a dial is off its default; per-session dial state is stored under BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/brodification-agent-mixer/sessions/, and the Desktop panel and dashboard bar write the plugin's own saved defaults into config.yaml (plugins.entries.brodification-agent-mixer.settings); the separately installed agent-mixer CLI keeps its own state in ~/.config/agent-mixer and ~/.local/state/agent-mixer, writes hook entries into ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/commands/mixer.md, ~/.codex/hooks.json or ~/.gemini/settings.json only when run as `agent-mixer install <harness> --yes`, and `agent-mixer ui` serves a token-guarded console on 127.0.0.1:8377.

entries.name: brodification-anilist
entries.description: AniList tracker for brodification Desktop — airing countdowns, a season browser, a local or account-backed watchlist, episode alerts and a daily digest, plus agent tools that read your own list and answer about a single show. Disclosure — stores your pasted AniList token in the active profile .env (sent only to graphql.anilist.co); alerts and the daily digest are brodification cron jobs it creates on the host you pick, and the digest job asks that host's agent to query the public AniList API itself.

entries.name: brodification-asgard
entries.title: Asgard
entries.description: Twelve Norse gods carved in runestone and wood: Odin, Thor, Freyja, Loki, Frigg, Baldur, Tyr, Heimdall, Hel, Skadi, Freyr and Bragi, as brodification Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: brodification-atoll
entries.title: brodification Notch Plugin
entries.description: Native brodification plugin that runs the local Atoll notch monitor for brodification session and turn status on macOS. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts a detached Node daemon on every brodification session that reads state.db read-only and sends session titles, model/profile/token stats and a ≤96-char redacted preview of your latest request to the third-party Atoll notch app over localhost. brodification notch setup clones and builds the author's Atoll fork (github.com/himanusia/Atoll at a pinned commit, not reviewed here) with Xcode and installs an unnotarized app to ~/Applications. Node deps install via brodification's npm ci prompt. Run brodification notch stop before removing.

entries.name: brodification-auto-titler
entries.description: Topic-aware session title tracking for brodification. brodification generates the first title by default; AutoTitler follows conversation changes and session close without changing the host title-generation switch. Disclosure — sends excerpts of each conversation (sampled user turns, short assistant replies, compaction summaries) to your brodification title-generation model in the background, also for up to 200 recent untitled sessions at startup; needs plugins.entries.brodification-auto-titler.llm.allow_task_override (or allow_provider/model_override for a custom route). 0.3 no longer edits config.yaml, but users upgrading from 0.2.x keep auxiliary.title_generation.enabled=false until they re-enable it (/autotitler status shows the fix).

entries.name: brodification-beads
entries.description: Native Beads (bd) work-graph plugin: fixed-argv adapter, scoped ready frontier, claim with read-back, guarded writes. Six tools over an explicit store path + actor; honest exit-code map incl. stale-13; plain bd stays fully sufficient (escape hatch). No desktop pane ships yet.

entries.name: brodification-blogwatcher
entries.title: Blogwatcher
entries.description: A Blogwatcher inbox for brodification Desktop and web, with themes, read controls and on-demand AI summaries. Disclosure: runs the original Blogwatcher CLI against its database; scans contact subscribed sites; requested summaries fetch public pages and send text to the configured brodification model after consent, which may incur costs. Summaries are cached locally. No telemetry or self-update.
known_issues: Requires the original Hyaxia/blogwatcher CLI on the brodification backend host; the blogwatcher-cli fork is not supported.
Remote Desktop clients need desktop/plugin.js copied locally. Restart the dashboard/API server after installing the backend.

entries.name: brodification-board
entries.title: Board
entries.description: A Miro-like board the agent draws with its own tools and you edit in a desktop pane, both sides working on one JSON document. board_apply builds a whole diagram in one call from ordered ops (nodes, edges, free lines, groups, notes, captions, layered auto-layout, bus trunks); board_render writes a PNG for chat or the interactive HTML editor; board_watch reports your own pane edits back to the agent. The pane docks beside the conversation with the same editor, saves your edits, and takes agent updates live. Disclosure — board_render shells out to a headless Chrome/Chromium already on PATH (nothing is downloaded; private temp profile, sandbox kept unless running as root) for PNG and self-test rendering; boards live in ~/.brodification/board/ shared across profiles (BRODIFICATION_BOARD_DIR / BRODIFICATION_BOARD_RENDER_DIR / BRODIFICATION_BOARD_WATCH override); serves /api/plugins/brodification-board/ on the plugin host; reads this profile's state.db read-only to find the session board_watch should wake; no external network calls and no stored credentials; board_watch's wake into a messaging chat additionally needs plugins.entries.brodification-board.allow_gateway_injection: true.

entries.name: brodification-boot-screen
entries.title: brodification Boot Screen
entries.description: Six-act boot animation for the brodification desktop app — black-screen brand reveal, over-exposed whiteout bridge, a technical-dossier plate, an authorization handshake with identity confirmation, and a welcome finale — with audio cues, theme-aware light/dark plates and Esc/Enter/Space controls. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Fully English UI. Adapted from 6shenhonghong9/dsh-startup-screen (MIT). Disclosure — on every Desktop launch (default: once per session) it covers the whole window with a full-screen animation that plays audio and spoken narration and waits for Enter/Space/click on two steps (Esc skips); while it is up it captures Enter/Space/Esc at the document level. Turn it off or switch to daily in its Startup Animation settings page.

entries.name: brodification-bot-hq
entries.description: Desktop fleet page plus a per-bot Home (status, metrics, alerts, tasks, routines, buttons) published by the bot as JSON. Disclosure — reads each local profile's home files, can run a declared cron routine from the UI on that bot's profile and credentials, and opens chat, a path, or a URL the bot declared; send_prompt buttons send the shown prompt into the bot's Bot Chat. Bot-declared run_action buttons run a script from the bot's home/actions/ folder: a script runs only after the user approves that exact file (SHA-256), is re-approved if it changes, and is limited to 30s and to that folder, but it runs as your user with the brodification backend's full environment, including provider keys loaded for the profile brodification was launched with. Approvals are kept under the brodification root in bot-hq/approvals/. The `brodification brodification-bot-hq setup` command (asks first unless --yes) links the plugin into every profile's plugins folder and enables it there. No database, signup, or telemetry.
entries.title: Bot HQ

entries.name: brodification-call-ledger
entries.description: Per-call cost ledger for brodification Desktop: every model call brodification makes is recorded from the observer hooks (provider, model, tokens, duration, outcome) and paired with the charge the billing provider actually took; works with no billing account, priced by brodification' own estimate where the price book knows the model. English or Vietnamese; dong or dollars. Disclosure — three observer hooks (post_api_request, post_auxiliary_call, api_request_error) record per-call metadata from every profile in the install (session id, platform, task, provider, model, token counts, duration, finish reason, context length; never prompt, response or tool-argument text) into one shared SQLite ledger at <install root>/plugin-data/call-ledger/calls.sqlite, and import this plugin's own older per-profile ledgers into it once. It caches the vilao.ai model list there and the USD-to-VND rate under the active profile's plugin-data/call-ledger. Network is GET-only: vilao.ai (wallet balance, per-request usage, consumer keys) with VILAO_PAT read through brodification's secret scope (vilao issues one full-scope token per account, including wallet writes; this plugin only reads), the public vilao.ai model list with no credential, and open.er-api.com for the dollar rate. The first full billing pull pages back through up to ten years of the account's usage. Nothing runs while the Desktop page is closed. Derived from brodification-resetwatch (Adolanium, MIT).

entries.name: brodification-cloud-file-manager
entries.title: Cloud File Manager
entries.description: Cloud Files for brodification Desktop — browse, search and sort by date, create folders and bulk-upload files and whole folders to the machine your agent runs on, preview its images, PDFs and code files, download a file, read and edit its Markdown and text files (view first; nothing is written until you press Save in the review, which shows the line diff for files up to 20,000 lines), drag files into the chat, import files from the agent's own Google Drive, and hand the agent file locations from the chat + menu without re-uploading. Built for remote gateways (token or sign-in); works locally too. Ships one plugin skill, brodification-cloud-file-manager:cloud-file-manager-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — adds a file API to the gateway (dashboard plugin routes under the gateway's existing auth) over the agent's working folders: the configured roots, else terminal.cwd, TERMINAL_CWD or MESSAGING_CWD, else the gateway user's home with its dot-entries hidden. It lists, sorts and searches those folders, reads the files you open or preview (Markdown and .txt files up to 1 MiB in the editor; the first 1 MiB of other code and text files; images and PDFs up to 10 MiB), creates folders, and writes uploads, Drive imports and editor saves (staged as hidden .cfm-* temp files in the destination folder; a name clash keeps both files). It overwrites only an existing .md/.markdown/.txt file you open and explicitly Save in its editor (refused if the file changed since you opened it). It has no delete action: it removes only its own .cfm-* staging files and folders (aborted ones, and stale ones over a day old) and, when an upload or import fails to publish, the empty file it had reserved for it. It never follows links out of those folders, and its file API never exposes the agent's brodification home apart from a working folder set inside it (roots, terminal.cwd, or a workspace/ folder it creates when the working folder would be the home itself). Download and drag into the chat use brodification Desktop's own authenticated file download and @file/@folder references; the plugin adds no route for them. Desktop listens for the agent's tool-completion events to refresh the open folder. Apart from Desktop's calls to the gateway and the report skill's GitHub requests, its only network use is Google Drive, read-only, through the agent's own google-workspace skill, whose scripts (from skills/productivity/google-workspace in the agent's brodification home, else the copy bundled with brodification) it runs with the gateway's Python and a minimal environment without API keys, buffering their output in the gateway's temp directory; the plugin never reads the Google token. While Desktop is open it re-checks the plugin and Drive sign-in about once a minute. The report skill runs brodification --version, brodification plugins list and brodification logs (filtered to this plugin), may save its search words, title and draft as local files, and searches electricsheephq/brodification-cloud-file-manager issues with gh or a web tool before drafting; it posts a public issue or comment there only after the user approves the exact title and text.
known_issues: In a split layout with two agents' chats side by side, a drag started while one agent's chat is in focus can be dropped into the other agent's chat; the reference then names a path on the wrong machine (no file moves between agents). Use Add to chat, or focus the target chat before dragging (electricsheephq/brodification-cloud-file-manager#55).

entries.name: brodification-codex-resets
entries.title: Codex Resets
entries.description: Know the moment OpenAI resets your Codex usage limits. A status-bar chip counts the time since the last reset; when a new one lands, a small card rises out of it (chip-only while you type), with a history page of every reset. Disclosure — polls the public codex-resets.com API every 60 s and loads fonts from Google Fonts; sends nothing about you or your sessions.

entries.name: brodification-context-overview
entries.title: Context Overview
entries.description: A Context button in the bottom status bar that shows how full the focused conversation's context window is: token budget, estimated allocation by category and context-file metadata, also during a running turn. Read-only, no backend.

entries.name: brodification-council
entries.description: LLM Council (karpathy/llm-council) as a brodification plugin. Four fixed advisor seats (First-Principles Analyst, Skeptic, Pragmatist, Researcher) answer in parallel, anonymously review and rank each other, and a Chairman model synthesizes the final answer. Members borrow your existing provider credentials - no API keys. Registers a Council group in every model menu, a council_deliberate tool, /council, brodification council CLI, and a desktop panel. Disclosure — council_deliberate and the Council model fan each prompt (as a session model, the whole conversation) out to every seat, judge and chairman model you assign, up to 2N+1 billed calls per turn on your existing provider credentials; it also adds a non-secret "council" marker row to auth.json and keeps run history in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/council/runs/.

entries.name: brodification-cron
entries.description: Operating skill for brodification cron: lifecycle rules (pause vs disable vs remove, `in 30m` vs `30m`), four ways to avoid needless LLM runs (no_agent, wakeAgent pre-check, monitor, [SILENT]), verify-after-change, a layered runbook and a read-only doctor that complements `brodification cron doctor` and reports one error across several jobs as one scheduler fault and a cron store that cannot be written. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — skill only, no network; the bundled doctor reads ~/.brodification/cron/jobs.json, ticker stamps and executions.db (or a named profile's store with --profile) read-only, checks the cron directory's permissions and free space without writing, and runs the local brodification cron doctor (argument list, no shell), whose job loader may repair malformed jobs.json entries (--no-builtin skips it).

entries.name: brodification-desktop-camera
entries.description: A camera button for the brodification Desktop composer. Open the preview, take a photo, and the frame lands in the composer as an image attachment, ready to send.

entries.name: brodification-discord-rpc
entries.description: Native Discord Rich Presence (RPC) integration for brodification — real-time session, model, token, and tool tracking with local-only IPC. Disclosure — publishes your most recent session title (or, in full title mode, the workspace folder name), model name and token total to the local Discord client as Rich Presence every 3 s (visible to other Discord users); opt-in settings also publish the git branch and a "View Repository" button with the public github.com/gitlab.com remote URL (credentials, ports and other hosts stripped); reads ~/.brodification/state.db read-only; reads the active workspace's .git/HEAD and .git/config read-only to resolve repository and branch; on Linux may scan running Discord processes' environment via psutil to find XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; writes a small presence-ownership file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (or the system temp dir) and, under herdr, queries the local HERDR_SOCKET_PATH socket for pane focus.

entries.name: brodification-dpapi-secrets
entries.description: Resolve brodification environment variables at startup from a single secret file encrypted with the Windows Data Protection API, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.dpapi.map, an ENV_VAR -> store-name mapping (bare names or dpapi:// names) plus an optional file path (default <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/secrets.dpapi). The file is one DPAPI blob keyed by the current Windows user profile, so it is unreadable by another Windows account and worthless off the machine; it is written by the bundled CLI (python -m brodification_dpapi_secrets set NAME, value read from a prompt or stdin, never from argv) and only read at runtime. Mapped names that are missing or empty are skipped with a warning; a file that is not ours, a blob this user cannot decrypt, or a payload that is not a flat string map is reported as an error with nothing injected. Disclosure - this source decrypts a file for every brodification process that enables it: resolved values become environment variables of the brodification process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. User-scope encryption only (the machine-wide flag is never used and is not exposed), and the at-rest protection is a bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles, not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no subprocesses, no network calls, no self-update. Windows only. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — decrypts a DPAPI-encrypted secret file (default <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/secrets.dpapi) at startup for every brodification process that enables it, and the resolved values become environment variables of brodification and its child processes like `.env` entries; the encryption is per Windows user and protects backups, cloud sync and copied files, not against other code running as the same user. Local only: no network calls, no subprocesses.

entries.name: brodification-dreaming
entries.description: Nightly deterministic memory consolidation ("dreaming"): corroborates candidate facts with what humans actually said on distinct days, proposes the few worth keeping with a verbatim edit anchor, asks whether stale memory entries still hold, and wakes the agent only when there is work — including a memory file close to its char limit. Fact sources: the holographic store, a SQLite or JSONL export, or none. Secrets and instructions are screened by the dream's own rules plus a verbatim copy of the holographic plugin's screen (scripts/holo_screen.py, MIT, same maintainer), applied to stored facts and human messages before anything reaches memory, the report or the model. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — scripts make no network or LLM calls and open state.db and every fact store read-only (SQLite mode=ro; with holographic >= 0.15.0 including its fact_versions/fact_confirmations tables, to say who stands behind a fact); they also read brodification config.yaml's memory/timezone keys and the holographic plugin's db_path/scope/cron_writes/min_trust_threshold (the floor recall applies, so a rejected fact is only reported when the store still trusts it) and, to say so in install.py --check, embeddings/mirror_memory_writes, the pending/memory approval queue, cron/jobs.json (to find their own jobs) and — only when chat_stores is set, with holographic scope user/chat/thread — the per-chat databases next to the store (counts of every one; facts of the chats listed in promote_from). The user-run installer copies three gate scripts into $BRODIFICATION_HOME/scripts, seeds $BRODIFICATION_HOME/dreaming.json and, through brodification' cron Python API, creates (or with --rebind re-points) two agent cron jobs bound to this plugin's own skill with only the memory toolset, plus one no_agent job (every 15 min, no model) that reads the fact stores to keep a hash index of diary lines and, for facts holographic >= 0.8.0 has forgotten, rewrites the dream's own cache files and diary without them and deletes the output files of the dream's own cron jobs that mention them (by id or verbatim text); with a chat --deliver target the reports are attached as a session you can reply to. The agent runs send recent human messages (up to 200 / 40k chars, each with its chat type and sender id) and fact snippets to your configured model; state goes to $BRODIFICATION_HOME/cache and a diary to $BRODIFICATION_HOME/memories/DREAMS.md (configurable); memory files are changed by the agent only through the regular memory tool, and with the holographic provider it also adds candidate facts via fact_store (with holographic >= 0.15.0 marked said or inferred; with holographic >= 0.8.0 also change / end / correct / forget, the last three only on a human's own answer; forget is irreversible), lowers trust on human-rejected facts via fact_feedback, with holographic >= 0.15.0 raises trust (fact_feedback confirmed, +0.05, at most 10 facts a night) on facts people repeated on two or more different days and, when keywords.enabled is set (off by default), adds search keywords to facts via fact_store update.

entries.name: brodification-experientiallabs
entries.description: Experiential Labs - OpenAI-compatible multi-model gateway provider (chat, /model picker, aux and curated fallback models, /usage wallet snapshot). All network calls go to api.experientiallabs.ai - /v1 chat + models via brodification' own transport, /api/v1/credits and /api/v1/key only when /usage runs; no telemetry; credentials resolve through brodification routes (brodification auth / .env). Disclosure — When you pick Experiential Labs as your model, every prompt, tool result and attachment of that session goes to api.experientiallabs.ai, a third-party gateway that routes to upstream model vendors. /usage sends your key to its Cost API (GET /credits and /key) or to the cost_api_base you set. Independent integration, not affiliated with Experiential Labs.

entries.name: brodification-federated-search
entries.description: Federated web search backend (provider name `federated`): fans one query out to multiple configured search backends in parallel and returns merged, deduplicated, relevance-ranked results (keyword scoring; optional LLM re-rank with automatic fallback). Phase 2 — official settings-page exposure (config_schema, six keys) merged with the legacy web.federated block, and per-line multi-card credential pools (environment-variable names only) with automatic failover and host-aligned cooldowns. Phase 3 — a desktop card config page (Settings → Plugins; opt-in via Settings → Skills & Tools → Plugins): one card per line, two-level membership checkboxes (backends / credentials), add/remove lines and keys, a per-line Key rotation strategy (pool_strategy), an LLM ranker model picker (seventh schema key `ranker`), and a current-settings string with paste import; no type picker/badges (`type` round-trips verbatim); every edit serializes back to the settings tree (string ↔ UI parity). The LLM re-rank request pins thinking off (`reasoning_effort=off`) and the card page states it. Disclosure — reads the operator's config.yaml (read-only) for its own settings (web.federated and plugins.entries.brodification-federated-search.settings); sends the query to the operator-configured sub-backends (registered providers or custom HTTP endpoints); no telemetry, no subprocesses, no credential storage (key values stay in the runtime environment).

entries.name: brodification-field-notes
entries.description: Field notes for a brodification install: search known pitfalls before debugging and record new ones with root cause; register every local core edit as a patch note with a declarative checks file, then verify read-only after each brodification update (OK / MISSING / UPSTREAMED / N/A / UNKNOWN with reason) and list core files changed outside the registry. Ships 42 pitfalls and 10 patch recipes checked against 0.22.0. Optional pinned Telegram dashboard edited in place by an hourly no_agent cron job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; never edits the core or runs patch scripts. Disclosure — its scripts only read the brodification core (pyproject.toml, read-only git status/diff) and never edit it or run patch scripts; the skill does walk the agent through hand-editing core files from its patch recipes and re-running the owner's re-apply scripts, each only after the user says yes. Network: Telegram Bot API only when the dashboard is enabled (reuses the agent's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from env or ~/.brodification/.env), and the public GitHub API without credentials (latest release plus compare against the installed commit SHA, cached 12 h; upstream.check=false disables). Writes: the notes store (~/.brodification/field-notes), ~/.brodification/field-notes.json, state and lock files in ~/.brodification/cache, a copy of the cron script in ~/.brodification/scripts when install.py runs (the skill runs it on first use), and one hourly no_agent cron job only when the user runs install_cron.py (it reads ~/.brodification/installs/*/facts.json to find brodification' own Python and re-runs itself with it). Without a dashboard chat, install_cron.py sends the job's alerts to the Telegram home channel when TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL is set (read from env or ~/.brodification/.env), else local.

entries.name: brodification-fleet-connector
entries.title: brodification Fleet Connector
entries.description: Owner-approved universal phone pairing and bundled read-only Live Operations reporting for selected brodification profiles. Disclosure — paired phones get broad fleet:operator access over the internet, including cron jobs (unattended runs), Kanban task dispatch and media reads, and see live session titles/previews and subagent goals from the profiles you select for reporting; any messaging account you make an owner (with a one-time claim code from `brodification fleet claim`) can create pairing links and approve phones from a private chat, so that account's security is your host's security. Runs an explicitly activated background connector/reverse proxy behind your HTTPS origin and may launch a local brodification backend; legacy QR flow opens a private local browser. Keeps an owner-only control socket in the system temp directory, plus pairing/owner state and shared local snapshots; reads selected profiles' session registries through private read-only imports. `brodification fleet reporting configure --apply` edits the selected profiles' config.yaml (with a backup). Local idle/retirement maintenance is explicit and not exposed to phones. Reporting adds no control power.
known_issues: Native platform/auth-provider operation requires plugins.isolation: in_process; host-isolated and mixed/multiplexed reporting contexts fail closed. Isolation is never downgraded.

macOS local acceptance includes existing phone pairing continuity and nine healthy idle reporting processes; Linux and other runtime/OS results are separate CI evidence. Active agent/delegation acceptance is not claimed.
Private read-only brodification registry imports can break on future releases. Validator retains a service caution and private-import warnings; no core runtime override is detected.

Trusted HTTPS origin reachable from host and phone is required. Legacy QR display additionally requires qrencode and an authenticated GUI/browser; terminal approval-code pairing does not require Telegram. Native Windows is unsupported; WSL browser display is experimental.

entries.name: brodification-gemini-live
entries.description: Realtime duplex voice with the Gemini Live API, built around handing real work to brodification. A single control in the composer (not a floating panel): tap, speak, hear the model, and when the ask needs files, a terminal, the web or memory the voice model delegates the job to the api server and keeps talking, reading the outcome aloud when it lands. Three verbs rather than thirty schemas — brodification_task starts, brodification_tasks reads the call's task board, and brodification_task_update denies, steers or stops a task. A task that stops to ask permission reaches the user as a spoken prompt and a "brodification needs you" indicator with Approve and Deny buttons; only the user's press approves it, never the voice model. Multi-task is one Live session plus a board, not a session per task. Mute drops the uplink without hanging up, and the call survives composer remounts, so opening a session mid-sentence does not kill it. Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live socket and the key, and the renderer is never given either, because the Live API carries the credential in the socket URL. Ships no Python dependencies of its own, which keeps it out of the uv workspace and lets one clone serve several profiles. Tested model behaviour is published in the README, including that gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking accepts a function declaration and then delegates only about 2 times in 5, which is why gemini-3.8-live is the default. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GEMINI_API_KEY from the brodification home's .env; delegated work runs as a brodification run in the serving profile's own memory with the profile's full toolset via the local api_server and API_SERVER_KEY, and those runs' results (up to 4000 characters each), the task board and approval prompts are sent back to Gemini as text. Nothing is sent anywhere else and no telemetry is emitted.

entries.name: brodification-gensyn-delphi
entries.description: Seven read-only tools. Disclosure — Seven read-only tools for Gensyn Delphi prediction markets; no funds move and nothing is signed or sent. Needs Node.js 20.18+ and a manual `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in the plugin folder (installs the pinned @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk and its locked npm deps) before the tools work. Runs a local Node subprocess per call (25 s deadline, not a sandbox). Sends your DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY only to delphi-api.gensyn.ai (testnet) or api.delphi.fyi (mainnet); history and quotes read api.goldsky.com and gensyn-testnet/mainnet.g.alchemy.com without the key, and quotes use a throwaway in-memory key the SDK requires. Tools are on for every surface by default, including messaging gateways, where anyone admitted can run these reads on the owner's key (rate limit 30 requests per minute per process); disable per surface with `brodification tools`.

entries.name: brodification-gensyn-ree
entries.description: ree_validate_receipt, ree_verify_receipt, ree_infer. Validate does not re-execute and does not stand behind text_output, finish_reason, token_count, model.name, or ree_version. Verify re-executes on CPU. Infer runs one of three small models and writes one receipt. Disclosure — Starts containers from the local image gensynai/ree:v0.8.0 (pinned by digest) and never pulls it; running docker pull yourself is consent to the REE-Binary-License. ree_verify_receipt and ree_infer mount ~/.cache/gensyn and ~/.cache/huggingface read-write (a Hugging Face token file stored there is visible to the container; no token is passed in the environment), may download Hugging Face weights for any model a receipt names, and their container network is not limited to Hugging Face; they ask for brodification approval on every call and refuse under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended runs, host isolation, or when the approval API is missing. ree_validate_receipt runs with network none, does not ask, and returns no receipt text. Any person admitted to one of your gateways can call these tools and approve containers on your Docker daemon; disable per surface with brodification tools. Choosing "always" adds one config.yaml allowlist line per call and never covers the next call. New receipts and temporary work files are written under ~/.cache/brodification-ree; nothing is stored under BRODIFICATION_HOME. The container is not a hostile-code sandbox. No cron is created.

entries.name: brodification-guide
entries.description: Read-only diagnostics for brodification configuration: /brodification-doctor in-session and brodification guide in a terminal. Eight read-only health checks (config, mcp, skills, commands, hooks, plugins, memories, sessions) and points to 21 troubleshooting skills, installed separately as a skills tap, for what the built-in doctor doesn't cover. Complements — never replaces — brodification doctor. Disclosure — reads config.yaml, SKILL.md frontmatter, skill bundles, plugin manifests, the shell-hooks allowlist and the built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md stores read-only (the report quotes short memory snippets); the sessions scope reads the tail of logs/agent.log read-only for runaway-session signatures (session ids, model names and token counts appear in the report); registers one read-only plugin skill, brodification-guide:start, listed in model sessions while the plugin is enabled; /brodification-doctor and brodification guide run brodification config path and brodification hooks doctor as subprocesses (argument list, no shell), and brodification hooks doctor executes every approved shell hook once with a synthetic payload; with opt-in proactive: true it runs the checks (including the agent.log scan) in-process at each session start/end (no hooks executed) and once per process runs git ls-remote against the plugin's GitHub repo to log a newer-release notice (no download, no local writes). The 21 troubleshooting skills are not loaded by the plugin: they install separately from the repo as a skills tap, which this entry's pin does not cover.

entries.name: brodification-herald
entries.description: Cross-profile agent dispatch for brodification — 12 tools for agents talking to agents: async dispatch with SSE completion, synchronous multi-turn chat, model-selectable in-process subagents, a durable SQLite run ledger, fail-closed per-target model-route discovery, and host-owned bare LLM inference. Disclosure — sends task text and bearer tokens to the brodification API servers you configure (plaintext HTTP permitted, warn-only); stores full dispatch text in a local SQLite ledger; delegate_subagent may use any provider credential you have configured.

entries.name: brodification-honcho-plugin
entries.title: Honcho Memory
entries.description: Desktop workbench for the Honcho memory behind the focused chat: read the newest conclusions, trace their premises, search messages, ask scoped questions, and add confirmed corrections or source files. Uses each profile's existing Honcho provider configuration. Disclosure — talks only to the Honcho server each profile is already configured for, through brodification's own Honcho client and credentials, and polls it about every 10 seconds for the focused chat while Desktop is open. Ask runs a Honcho reasoning call that may use credits. Add fact/correction and Add to session write to Honcho only after you confirm the target in a dialog; Add to session uploads the text or PDF/JSON/text file you choose. A chat from another local profile is read with that profile's own Honcho configuration, only where this plugin is enabled. It reads the focused chat's title and folder from the profile's session database, read-only. No telemetry.

entries.name: brodification-impossibl
entries.description: Impossibl, the AI gateway (100+ models from every major lab behind one OpenAI-compatible API), as a model provider

entries.name: brodification-insight
entries.description: Selection-definition lookup for brodification Desktop. Select any text, get an AI definition with sources in a popup. Renders the definition inline, runnable code aside. Backend is a stateless brodification insight CLI; panel, providers, and one-click model picking are configurable. Disclosure — definitions are generated with your configured provider keys (the selected term, your format template and optional web-search results are sent to that provider) via a short-lived `brodification insight` CLI run; no background process remains. When web search is on it also queries your configured searxng instance and fetches result thumbnails from their image hosts, inlining them into the panel; nothing is fetched without a searxng URL.

entries.name: brodification-iroh-interconnect
entries.description: Authenticated brodification agent-to-agent tasks and optional file transfer over Iroh QUIC. Disclosure — tasks from a paired peer run in your live gateway agent with its full toolset; pairing is confirmed via the tool's confirm=true argument, not a UI prompt. Uses n0's public relays by default (BRODIFICATION_IROH_RELAY=off or a self-hosted URL for LAN-only). iroh_send_file can share any readable path the model names (credential-name denylist only, overridable with allow_sensitive); remote-triggered auto-fetch is off by default and confined to BRODIFICATION_IROH_AUTO_FETCH_DIR. The Rust sidecar is built locally with cargo, never downloaded.

entries.name: brodification-jailbreak-kernel
entries.description: Jailbreak-kernel plugin for brodification (ported from dsh-infinite-gen-4): session-scoped modes (off/slim/on/full) with kernel profiles (core/research/creative/max), session-aware system-prompt sections, llm_request request-layer system rebuild, and opencode session rotation, removing model refusals. Ships a /jailbreak command, a progressive-disclosure ops skill, and a 276-check offline self-test. Disclosure — llm_request middleware that, by default (`on`/`full` modes), replaces the system prompt on every request with a refusal-removal ("jailbreak") kernel plus only the memory and runtime-environment sections (agent rules, skills index, context files and other plugins' sections are dropped); `slim` appends it instead, and `off` passes requests through but strips all plugin prompt sections, including other plugins'. Rotates the x-opencode-session header on opencode routes. Writes a diagnostic dump per session (full system prompt incl. memory/persona text, plus the first 200 chars of every other message and the model/provider/base_url) to its own plugin dir (dumps/); `/jailbreak dump off` or `BRODIFICATION_JAILBREAK_DUMP=0` turns it off. No network, no exec.

entries.name: brodification-jetstream
entries.description: NATS JetStream event bus: agents publish events (nats_publish), pull one batch (nats_fetch), and wake on subject matches — live-session watches or wake routes (config-declared or runtime-registered via jetstream_wake) with durable consumers, manual ack, an idempotent wake ledger and rate rails; an opt-in lifecycle tap mirrors brodification events onto brodification.> subjects. Disclosure — connects only to the NATS servers in your own config (no third-party calls, no telemetry); the platform adapter holds persistent subscriptions and reconnect loops for the gateway's lifetime; token/nkey/user-pass secrets come from ${VAR} references read via the profile-scoped secret scope and a configured creds file is read from its path, never written or rotated; wake routes render event payloads into prompts that start gateway turns or fire an existing cron job (optionally under another named profile), the agent itself can add up to 16 durable wake routes with jetstream_wake that persist in plugin data across restarts (subject still limited to subscribe_allowed, no cron-job or cross-profile targets), and jetstream_watch injects matching events into the live session when allow_gateway_injection is on, so keep subscribe_allowed scoped to trusted publishers.

entries.name: brodification-jina
entries.description: Jina Reader web backend for web_extract (r.jina.ai, works without a key) and web_search (s.jina.ai, needs JINA_API_KEY). Unofficial; not affiliated with Jina AI.

entries.name: brodification-kame-api-rotation
entries.description: Smart API key rotation: the healthiest key for every call, each 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / quota refusal sized from its own evidence. Install with its companion brodification-kame-provider, which hands brodification this plugin's rotating client through ProviderProfile.create_client (and create_messages_client where brodification offers it); no core override. Disclosure — /kame-keys add|import|split, and on start a key variable holding several comma-joined keys, write one auth.json pool row per key through brodification' pool API after a plaintext backup (last 5 kept; switch: resolver_disabled); key-redacted, size-capped owner-only local logs and a status file per profile; the Desktop panel reads that file and queues its settings requests through its own dashboard/plugin_api.py route (GET /state, POST /control, this plugin's plugin-data folder only); while every key is resting, chats (CLI, Desktop, messaging gateway) keep waiting with no total limit (each key's rest capped by max_hold_seconds) and cron runs give up after 300 s with the provider's refusal unless max_total_wait_seconds is set.

entries.name: brodification-kame-provider
entries.description: Companion to brodification-kame-api-rotation (install both). A model-provider plugin that re-registers brodification' bundled API-key profiles unchanged except for create_client and create_messages_client, which return the rotation plugin's key-rotating client; otherwise None and brodification builds its own. Same endpoints as brodification, no third-party service, no core override.

entries.name: brodification-kemet
entries.title: Kemet
entries.description: Twelve Egyptian gods in painted relief and gold leaf: Thoth, Ra, Isis, Osiris, Anubis, Horus, Bastet, Sekhmet, Set, Nut, Ptah and Hathor, as brodification Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: brodification-lang-ca
entries.description: Catalan (Català) language pack for brodification — UI translation for core (CLI, gateway, approval prompts and tips), TUI and Desktop. Covers all text-overridable catalog keys; preserves command syntax and non-text Desktop values. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: brodification-lang-el
entries.description: Greek (Ελληνικά) language pack for brodification — Desktop UI (~5,060 of 5,065 keys) plus the 102 most visible core CLI slash-command descriptions; missing keys fall back to English. TUI and the remaining core CLI strings are not covered yet. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: brodification-lang-it-full
entries.description: Italian (Italiano) language pack for brodification Desktop — 5,082 of 5,085 keys on main (firstRun, themePicker, connector accounts and the update-channel picker included; the 3 the pack format rejects are array/object leaves that fall back to English). Core, CLI and TUI keep the Italian catalogs already bundled with brodification. Generated from the hand-reviewed typed catalog maintained in gradia64/brodification-agent (gradia-desktop-it branch); function-backed keys ship as positional {0} templates. Independent community translation, unrelated to brodification-lang-it. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: brodification-lang-it
entries.description: Italian (Italiano) language pack for brodification — UI translation for core (approval prompts, gateway/slash replies, CLI, tips), TUI and Desktop. Coverage: core 3437/3437, TUI 1259/1259 and Desktop ~5,000 keys (missing ones fall back to English). Parser-safe: hard-parsed menu brackets and [Y/n] prompts stay verbatim; placeholders, URLs and CLI flags preserved. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Traduzione italiana dell'interfaccia brodification. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: brodification-lang-ko
entries.description: Korean (한국어) language pack for brodification Desktop — Desktop UI (4,962 of 5,065 keys on v0.21.7, 4,982 of 5,085 on main); CLI, gateway and TUI keep the Korean catalogs already bundled with brodification. Independent translation from the English source; values identical to English are omitted so missing strings fall back to English. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: brodification-lang-pt-br
entries.title: Brazilian Portuguese (Português do Brasil) Language Pack
entries.description: Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) language pack for brodification covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,477/3,477 keys), the Ink TUI (1,356/1,356) and the Desktop app (5,172/5,176). Every translatable key exists and every value is translated against the English source of `main`: no key upstream has since removed, zero placeholder divergence, and the four remaining Desktop keys are arrays/structured values a text pack cannot carry. Checked with `brodification plugins validate` and with the pack's own `tools/verify_pack.py`, which also runs as public CI on every push. Core and TUI mirror the bundled `pt` locale, registered as a real `pt-br` variant so it wins over the `pt`/`pt-BR` alias; the Desktop catalog is the original contribution (first proposed upstream in PR #92590, 2026-08-23), since the Desktop app ships no Portuguese at all. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `brodification config set display.language pt-br`. A weekly drift workflow reports when `main` adds or drops keys; nothing self-updates. Tradução pt-BR da interface do brodification.

entries.name: brodification-lang-th
entries.title: Thai (ภาษาไทย) Language Pack
entries.description: Thai (ภาษาไทย) language pack covering all three brodification UI surfaces — Desktop (5,023/5,030), core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,437/3,437), and the Ink TUI (1,259/1,259) — 9,719/9,725 keys total (99.9%). All three catalogs checked against the English reference with `brodification plugins validate`. Manifest-only plugin: flat nested YAML overlays under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `brodification config set display.language th`. Disclosure — text-only catalogs (no code, network or dependencies); untranslated keys fall back to English: the 7 array/conditional Desktop keys listed in the repo README, plus strings brodification added after the pack was built.

entries.name: brodification-lang-vi
entries.description: Vietnamese (Tieng Viet) language pack for brodification — full UI translation across every surface: core (approval prompts, gateway/slash replies, CLI, tips), TUI, and Desktop catalogs. Checked against the English catalogs with brodification plugins validate. Parser-safe: hard-parsed menu brackets and [Y/n] prompts stay verbatim; placeholders, URLs and CLI flags preserved; multi-line values use real newlines exactly like the English catalogs. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Ban dich tieng Viet day du cho toan bo giao dien brodification. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: brodification-lcm-x
entries.title: LCM-X
entries.description: Lossless memory for long sessions: LCM-X keeps every turn in a local store instead of compacting it away, and the agent can search and expand it. The store is local SQLite (lcm.db) with a recoverable DAG of summaries over it and 15 lcm_* tools for search, recall and expansion. Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from brodification-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop brodification, then in plugins.enabled replace brodification-lcm with brodification-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model brodification is configured with. Disclosure — optional semantic recall (embeddings_enabled, off by default) sends message text to the embedding provider you configure (Voyage via VOYAGE_API_KEY, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama), and once enabled new summaries are embedded automatically in the background; in-process FastEmbed keeps it on the machine after a one-time model download. For known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in), and oversized tool outputs are by default written as plaintext files under BRODIFICATION_HOME/lcm-large-outputs and replaced in the model's context by recoverable references. The engine also reads brodification' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on brodification builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm_status/lcm_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use.

entries.name: brodification-ledgerline
entries.description: Inspect session costs and usage in brodification Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-live-voice
entries.description: Full-duplex Live Voice for brodification Desktop — GPT-Live-1 on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription via the local Codex app-server, with live transcript, voice tool calls and task delegation to the user chat. Disclosure — subscription voice uses your brodification openai-codex sign-in through brodification-signed requests (requires_auth; the plugin never holds or refreshes the token) to mint OpenAI Realtime client secrets, and the usage panel reads brodification's own account-usage fetcher; the gpt-live-1 lane runs the local codex app-server on the Codex CLI's own login, and the dashboard can run codex login --device-auth, copying ~/.codex/auth.json (or $CODEX_HOME) to a backup before that login, restoring the backup if the login is cancelled, and reading the file read-only for sign-in status; with TALK_OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY set it uses that key instead; if brodification-talk is installed it loads that plugin's modules from ~/.brodification/plugins/brodification-talk and substitutes its own talk_auth; voice audio goes to OpenAI over WebRTC, and spoken tasks are submitted as messages in your focused chat.

entries.name: brodification-loadout
entries.description: Desktop pane to manage skills and MCP connections across agent apps: save named loadouts, review changes, apply them, and undo the latest managed operation.
