Agent half is inert (no tools or hooks). Disclosure — MCP sync copies your brodification mcp_servers env/header secrets into ~/.codex/config.toml and claude_desktop_config.json (with 0600 backups).

entries.name: brodification-memory-pane
entries.title: Memory Pane
entries.description: A brodification Desktop pane for the built-in memory: see what the focused chat remembered, updated or forgot, and edit, delete or undo any entry without leaving the conversation. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — a tool_execution middleware reads MEMORY.md and USER.md around each memory call and logs the entry-level changes to $BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/brodification-memory-pane/; the pane rewrites memory entries only when the user edits, deletes, adds or undoes one, through brodification's own memory store; no network, credentials, shell commands or background processes.

entries.name: brodification-memory-ui
entries.description: Read-only brodification Dashboard and Desktop plugin for inspecting built-in, holographic, Mem0, Honcho, Mnemosyne, Hindsight, and ByteRover memory. Disclosure — reads the active profile's memory files, provider configs and provider API keys (keys are never returned to the UI), and on user action sends search/recall/reflect queries with configured bank/peer/user IDs to the configured Mem0, Honcho and Hindsight endpoints (Hindsight Cloud default api.hindsight.vectorize.io) using those keys; ByteRover queries run the local `brv` CLI; for a local embedded Hindsight setup a contents read may start the `hindsight-embed` daemon; no memory is written.

entries.name: brodification-memory-wiki
entries.description: Memory Wiki dashboard tab: browsable subject pages and daily logs derived from local session history, plus a read-only Persistent Memory (MEMORY.md / USER.md) audit panel.

entries.name: brodification-minimizer
entries.title: Minimizer
entries.description: YAGNI coding and code-review guidance for brodification: reduce over-engineering, reuse existing behavior, and preserve requirements. One static prompt section; no tools or hooks.
known_issues: Guidance is advisory, not enforcement; existing session prompts may retain it after disabling.

entries.name: brodification-mobile
entries.title: brodification Mobile Adapter
entries.description: WebSocket platform for your own mobile, desktop or web app: it talks to the agent directly — text, voice, images, video and documents in both directions, approval/clarify/slash cards answered from the app, streaming edits, typing and avatar state events, cron delivery to a chosen device. On request it also answers command-catalog and model-list frames (commands from the agent's own registry, models from its model inventory) so a client renders command and model pickers from the agent's data instead of bundling a snapshot; auto-push after ready is off by default (MOBILE_CATALOG_AFTER_READY=1). Ships TypeScript and Python SDKs, platform guides and an acceptance checklist. Disclosure — opens a listening WebSocket server (plain ws://, no built-in TLS; 127.0.0.1:8787 by default, the wildcard address only when set, behind a wss proxy) guarded by MOBILE_TOKEN plus optional per-device tokens; anyone holding an unbound token can chat with the agent, run slash commands and answer the approval and clarify cards of the device id they connect as; device_id=token entries bind a token to one device. deliver frames are accepted only from loopback peers or MOBILE_DELIVER_TOKENS. Inbound media is written under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/mobile-media; secrets are read through brodification's profile-scoped route; approvals resolve through brodification's own resolvers; no telemetry, no third-party network calls, no self-update.

entries.name: brodification-monitor
entries.description: Kanban worker health in the Desktop status bar — live activity per running card with stall and loop detection (same tool + same arguments repeated), plus a compact per-provider quota readout (the related ai-usage-tracker plugin covers quota windows as a standalone feature). Zero model tokens. Disclosure — opens BRODIFICATION_HOME/kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only for worker activity; for quota chips it reads every brodification profile's credential pool (each profile's auth.json, with that profile's .env as secret scope) into read-only snapshots plus DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the environment or .env files, and calls brodification' own account-usage fetchers for each configured provider (Anthropic, Codex, OpenRouter, DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance, and any provider plugin exposing fetch_account_usage), sending each entry's own token only to its own provider. The plugin never refreshes or persists a credential; on a Codex HTTP 401, brodification core may refresh the active profile's matching Codex token via OpenAI's token endpoint and rewrite that profile's auth.json. No other network egress.
entries.maintainer: brodification Monitor contributors (independent of Nous Research)

entries.name: brodification-monitoring-dashboard
entries.title: Monitoring Dashboard
entries.description: Prompt-customizable desktop dashboard with live host metrics, session activity, clocks, calendars, and text widgets. Disclosure — polls ~/monitoring-dashboard on the desktop device through the Desktop native file bridge, and its Reset command moves only the dashboard's own page/panel marker files in that folder to the OS trash (never dashboard.json or the folder); host metrics and session activity stay on the machine.

entries.name: brodification-mpp
entries.description: Pay supported HTTP 402 MPP challenges on Tempo through mpp_fetch and in-process HTTPX clients. Uses a dedicated wallet. Disclosure — with MPP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS unset, any supported HTTP 402 MPP challenge returned to core HTTPX traffic (not only mpp_fetch) is auto-paid from the Tempo wallet with no per-payment cap or confirmation; the origin allowlist is the operator's control.

entries.name: brodification-muse-code
entries.description: Muse Spark in brodification billed to the Muse Code monthly login (device-code login, no API key).

entries.name: brodification-muse
entries.description: A proactive companion for brodification: follows accepted goals (active/done/cancelled), prepares sourced research and Feed articles, maintains memory, and assembles rolling 30-day or natural-month calendar views. Read-only local Dashboard/Desktop pages show Feed, Ideas and Goals; profile selection cannot install, enable or disable Muse in any profile. One Skill, one state tool and six fixed recurring jobs; selected notices and weekly/monthly reports go to the active profile's Bot Chat and run an assistant turn there. Sources, authorization, quiet hours and actual result/delivery receipts remain distinct; partial coverage is not global availability. Disclosure: first load creates profile-local files/SQLite state and owned Cron scripts/jobs. Private/local input inbox rows retain their first 8000 characters and source identities, with associated chat/user routing IDs when present. The newest 500 remain; older rows are cleaned on later input only after both hourly/nightly cursors cover them. Unprocessed backlog can exceed 500 and has no fixed retention time. Native conversations/tool results are read separately; research records can retain returned payloads. Idempotency journals and oversized tool results stay in the profile state database without automatic expiry and may contain written content or tool output. Bounded conversation previews support full revision-checked paging. Delegates are instructed to remain read-only under inherited permissions, not sandboxed. Workers always use public delegate_task dispatch and follow the user's delegation settings; leave delegation.provider/model empty to keep the parent model. New Cron watches require cron.allow_agent_scheduling; local goal registration creates no job. Watch prompt/stop fields each allow 4000 characters; new repeating watches (interval or cron) must be at least 30 minutes apart, one-off schedules are exempt. Windows is not supported (POSIX file locks) and CI does not cover it. Background work incurs normal model/tool costs. No telemetry, self-updater, mandatory service, core/SOUL replacement or phone/read-receipt guarantee. Native remove retains data/tasks for the documented owned-only cleanup.

entries.name: brodification-newswire
entries.description: Breaking-news ticker for brodification Desktop: a scrolling RSS/Atom/JSON-Feed strip above the statusbar with per-source favicons, feed search + discovery, grouping modes, offline cache, and in-app reading. Zero API keys, zero model tokens.

entries.name: brodification-nous-prices
entries.description: Browse Nous Portal model prices and account balances in brodification Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-office
entries.description: View and manage Bot Mode agents in a shared office in brodification Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-openwhispr
entries.description: Local-first OpenWhispr dictation history and shared notes for brodification agents: find what the user said, search notes, transcribe local audio. Free local desktop bridge by default, paid cloud opt-in only. Skill-carrier plugin, no tools or hooks registered. Disclosure — skill only: the agent runs the external OpenWhispr CLI (installed with an unpinned `npm install -g @openwhispr/cli`) through the terminal tool to read your dictation history and notes over the OpenWhispr desktop app's authenticated loopback bridge, and, with your consent each time, to create, update or delete notes, transcriptions and dictionary entries and to transcribe local audio files; OpenWhispr Cloud (api.openwhispr.com, including an email-code sign-in that mints an API key kept in the CLI's own config) is used only when you opt in; the agent never opens credential files itself.

entries.name: brodification-opper
entries.description: Opper, the EU-hosted AI gateway (700+ models behind one OpenAI-compatible API), as a model provider

entries.name: brodification-pantheon
entries.title: Pantheon
entries.description: Eighteen brodification Desktop themes in dithered classical marble, one god each: all twelve Olympians plus Hades, Nyx, Helios, Selene and Medusa. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers eighteen themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while a Pantheon theme is active. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: brodification-pickup
entries.description: Pick up where you left off: up to 10 cards (5 by default) of unfinished work from your recent brodification chats, project folders and files, each with where you stopped and a one-click next step. Adapted from Herald OS by Luke (iamlukethedev), MIT. Disclosure — after explicit in-app consent (stored per profile), each Refresh reads recent chats from every profile's session store (read-only; profiles the user skips in Settings are never opened) and sends chat excerpts and metadata, project/file names and paths, git branch/changed-file names and recent commit subjects to the current profile's brodification LLM route (the auxiliary title-generation model, main provider unless configured); runs read-only git and, on macOS, Spotlight `mdfind`; never reads document contents; writes only $BRODIFICATION_HOME/pickup/. The "Next step" button can submit a model-written prompt straight into the card's chat in one click. The optional install.sh, when asked, adds the plugin to every profile's plugins.enabled (undone exactly by uninstall.sh).
known_issues: On installs with several profiles, brodification issue #134712 can make the Desktop backend answer Plugin not found; the page explains the fix (enable brodification-pickup in every profile, then restart Desktop).

entries.name: brodification-pii
entries.description: Uses local Presidio and spaCy to redact supported PII in outgoing user text. Disclosure — filters Chat Completions user messages and Responses user input locally; system prompts, tool outputs and tool-call arguments are preserved. Fail-open: detector errors, including a missing model, send original text. Install spaCy en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 separately from its GitHub release wheel in the brodification Python environment before enabling; brodification installs only the named PyPI dependencies. No runtime model downloads or remote detection.

entries.name: brodification-plex-music
entries.description: Mini-Plexamp for brodification Desktop: statusbar player for your Plex music library — likes synced to Liked Songs, custom playlists with rename/delete, shuffle + repeat, sleep timer, queue editing, OS media keys. Needs only Plex Media Server. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — talks only to the Plex Media Server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:32400), sending your Plex token in the request URL as Plex requires; the token is stored in Desktop plugin storage, and the optional "Get token…" button reads the Plex `.LocalAdminToken` file you pick. Likes and playlist create/rename/delete write to your Plex server. No agent tools, no telemetry.

entries.name: brodification-plugin-chrome-profiles
entries.description: Switch brodification browser tools to a named Chromium-family profile (Chrome, Edge, Brave), local or remote, over CDP.

entries.name: brodification-plugin-gen
entries.description: Generate, scaffold, and extend brodification plugins from simple descriptions.

entries.name: brodification-plugin-guard
entries.description: Static review of candidate brodification plugins; target code is never executed.

entries.name: brodification-plugin-netbox
entries.description: NetBox change management: query DCIM/IPAM objects, build a reviewed field-level diff, apply with a journal and roll back.

entries.name: brodification-pokemon
entries.title: brodification Pokémon
entries.description: A cozy pixel-art companion garden for brodification Desktop with three starters, nicknames, fetch, berries, XP, and optional evolution through all nine starter forms. The companion keeps you company on long turns, reacts quietly to failures, to what brodification is doing and to turns finishing in other chats, and lives through seasons with real day length and moon phases, offline showers, wild visitors it greets in character, old-friend cameos, keepsakes, milestones that leave a bench, a lantern and bunting in the garden, and a sapling that grows with the days. Reachable from the keyboard, the status bar and the command palette. Independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab community contributions; artwork is excluded from the source-code MIT license. Uses local plugin storage and read-only session activity, with no runtime network requests, credentials, backend, or model calls. Disclosure — independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab contributions that are excluded from the MIT code license; reads session busy state and message-complete/tool-start/tool-complete events read-only (other chats contribute only "a turn finished"), focuses the composer (caret only, no text) or reveals its own pane only on a user click or command, saves a PNG snapshot to your downloads only when you click Save a snapshot, and keeps companion state in plugin storage; no network or model calls.

entries.name: brodification-project-stewardship
entries.description: Durable project ownership and bounded initiative management for brodification fleets. Disclosure — a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a project's saved rules, decisions and facts to turns of bots assigned to that project; objective checks run allowlisted local programs only at autonomy level 3+ and GitHub objectives shell out to your own `gh api`; it creates and edits brodification Kanban tasks through brodification' internal kanban modules (title/body/tenant written directly to kanban.db), keeps its own SQLite DB under `<brodification home>/plugin-data/brodification-dockyard/`, and its optional HTTP API (`/stewardship/v1`, 127.0.0.1) stays closed until you set a bearer token.

entries.name: brodification-pubky
entries.description: Setup helper for managed Pubky agents. The launcher syncs agent state, including conversation database snapshots and portable configuration, to your remote Pubky homeserver.

entries.name: brodification-quest
entries.description: Read-only pixel-art RPG view of real brodification Kanban and worker activity, with a live web dashboard tab and an optional native Desktop page. The Desktop page currently supports explicit local connections only; registry and SSH remote connections fail closed until a public SDK connection-lifecycle hook is available. Standalone demo data is synthetic. Disclosure — reads local brodification data outside its own directory (kanban.db, every profile's state.db, profile.yaml, config.yaml model/effort, logs/agent.log, bot-status.json) on each dashboard poll: every /replay or /events request (about every 10 s while the tab is open) runs the bundled Python extractor as a subprocess (argument list, no shell, 30 s timeout); a background thread samples bot-status.json every 30 s (BRODIFICATION_QUEST_SAMPLER=off disables it) and writes bot-status history, checkpoint state, a lock and a random 0600 HMAC key under <brodification_home>/brodification-quest/ (not yet plugin-data); profile names and task titles are hidden unless enabled and only shown to host-authenticated dashboard sessions; the Desktop page works only on an explicit local connection; no network calls beyond the local brodification backend.

entries.name: brodification-resetwatch
entries.description: Track subscription quotas and reset times in brodification Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the brodification Python interpreter located via BRODIFICATION_PYTHON / VIRTUAL_ENV / the parent process or the brodification installer's managed venv (BRODIFICATION_HOME/installs); it reads provider API keys from the brodification .env, brodification's own saved OAuth logins (auth.json credential pool, read-only), the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden_cache.json, read-only, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source) and Docker s6 container env files, plus other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins (including macOS keychain entries), and sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint.

entries.name: brodification-rich-ui
entries.description: Rich, evidence-backed answer cards — tables, charts, metrics, timelines, sources — rendered inline in the desktop transcript Disclosure — Image and ImageGallery cards load agent-supplied https image URLs (up to 8 per gallery) from any host when the card renders in Desktop

entries.name: brodification-routines
entries.title: brodification Routines
entries.description: A minimal Routines page in brodification Desktop that turns crontab's five cron.manage actions into a plain-language interface for non-developers - name a routine, pick a schedule, write the prompt, and pause or resume it. No cron syntax, no service, no database; routine data stays in the host.

entries.name: brodification-rss
entries.description: Read RSS and Atom feeds and discuss articles in brodification Desktop. Disclosure — feeds and full articles are fetched with curl through the gateway's shell.exec on the connected brodification host (public-IPv4 SSRF guard); opt-in AI grading sends article excerpts to your configured model and creates BRODIFICATION_HOME/skills/rss-importance-grading/SKILL.md if missing; opt-in image loading fetches publisher images directly from Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-rustpush-imessage
entries.description: Local-only iMessage platform plugin backed by a launchd-supervised OpenBubbles RustPush sidecar over a same-user Unix socket.

entries.name: brodification-security-audit
entries.description: Approval-gated local security audit for brodification using Gitleaks, OSV-Scanner, and Semgrep CE.

entries.name: brodification-self-healing-context
entries.title: brodification Self-Healing Context
entries.description:
Intercepts runtime errors and dynamically patches the context window 
using local SQLite FTS5 memory for zero-downtime recovery.

entries.name: brodification-seo
entries.title: brodification SEO
entries.description: Native brodification port of Claude SEO 2.4.2: 45 SEO workflow and specialist skills, a credential-scoped brodification_seo_run tool, an isolated Python runtime, and advisory JSON-LD feedback. Derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0). Disclosure — derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0); the brodification_seo_run tool starts local subprocesses in the brodification host process, not a Docker terminal sandbox, and model-supplied script arguments may name host paths, so it can read host files (the Gemini image-edit utility uploads the named file to Google, the IndexNow utility reads a URL-list file); `brodification seo setup` downloads Python packages from PyPI within version ranges into a private environment and optionally Chromium through Playwright; audits fetch user-selected websites; separately configured providers (Moz, Bing Webmaster, Keywords Everywhere, Google APIs, Matomo, DataForSEO, IndexNow, Google Gemini) receive the data sent to them and may incur charges; skills ask before paid or mutating calls but the tool does not enforce approvals; Gemini images are saved to ~/Documents/nanobanana_generated, and other runtime state stays in brodification plugin data storage; provider keys are read from the active brodification profile and passed only to the script that needs them; Google OAuth workflows are disabled; no telemetry, bundled credentials, background process or self-updater.

entries.name: brodification-session-diff
entries.description: Persistent session file diffs, run comparisons, and individual edit history in brodification Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-session-reset-policy
entries.description: Opt-in idle/daily gateway conversation resets. Reads the existing session_reset block (mode idle | daily | both, idle_minutes, at_hour) and starts a fresh session on the first inbound message past the boundary. No timers, no background writes.

entries.name: brodification-session-warmer
entries.description: Opt-in bounded idle prompt warming for explicitly allowlisted OpenAI-compatible text-chat endpoints. Sends potentially billable requests; no tool execution or conversation writes. Does not support Codex/Responses or native Anthropic. Authenticated endpoints use optional BRODIFICATION_SESSION_WARMER_API_KEY.

entries.name: brodification-sidepulse
entries.description: SidePulse lifecycle status backend; Desktop focus tracking requires the separate companion in the linked setup guide. Disclosure — forwards event names, a hashed agent id, the raw session_id and tool names to a local AF_UNIX socket and a 0600 jsonl log; no network egress.

entries.name: brodification-slash-router
entries.description: Jev-powered routing for misspelled, shortened, and meaning-based slash commands in the brodification Desktop composer. Preserves drafts when unsure. Requires a TypeSafe API key; every non-exact lookup uses paid TypeSafe API usage. Disclosure — every non-exact slash token is sent through the plugin's local backend to api.typesafe.ai (paid, your TYPESAFE_API_KEY) together with the Desktop command catalog (names and descriptions), any prior route, up to 8 saved correction explanations and any clarification you type into its panel; message arguments and conversation content are not sent; the backend reads BRODIFICATION_HOME/.env only to check whether TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set.

entries.name: brodification-snapcompact
entries.description: Snapcompact context engine: archives conversation history as dense bitmap PNG frames that vision models read back at ~1/3 the token cost.

entries.name: brodification-speech
entries.description: Give your agent the voice it deserves. Guided TTS and STT setup for brodification, with voice search and previews, model switching, testing, and native spoken replies across supported providers. Access 80+ speech models through a single API key with the AllModels router.

entries.name: brodification-ssh
entries.description: Manage SSH connections and remote workspaces in brodification Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-structured-aux-models
entries.description: Routes selected brodification auxiliary tasks (approval, MCP sampling, compression) through bounded Jev decision calls on OpenRouter instead of free-form chat prompts, failing open to the operator's own auxiliary provider for anything it cannot express as a decision. Disclosure — sends redacted approval prompts, MCP tool names and compression transcript blocks to openrouter.ai using your OpenRouter key (read-only); on any error approvals escalate to you, never auto-approve; the default decision_model is a moving alias, pin it.

entries.name: brodification-stt-enhance
entries.description: Local speech-to-text (provider stt_enhance) with faster-whisper or opt-in sherpa-onnx Parakeet V3 and long-audio chunking, plus an optional bounded LLM pass that enhances the transcript using a custom skill, an inline prompt or the default, and keeps the raw transcript on failure. Disclosure — audio is decoded locally. Post-processing is on by default and sends the transcript text to the LLM brodification routes the stt_enhance auxiliary task to (your main, usually remote, provider unless you point it at a local endpoint or set post_processing.enabled: false). It reads the body of the SKILL.md you configure (never executed) and runs ffmpeg/ffprobe. The opt-in Parakeet backend reads a local model export and, on first use and only when your config.yaml explicitly sets security.allow_lazy_installs: true, installs pinned sherpa-onnx and numpy from PyPI into ~/.brodification/plugin-runtimes/brodification-stt-enhance/ (shared by all profiles). No tools, hooks, background processes, telemetry or stored credentials.

entries.name: brodification-subscription-meter
entries.description: Provider-neutral subscription quota matrix panel — each provider's subscription window as a single time x quota row (elapsed vs remaining at a glance), with UI-side show/hide per provider row. Disclosure — reads provider keys from the current profile's .env and token presence from its auth.json, and calls each provider's own usage/balance API with that key (Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, Command Code, DeepSeek, xAI management, OpenRouter, Alibaba Cloud BSS, Grok, Codex via brodification); an optional shared_sources setting reads another profile's .env/auth.json the same way; nothing is written outside this plugin's settings.

entries.name: brodification-switchyard
entries.description: Jev-powered brodification plugin for skill/model routing, typed assess, DOM/Cua computer use, adaptive reasoning effort with a per-turn receipt line, and FTS rerank. Disclosure: the default-on adaptive llm_request sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message to TypeSafe/OpenRouter after brodification redact_for_egress (no history or tool output); greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call; without the brodification redactor it sends metadata only (disable via adaptive_reasoning_effort false). Separate default-on hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters of the current user turn after brodification redact_for_egress, plus skill names, to the same provider; without the redactor it stays local (opt down to local_only); light turns (greetings, closed acknowledgements, and read-only listings) skip that hosted call by default. Model routing remains advisory. Disclosure — By default, adaptive effort sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message, and hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters plus skill names, to TypeSafe/OpenRouter Jev after brodification redact_for_egress (greetings and light turns stay local). The jev_session_search_rerank and jev_computer_use DOM tools send query/card and public-page text using the plugin's own masking. Off unless enabled: evidence prefetch sends source files the user names under evidence_finder_root (up to 80 KB), cross-tool stuck advice sends redacted error excerpts, and the switchyard-approvals provider, once selected for auxiliary.approval, sends flagged shell commands and your approval policy to OpenRouter Jev, whose confident verdict can auto-approve them (any failure falls back to a human prompt). /switchyard effort receipt saves the plugin's own setting to config.yaml.

entries.name: brodification-t3-control
entries.description: Bounded tools to list, read, create, and control local T3 coding threads on Linux and WSL2.

entries.name: brodification-tabular
entries.description: Tabular AI that grows with your tables — brodification skills for honest tabular ML, one entry point. Disclosure — Installing pulls numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, pyarrow, joblib and pyyaml into brodification's environment. The skills have the agent run Python on your data files, may ask it to pip install catboost, tabicl/torch, mapie or matplotlib, and the TabICL skill downloads a pretrained checkpoint of a few hundred MB on first use. Saved checkpoints are pickles: load only ones you made.

entries.name: brodification-tailscale
entries.description: Browse Tailscale devices and connect to remote brodification instances in brodification Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-talk
entries.description: Realtime voice for brodification through terminal, Discord, dashboard and Desktop. Live voice mode (TALK_VOICE_MODE=live, TALK_LIVE_AUTH=subscription) connects with your own Codex OAuth session to the undocumented chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls endpoint, which is outside the vendor's published API terms and may change or stop working without notice.

entries.name: brodification-taskbar-badge
entries.description: Windows taskbar badge on the brodification window when a turn finishes. Calls navigator.setAppBadge on the message.complete event while the window is in the background, and clears it when the window regains focus or another session is opened. Disclosure — no network calls and no data leaves the machine; the badge is drawn by the app's own Electron process, which maps the Chromium Badging API onto the Windows taskbar overlay.

entries.name: brodification-teammates
entries.description: Give your agent a team: named subagents with their own instructions, tools and model, which it assigns work to, checks on and steers mid-task. The operator defines the roster; the agent follows up with a digest of earlier results and can work a Kanban teammates lane with a review handoff. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent_lifecycle API. Stock brodification; no patched core. Disclosure — adds six tools (teammates_roster, teammate_assign, teammate_check, teammate_wait, teammate_message, teammate_stop) and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process brodification subagents using credentials selected by brodification from the parent, delegation settings or an operator-configured teammate route where supported. Toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write_file and patch); brodification can add inherited MCP toolsets back unless delegation.inherit_mcp_toolsets is false. A teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering uses the lifecycle steer where brodification provides it, otherwise delegate_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent. Under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. Optionally the roster is read from an operator-named YAML file (roster_file, relative to the profile home or absolute, so several profiles can share one); the plugin never writes it. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries, role hashes and available token receipts; no full transcripts). It does not read credential stores. Where supported in-process, subagent_start and post_api_request hooks collect token receipts for mapped child sessions. For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. It runs one in-process monitor thread per run to retain finished results and, for lane runs, keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own. Completion-notice code exists but never injects on current brodification because the host cannot bind notices to the receiving session; use teammate_wait instead. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this repository with gh only after the user approves the draft.

entries.name: brodification-telegram-business
entries.description: Observe-with-approval Telegram Business Mode (secretary bot): brodification drafts replies to your customers' messages and DMs each draft to you with Send, Edit and Discard buttons; nothing reaches a customer until you tap Send. A brodification Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — each customer message is sent to your active brodification model to draft the reply, and drafts and connection records are stored locally in <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/telegram-business/state.db.

entries.name: brodification-telemetry-dashboard
entries.description: Dashboard-only read plugin: visualize the shared-metrics telemetry brodification collects locally — metric families, drilldowns, milestone timeline, install snapshot, and the exact next package payload. Send stays off.

entries.name: brodification-telemetry
entries.description: Observability + budget guardrails for brodification — tokens, cost, latency, tool calls per session and cron job. Persists to local SQLite. Exposes /stats and /budget slash commands. Disclosure — records per-session tokens, cost, latency, tool names and sender/profile ids (no message text) in ~/.brodification/telemetry/telemetry.db; fetches public model pricing from openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on first load and at most once a day; in the default enforce mode first load writes a $5/day, $100/month global budget to telemetry/budget.yaml, and a hard breach blocks every tool call and pauses the over-budget cron job until the window resets (set plugins.entries.brodification-telemetry.settings.mode: observe to record without enforcing); the optional standalone dashboard server binds 127.0.0.1 with no auth.

entries.name: brodification-tenuo
entries.description:
Security guardrails for brodification tool calls: per-call authorization, so a prompt injection cannot make the agent do more than you allowed. Each call is checked against a signed, expiring permission slip (a warrant) before the handler runs, down to the arguments (file paths, search queries, spending limits), and every decision lands in a local audit log. Give cron jobs, delegate_task subagents and gateway users their own policy.
Disclosure — brodification-tenuo is a no-op until a warrant is configured and blocks every tool call in a kanban worker that has no per-task warrant; it appends every tool call's name and full arguments to $BRODIFICATION_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false); when TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane.
entries.title: Tenuo

entries.name: brodification-terminal
entries.description: Run the brodification terminal interface in a brodification Desktop workspace tab.

entries.name: brodification-token-speed
entries.description: Live decode tokens-per-second chip for the brodification Desktop status bar: 1-second sliding window while the model is still streaming, tool execution time excluded from decode seconds, UI spinner frames never counted, TTFT tracked separately, cumulative totals calibrated against authoritative provider usage at turn end. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: brodification-toolsmith
entries.description: Local developer tools, transformation recipes, and reviewed chat handoff inside brodification Desktop.

entries.name: brodification-town
entries.description: Local pixel-art town where every brodification session is a resident and every tool call walks to a building. Passive lifecycle bridge to a loopback-only server; prompts, arguments, and output never leave the process. Disclosure — version 0.3.0 bundles the Town Node server and a prebuilt browser app inside the plugin directory and adds a brodification town setup/start/status/stop/open command tree. Nothing is downloaded and no npm install runs at any point; node (^20.19 or >=22.12) must already be installed and is launched only by the explicit brodification town start command, bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Runtime state, a 0600 bridge token, a bounded event journal and rotated server logs are written under BRODIFICATION_HOME/brodification-town/runtime/. On start the server also reads BRODIFICATION_HOME/cron/jobs.json (job id and enabled flag only) to place one resident per enabled scheduled job.

entries.name: brodification-tripo
entries.title: brodification Tripo
entries.description: Tripo 3D tools on Tripo's v3 API (openapi.tripo3d.ai). Text, photo or multiview to 3D, image edits, retexturing, splitting into parts, Smart UV, auto-rigging, preset animations, retopology, format conversion (FBX, USDZ, STL, 3MF, OBJ, GLTF) and downloads, with an inline 3D viewer and a Tripo library pane in brodification Desktop. Every credit-spending call goes through brodification's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a per-chat limit makes it ask again past 100 credits. Needs TRIPO_API_KEY. Unofficial; not affiliated with Tripo or VAST. Disclosure — sends prompts and the local images or 3D model files you or the agent name (up to 50 MB; every local-file upload, free calls included, goes through brodification's approval prompt) to Tripo's API at openapi.tripo3d.ai with TRIPO_API_KEY; saves downloaded models to $BRODIFICATION_HOME/tripo/ or a folder the agent picks (never overwriting: a clash gets a " (2)" suffix), and the Desktop viewer's save button copies models into your Downloads/Tripo folder; no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: brodification-trove
entries.description: DAG-based context engine that never loses a message — full-text search, semantic recall, assertion-backed evidence compilation, and pre-answer sufficiency gating Disclosure — replaces the context engine and stores every turn's full raw transcript in BRODIFICATION_HOME/trove.db with secret redaction OFF by default; with TROVE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=voyage, transcript text is sent to Voyage AI for embeddings; as a fallback it reads private AIAgent attributes read-only via frame inspection. No other network egress.

entries.name: brodification-vcc-engine
entries.description: Instant context compaction for brodification: builds the compaction summary in milliseconds with no LLM call, keeping the exact commands, exit codes, errors and files, each linked back to its original message for recall via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, shell commands or credentials; reads brodification's config.yaml through brodification's own loader; subclasses ContextCompressor and relies on its private methods, falling back to the stock compressor if they are missing.
entries.title: Instant Context Compactor

entries.name: brodification-vcc
entries.description: Algorithmic (no-LLM) context compaction engine: builds summaries by deterministic regex extraction instead of a summarizer-model call — zero-token, byte-reproducible, inside the built-in ContextCompressor; compacted turns stay searchable via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, no env vars, no secrets, no telemetry; registers no tools/hooks/middleware and reads only the turns the host passes for compaction; debug: true (default false) writes one metadata-only file $BRODIFICATION_HOME/vcc-debug.json. Derived from pi-vcc (MIT, sting8k)

entries.name: brodification-verifier
entries.description: Attach an independent verifier (advisor) model to your brodification session: it reviews each primary-agent turn delta, raises findings (note / caution / blocker), and can steer a blocker back into the session before the primary agent goes wrong. Read-only tool access (read_file, search_files) is available but off by default and best treated as opt-in plumbing -- measured across 216 reviews the reviewer made ~4 tool calls. Supports a VERIFIER.yml roster of named specialists, each with its own model and tool grant, plus VERIFIER.md review priorities. Ships disabled and off by default. Disclosure — off by default. When enabled, each primary turn's regex-redacted transcript delta goes to the verifier model's provider on that provider's terms and billing (one or more calls per turn per roster entry). So do any VERIFIER.md / VERIFIER.yml briefs found in BRODIFICATION_HOME and from the working directory up to the repo root (confined to that root, 256 KiB per file). A project VERIFIER.yml can add named verifiers and instructions whose findings are injected into your session, and a blocker finding can keep a coding turn going. With advisor_tools on, an advisor can read any file the session can read through read_file/search_files, and those reads also go to the provider. The optional engagement gate sends a ≤1,500-char redacted digest per turn. The optional phase gate sends the redacted arguments of an impending destructive or publishing tool call and can block that call (it fails open). Findings, reasoning, short redacted excerpts and gate decisions are logged under BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/brodification-verifier (rotated at 8 MB). Adds a /verify command, a dashboard API and a Desktop Verifier page. Development scripts (evals/, sidecar/, autoresearch/) run only when launched by hand: provider experiments use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the process environment or the host `brodification` CLI, and offline analysis reads the active profile's session database and decision logs. No telemetry, no runtime shell execution, no access to brodification's stored credentials.

entries.name: brodification-video-editor
entries.title: Video Editor (local FFmpeg)
entries.description: Local video editor for your own footage: 45 FFmpeg tools for the agent (cut, silence removal, 9:16 reframe, captions, music with ducking, loudness, platform export and checks) plus a visual editor in brodification Desktop with canvas, any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays and music, scenes and an English/German help. 100% local, no API key. Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Disclosure — the Desktop page starts a local web server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-run token) that can read and write media and image files anywhere under your home folder (and any VE_EDITOR_ROOTS); preview caches go to the system temp folder. The agent tools run ffmpeg/ffprobe on the input paths the model passes and write media, image or .srt files at the output paths it passes (replacing an existing file only with overwrite: true).
known_issues: Requires FFmpeg and ffprobe on PATH (apt install ffmpeg / brew install ffmpeg / winget install Gyan.FFmpeg).
lk_transcribe_captions is optional and needs 'pip install faster-whisper' plus a model already on disk.

The visual editor has one main video track plus any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays, audio and scenes; these items sit at fixed times and do not move when the main clips are cut (bundle them in a scene to move them together).

known_issues.Licence is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0: free for non-commercial use, commercial use needs a separate licence from Lokyy.de.

known_issues: The editor preview needs H.264 or VP8 playback in the app's browser engine; editing and export work without it.

entries.name: brodification-vision-inline
entries.description: Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision_analyze handler through tool_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image_input_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on brodification private vision helpers, so after a brodification update it may silently fall back to the normal path.

entries.name: brodification-whatsapp-voice
entries.title: WhatsApp Voice Calls
entries.description: Live voice calls with brodification over WhatsApp, on the linked-device (personal number) setup most brodification users already have, with no WhatsApp Business account. Call your bot's number and talk to your brodification: the voice uses brodification's own persona (a short briefing fetched from brodification) and hands real work to brodification mid-call. Or let brodification call you for things that matter: whatsapp_call_owner rings only the configured owner number (it has no destination parameter) and reports answered, no answer or declined, so the agent can fall back to another channel, including from cron. A short summary of each call arrives in WhatsApp. Speech runs on Gemini Live (gemini-3.8-live by default), reusing the Gemini key brodification already has; any Live setup field is configurable, plus a language lock. Setup is a dashboard tab (pairing QR, settings, test call) or an agent runbook skill. Disclosure — runs a separate sidecar process (Rust, built on whatsapp-rust) that the user starts or installs as a systemd/launchd user service; the binary is downloaded from this repo's GitHub release, built and attested by its release workflow, and checked against checksums pinned in the repo (plus the build attestation when the gh CLI is present). The sidecar becomes an extra linked device of the bot's WhatsApp number through an unofficial protocol, stores that session in the plugin's data directory, and answers only the owner's number. During calls it streams audio to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with GOOGLE_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY (read via get_secret), along with the persona briefing, the outgoing call's reason and ask_brodification results as text. It calls the local api_server with API_SERVER_KEY for ask_brodification (a full brodification turn with the owner's tools), the persona briefing (at startup and after each call) and the post-call summary, a run that may write to brodification memory and whose result is sent to the owner on WhatsApp. The dashboard tab's backend saves only this plugin's settings (through brodification config set), starts and stops pairing, places test calls to the owner, and restarts the sidecar service (systemctl --user or launchctl). No telemetry.
known_issues: Uses an unofficial, reverse-engineered WhatsApp protocol (whatsapp-rust): WhatsApp updates can break calls, and automated use may get the bot number restricted. Use a number you can afford to lose.
Prebuilt sidecar binaries cover Linux amd64/arm64 and macOS arm64; elsewhere it builds from source (Rust 1.94+, cmake, a C compiler).

entries.name: brodification-wincred
entries.description: Resolve brodification environment variables from the current user's Windows Credential Manager at startup, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.wincred.map, an ENV_VAR -> generic-credential-target mapping (bare names or wincred:// names); each value is read with CredReadW in the current user's vault and handed to the secret-source orchestrator, which applies it with the usual precedence, provenance and conflict rules. Values may be UTF-8 or UTF-16LE (cmdkey and the Credential UI write UTF-16); anything that does not decode to text, or that contains interior NULs, is skipped with a warning instead of being injected as a mangled key. Disclosure - this source reads your Windows Credential Manager: only the generic credentials named in the map, with no enumeration of the vault. Resolved values become environment variables of the brodification process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. The package is read-only and stdlib-only (ctypes): it never creates, updates or deletes credentials, writes no files, starts no subprocesses, makes no network calls and does not self-update. Windows only. Credential Manager is user-scoped, so this raises the at-rest bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles; it is not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — when enabled, reads only the Windows Credential Manager generic credentials named in secrets.wincred.map (no vault enumeration) and injects them as environment variables of the brodification process and its children, exactly like .env entries; read-only, stdlib ctypes, no subprocesses, no network, no file writes; user-scoped at-rest protection, not a boundary against code already running as the same user.

entries.name: brodification-windows-computer-use
entries.description: THEIA — The Human Environment Intelligence Aperture: virtual-desktop capture, fused stage observation, guarded caches, bounded dynamic workflows, and persistent raw-RGB LocateAnything C++/Q5 CUDA grounding.

entries.name: brodification-windows-ops
entries.description: Windows and WSL triage skills for brodification: processes that survive a quit (orphaned stdio MCP trees, lingering python/uv/node children), WSL-to-Windows interop where an argument reaches cmd.exe as shell syntax, config and encoding traps (UTF-8 BOM, legacy console code pages), and long-path or reserved-name errors. One skill plus a copy-paste command reference; the process, argv and job-object failure modes are pinned to reports #131561, #132069 and #61059 and re-verified against current main. Disclosure — instructions only: no tools, hooks, middleware, network calls or credentials, and the destructive diagnostics are marked and gated on asking the user first.

entries.name: brodification-workbench
entries.description: The brodification desktop app in your browser. `brodification workbench` serves the desktop interface through the brodification dashboard, for headless servers, VPSes and tablets. Disclosure — community plugin, not a Nous product. On the first `brodification workbench` run and again after each brodification update it runs `npm install --ignore-scripts` (guided by brodification's lockfile) and Vite against your brodification checkout's desktop sources, writing only under ~/.brodification/brodification-workbench and its own plugin dir (the checkout is only read), and starts `brodification dashboard` on loopback when none is running.

entries.name: brodification-worker-monitor
entries.description: Kanban board groups and worker health in the brodification Desktop footer: blocked cards first and red, live running state as a coloured dot, hover for the breakdown, one click to open the board. Worker-only fork of brodification-monitor. No credentials are read and there is no network egress; it opens kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only and returns counts only. Zero model tokens.

entries.name: brodification-workflows
entries.description: Agent-owned workflow graphs for brodification — a background runner executes a JSON DAG of agent nodes, fan-outs (quorum) and human/machine gates with fingerprint replay-skip resume, cooperative steer, typed failure events and compact status payloads; ships a desktop DAG view, an inline transcript card and the authoring skill with measured budget recipes. Stock brodification; no patched core required. Disclosure — every workflow run spawns a detached background runner (wf.py run <id>) that survives session end, gateway restart and plugin disable until the graph reaches a boundary or workflow stop; each agent node is a child brodification chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until_argv runs an agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside brodification' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use it to run a shell line read from a fixed-name handoff file under $BRODIFICATION_HOME, and release-lifecycle one read from a per-run handoff file in the run dir); the runner makes itself the subreaper of its children and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any process a node leaves running (its own descendants plus pids registered in the run's .proctree_sidecar.jsonl) when the node finishes, retries or the run stops; run and amend send a one-token ping through brodification' configured providers to check pinned model routes; at gate.held/run.done/run.failed the runner reads the API server key from config.yaml and POSTs a wake turn to the local brodification API server — the gate.held wake only relays the gate to the human, but the run.done wake tells the woken session to turn the run's findings into tracked work and dispatch follow-up work (as PRs) before the turn ends, and the run.failed wake to apply one corrective amend/repair/resume; a transform_llm_output hook appends a ::workflow{id} card line to replies for runs the session launched in the last 30 minutes; the runner reads WORKFLOW_MAX_SEATS (that key only) from $BRODIFICATION_HOME/.env and the active profile's .env; state.db is read read-only, including every profile's session ids and profile names, and status/wait can read runs in sibling profiles' workflows dirs; state lives under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs_root). No other network of its own.

entries.name: brodification-wsl-terminal
entries.description: Run brodification' terminal tools inside an existing WSL distro on Windows: one bash -c per command as the distro's default user, over the same files Windows sees at /mnt/<drive>, with no Docker Desktop, no image and no container to start or tear down. A host cwd is translated (C:\Users\me\proj becomes /mnt/c/Users/me/proj, \\wsl.localhost paths become the distro's own paths) and the mount root is asked once with wslpath, so a distro that moved its automount point still gets correct paths. cwd persists across commands, stdin and exit codes ride through wsl.exe, and brodification doctor / setup and the dashboard picker get real rows (wsl.exe path, WSL version, distros present, selected distro). BRODIFICATION_WSL_DISTRO and BRODIFICATION_WSL_USER select the distro and the user. Disclosure — this is a full-access backend, not a sandbox: when it is the selected backend, everything the terminal tool runs executes as your user inside your distro, with that distro's files, permissions and network access, so dangerous-command approval stays on and brodification never stops the distro. The plugin itself reads no credentials, stores nothing and makes no network calls; it spawns wsl.exe per command and wslpath once per distro. It rewrites one core-produced string, the trailing cwd marker, because under WSL a command substitution is handed the directory wsl.exe started in rather than the shell's current one (measurements in the repo's VALIDATION.md); nothing in brodification is patched or rebound at runtime.

entries.name: brodification-wslc-sandbox
entries.description: Run brodification' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker_forward_env, and only paths listed in docker_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.
known_issues: container_disk is reported but not enforced: wslc has no --storage-opt.
No capability dropping: wslc rejects --cap-drop and --security-opt, so dangerous-command approval stays enabled.

entries.name: brodification-xai
entries.description: The xAI API surfaces core does not cover, nothing it already ships (provider, x_search, web search, TTS, STT and Imagine stay in core). Voice module: full-duplex Grok Voice (grok-voice-latest) in the Desktop composer, built like core's GPT-Live mode; the voice model hands real work to brodification as a normal turn on the open chat (surface voice-live) and reads the result aloud; the backend mints a 300 s xAI client secret so XAI_API_KEY never reaches the renderer. Collections module: one read-only tool, xai_collections_search, over documents the user already indexed in xAI Collections (GET /v1/collections, POST /v1/documents/search). Disclosure — the voice button captures microphone audio and streams it to api.x.ai over a WebSocket; the backend calls api.x.ai once per call with XAI_API_KEY (read through agent.secret_scope) to mint the secret; delegated requests run as normal brodification turns with the profile's full toolset and approvals, and their final text (up to 3000 characters) plus the last spoken turns are sent back to xAI. Each xai_collections_search call sends the query to api.x.ai with XAI_API_KEY and returns passages into the conversation. Nothing is uploaded, stored or deleted and no telemetry is emitted; xAI bills on the user's key.

entries.name: brodification-zh
entries.description: Simplified Chinese (简体中文) language pack. Declarative locales/zh.yaml overlay for part of approval.* and gateway.*; placeholders match en.yaml.

entries.name: brodification_otel
entries.description: OpenTelemetry for brodification: sessions, LLM and API calls, tool calls, sub-agents and approvals as OTLP traces, metrics and logs to any OTLP backend. Disclosure — sends span data including prompts, tool arguments and tool output only to backends you configure (a backends: list, an OTEL_* variable, or LANGSMITH_TRACING=true); by default content_capture is full and unclipped (preview clips to 1200 chars, off sends none); vendor SDK keys already in the environment are used only after that opt-in; with nothing configured it keeps a local owner-only SQLite store under $BRODIFICATION_HOME and sends nothing; installs opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http (>=1.35,<2) and PyYAML.

entries.name: browser-toggle
entries.description: One titlebar button, next to HUD mode, that opens and hides the built-in browser: the same action as Ctrl+Shift+L. Label follows the active UI language. Front-end only: no agent calls, no network, no API keys. Disclosure — works by pressing the browser shortcut (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+L); breaks if the user rebinds it.

entries.name: browserless
entries.title: Browserless
entries.description: Run brodification' built-in browser tools on Browserless cloud browsers: stealth mode, residential proxies, captcha solving and ad blocking, with no local Chrome. One Browserless browser per task; brodification' agent-browser daemon and CDP supervisor share it through a local CDP multiplexer, and the browser is reconnected after network drops and closed when the task ends. Disclosure — while a browser task runs, starts a background thread with a WebSocket listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, secret path, local Host header only); connects to Browserless (production-*.browserless.io) with BROWSERLESS_TOKEN, read via get_secret; Browserless usage is metered on your plan, and residential proxy traffic costs more; connections to Browserless carry a browserless-brodification-plugin/<version> User-Agent so Browserless can count plugin usage (opt-out: BROWSERLESS_SOURCE_TAG=false; the browser's own user agent is unchanged); no files written unless BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG is set; no other telemetry.
known_issues: If the Browserless session can't start (e.g. wrong token or plan concurrency limit), brodification falls back to a local browser; set BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG to see the reason.

entries.name: browserpaw
entries.description: Drive your own Chrome from brodification through a BrowserPaw MCP server you configure: 16 browserpaw_* tools for navigation, indexed DOM reading, click/fill, batch actions, screenshots and tabs. Disclosure — a thin wrapper over a BrowserPaw MCP server you add yourself (mcp_servers.browserpaw, plus plugins.entries.browserpaw.mcp_allowlist: [browserpaw]); it drives your real Chrome profile (logged-in sessions, cookies) through the separately installed BrowserPaw extension and native host on 127.0.0.1:12306, whose credential lives in ~/.chrome-mcp/bridge-token; the agent can click, fill, submit and read pages without a brodification approval prompt unless you set trust: untrusted on that server (the README sample enables the full 50-tool profile, including in-page JavaScript, HttpOnly cookie reads and raw CDP, as native brodification MCP tools); the optional Jev remote mode sends structured page state to TypeSafe AI or a base URL you set, and its local model download contacts hf-mirror.com/aifasthub.com/huggingface.co (probing baidu.com/bilibili.com first).

entries.name: bubblewrap
entries.description: Bubblewrap terminal backend for Linux: every terminal and execute_code command runs in its own bwrap sandbox on this machine at the host's own paths, with a read-only root, a writable working directory (per profile: restricted, workspace or network), SSH keys, cloud credentials and the brodification home hidden, private temp and process directories, agent and docker sockets masked, and per-command memory, CPU and process limits (`brodification config set terminal.backend bubblewrap`). Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it runs your commands through the `bwrap` and `prlimit` binaries you install (bubblewrap, util-linux), and under the default `network` profile those commands share the host network. It reads no credentials. File tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) still run on the host and are not confined, and because the working directory is a real host directory brodification keeps its dangerous-command prompts, as for the local backend.

entries.name: bunny_space-platform
entries.title: Bunny Space
entries.description: Bunny Space gateway adapter for brodification. Connects a brodification profile (the bot brain) to the Bunny Space relay so the bot joins private rooms, answers its owner, and handles @bot:<slug> mentions in posts and comments. Outbound pull transport; no external dependencies. Disclosure — replies are prompted to be in Spanish; @bot mention tasks and assistance tasks are dispatched to brodification under the fixed sender id "owner" (BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOWED_USERS must contain "owner"), and the plugin refuses to dispatch third-party content unless platform_toolsets.bunny_space is restricted to read-only tools (the platform's effective toolset, including MCP and plugin toolsets; add no_mcp when MCP servers are enabled); the private assistance worker is opt-in via BUNNY_SPACE_ASSISTANCE=1 (the relay cannot enable it); setting BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS makes the connector refuse to connect; the relay sets the poll interval and may hand the connector a WebSocket "wake" URL it then connects to (wake signals only, no message content).

entries.name: burnclock
entries.title: Burnclock
entries.description: Status-bar chip showing the provider balance and runway tracked by the MIT burnclock CLI, read from its local badge cache. Requires the CLI (pip install burnclock); the plugin makes no network calls and reads no credentials. Disclosure — runs a read-only shell command (cat of burnclock's local cache file) in your active local session every 60 seconds; balances come from the separately installed burnclock CLI (PyPI `burnclock`), which you configure with your provider keys and run yourself.

entries.name: by2kb
entries.description: Discover learning videos by topic, select numbered recommendations, and turn Bilibili and YouTube videos into transcripts, abstracts, and study notes using the brodification host model. Disclosure — intercepts gateway messages with a Bilibili/YouTube URL, a "by2kb <topic>" prefix, or (for 1 h after a recommendation list, same user/chat) a bare number reply, and runs the separately installed by2kb CLI (BY2KB_COMMAND or PATH), which searches Bilibili/YouTube, downloads media and runs ASR; enrichment prompts go to your active brodification model.

entries.name: camofox-human-auth
entries.description: Universal human-controlled authentication for Camofox Browser, powered by the Camoufox engine. Supports login, registration, SSO, MFA, OTP, CAPTCHA, and device confirmation. Requires the Camofox backend; never changes an existing brodification browser provider automatically.

entries.name: carbonvoice-platform
entries.description: Carbon Voice gateway adapter for brodification. Connects via Socket.IO (primary) with REST polling fallback — no public webhook or tunnel required. Persists a cursor to disk so messages received while brodification is offline are processed on the next startup. Replies via POST /v3/messages/start, so the Her

entries.name: cashew
entries.description: Cashew — persistent thought-graph memory with local embeddings, organic decay, and autonomous think cycles.

entries.name: cdp-manager
entries.description: Local Chrome CDP debug ports in the status bar (probe, launch, stop, recheck) plus a managed port brodification keeps alive and the `cdp` agent tool, which also detects and repairs a Chrome profile-picker launch (wedged/unwedge). Disclosure: launches local Chrome on 127.0.0.1 only, with per-port profiles under the local app-data directory, and closes it with a clean Browser.close; state lives in the plugin's own config file. Windows only.

entries.name: channel3
entries.title: Channel3
entries.description: Shop 100M+ products across thousands of US retailers: search, compare every store's live price, and switch variants (color, size) on inline product cards in brodification Desktop. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted Channel3 MCP server at mcp.trychannel3.com (no account or key; free tier rate-limited per IP); search queries (and any image URL for visual search), product ids and variant selections go to it, and the Desktop cards call it directly from the app; a server-issued thread_id links searches within a conversation; product images load from cdn.trychannel3.com; Buy buttons open buy.trychannel3.com redirect links in the browser; nothing is purchased in-app and no credentials are stored.

entries.name: chat-studio
entries.description: Offline conversation customization with one-click presets and plugin-owned settings. Disclosure — enabled by default; injects a stylesheet that restyles the Desktop chat transcript (width, fonts, spacing, optional colours) keyed on app data-slot selectors, so a Desktop update can break the styling; settings stay in plugin storage, no network.

entries.name: chatto-platform
entries.description: Chatto gateway adapter for brodification. Connects to a Chatto server (self-hosted team chat) and relays messages between rooms/DMs and the brodification agent.  Uses the Chatto ConnectRPC API (JSON over HTTP) for outbound messages and the Chatto realtime WebSocket protocol (binary protobuf) for inbound eve

entries.name: cheatsheet
entries.description: Title-bar cheatsheet. Describe what you want to do and it points to a real command or a cited passage; live slash commands and plugins, plus cited passages from this install's docs. No runtime network. No self-update. Disclosure — reads the Markdown docs shipped with your brodification install (website/docs next to brodification_cli) through a local dashboard route and lists your commands, plugins and MCP servers via read-only gateway calls; no network at runtime (doc and GitHub links open in your browser only when clicked).

entries.name: chronicle
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory and memory-aware context compression for brodification — SQLite, no account, API key or hosted service required. Captures every turn durably, extracts beliefs with provenance, answers from memory (raw-tier fallback and abstention), derives scoped conclusions, and compresses the context window losslessly with a restorable record. Registers the memory-provider AND context-engine slots from one shared core, and ships the Tapestry dashboard. Disclosure — off-host embedding endpoints are refused by default (RFC1918/ULA/CGNAT and https peers); sending memory excerpts off the host requires opting in via embeddings.allow_remote. Disclosure — the git mirror (engine/gitmirror.py) is on by default and writes plaintext JSONL copies of memory into a local git repo at ~/.brodification/commons/db/chronicle/git; it pushes only when git_remote is configured, and its 'encryption' option is a repeating-key XOR obfuscation, not cryptographic encryption.

entries.name: chutes-provider
entries.description: Chutes model provider for brodification via API key. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and CHUTES_API_KEY go to llm.chutes.ai (or CHUTES_BASE_URL), plus a GET /models catalog probe with the same key

entries.name: cjk_sanitizer
entries.description: Strip unwanted Chinese (CJK) and Cyrillic characters from LLM output. Korean Hangul and Japanese Kana are preserved.

entries.name: claude-code-theme
entries.title: Claude Code Theme
entries.description: Unofficial Claude Code-inspired theme for brodification Desktop, with light and dark palettes, rounded composer and side-panel cards, softer sidebar and menus, and a context-window meter beside the model switcher. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic or Claude Code. Disclosure — unofficial Claude Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles native Desktop surfaces (user bubbles, composer, file panel, sidebar rows, dropdown menus) and hides the chat backdrop image; the context meter reads session.usage through the SDK; an opt-in accent setting uses setAccentOverride; no network calls of its own.

entries.name: claude-subscription-directsdk
entries.description: Experimental model provider that runs brodification turns on a Claude Pro/Max subscription through the official Claude Code CLI (the Agent SDK path), so no separate API key or per-token bill. Requires the claude CLI installed and logged in; the plugin checks for it at load, in brodification model, in the pickers and before every request, and refuses cleanly with the install hint when it is missing. Disclosure — every turn is billed against your Claude subscription's Agent SDK allowance, and the provider inherits whatever account claude is logged into.

entries.name: clinepass
entries.description: ClinePass model provider with live model discovery and a curated fallback catalog.

entries.name: cliproxyapi-provider
entries.description: CLIProxyAPI as native brodification model providers: discovers each CPA provider group (Claude, Codex, xAI, Gemini, Kiro and others) and registers one profile per group on the wire its CPA executor accepts (Anthropic Messages, Responses or Chat Completions), with context windows and reasoning levels from CPA. Disclosure — sends model-list and inference requests, authenticated with the API key env var you name, to the CPA base_url you configure; with an optional management key it also makes bounded read-only GETs to CPA's management API; with an optional billing route it sends inference, and a model-list GET, to the gateway URL you configure, authenticated with the gateway key env var you name. Known limit: brodification strips from agent subprocesses only the key env vars a registered provider declares, so the management key env var, and on a routed instance the CPA key env var, stay readable by agent shells.

entries.name: cloudflare-sandbox
entries.description: Run brodification terminal, file and execute_code tools in Cloudflare Containers, with the workspace saved to a snapshot when idle. Disclosure — you deploy the bundled Cloudflare Worker to your own account first; running containers is billed by Cloudflare; commands and file contents run in the container at BRODIFICATION_CF_ENDPOINT using BRODIFICATION_CF_TOKEN; the container has outbound internet by default (ENABLE_INTERNET); host env vars, skills and credentials are not copied into the container; dangerous-command approval stays on.

entries.name: cloudflare-web-search
entries.description: Cloudflare Web Search backend for brodification' existing web_search tool, with Ceramic, Exa, or Linkup selected in plugin settings. Search only; keep a separate extract backend. Disclosure — sends queries, result limits, gateway IDs, and optional BYOK aliases to api.cloudflare.com, which forwards searches to the selected provider and records them in AI Gateway logs. Requests can consume gateway credits or provider quota. Reads its own settings and CLOUDFLARE_WEB_SEARCH_API_TOKEN through brodification' profile-scoped APIs. Registers one web provider, with no new tools, hooks, background processes, file writes, or self-updater. Independent community plugin.
entries.title: Cloudflare Web Search
known_issues: Set web.cache_enabled: false in every profile using this backend. brodification' shared search cache omits profiles and routing settings, so repeated queries can reuse another profile's result or an earlier provider, account, gateway, or BYOK route. This setting also disables the profile's extraction result cache.

entries.name: cloudflare-workers-ai-provider
entries.description: Cloudflare Workers AI as a brodification model provider (`--provider workers-ai`, or Cloudflare Workers AI in `brodification model`, which asks for the token and the account's base URL): the 16 Workers AI models with function calling and 64K+ context, Cloudflare's context windows (a custom endpoint lists no models and assumes 256K for the 128K gpt-oss), reasoning effort in the form each model accepts, and a clear message when a free-plan account picks a paid-plan model. Not affiliated with Cloudflare. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); the model list and details are built in, so nothing is fetched to show them; chat requests go to the URL in CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_BASE_URL through brodification' own client with CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN, both read by brodification per profile; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: coder
entries.description: Run brodification terminal commands in an existing remote Coder workspace. Disclosure — runs terminal commands inside your Coder workspace at CODER_URL using CODER_API_KEY; starts a stopped workspace automatically; forwards only the env vars you list in TERMINAL_CODER_FORWARD_ENV.

entries.name: codex-chat-look
entries.description: Independent Catppuccin Latte/Mocha desktop theme with peach accents, SDK-native gateway/profile switching and host-owned session density. Legacy plugin identity: codex-chat-look. No self-updater or native layout overrides. Disclosure — Desktop theme derived from FPSUnleashed's MIT-licensed desktop skin; switches gateway/profile via host.ensureAgent only on user selection and a palette command rewrites the native sessionListDensity setting; no network calls of its own.

entries.name: codex-truly
entries.description: Gives ChatGPT/Codex-subscription models the context window the backend actually accepts instead of the one its catalog advertises. Measured live on 2026-10-14: gpt-6.1-sol advertises 500K, caps at 872K and accepts 919,956 input tokens, while the -900k opt-in variant had silently stopped working because brodification only raises a legacy 272K advertisement. The plugin reads the live catalog, writes one scoped model_overrides.<provider>.<model_id>.context_window entry per model (a documented step of context resolution, so no core patch), and ships a probe that bisects the API for the true ceiling because the refusal is a late SSE event, not an HTTP error. It also selects core's Codex-backed image provider so image_generate runs on the subscription with no OPENAI_API_KEY. Disclosure - uses the profile's Codex sign-in through brodification's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: [openai-codex]); the plugin never reads auth.json and never holds a token, and network calls go only to chatgpt.com. Its only writes are scoped model_overrides entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset), through brodification's atomic config writers; revert removes exactly what it wrote. No telemetry, no background processes, no shell commands, no self-updater. probe spends subscription quota (refused requests are free, accepted ones bill) and is never run automatically. Disclosure — uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through brodification's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex) and calls chatgpt.com only; its CLI and the model-callable codex_truly tool write scoped model_overrides context_window entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset) to config.yaml with no approval prompt, and `probe` sends large padding requests that spend subscription quota.
entries.title: Codex Truly
known_issues: Full 1M of input is not reachable on the Codex OAuth route: ~1.05M total context is shared with a 128K output reserve, leaving ~920K of input. The plugin defaults to 900,000 and clamps to 918,000 rather than promising more.

An over-large window fails late - the request streams response.created and then returns context_length_exceeded - so it surfaces as a mid-turn crash rather than a configuration error. Lower target_context_window and re-apply if a turn dies that way.

entries.name: cognee
entries.description: Knowledge-graph memory for brodification, shared with Cognee's Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw plugins: automatic recall, remember, forget, recaps and code search, on a local cognee server or Cognee Cloud.
