Disclosure — runs a local cognee server (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8011) and a session-close watcher in the background; each turn plus its tool calls and results (redacted, capped) go to that server and on to your configured LLM provider (OpenAI by default), or to Cognee Cloud / COGNEE_BASE_URL in remote mode; turns the server could not take are queued in ~/.cognee-plugin; the store lives in ~/.cognee, outside BRODIFICATION_HOME and shared across profiles and with Cognee's Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw plugins; cognee sends anonymous telemetry unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1.

entries.name: cognition
entries.description: Cognition session-end memory — facts regex-extracted from your messages at session end, stored in a local SQLite queue and JSON log under one repo label, with fetch-first merge, per-entry provenance, and budgeted prefetch (tools: cognition_search, cognition_status, read-only cognition_dream). Disclosure — saves verbatim excerpts (up to 400 chars) of your own messages that match preference/decision phrases in plain local files under BRODIFICATION_HOME/cognition/ (SQLite queue, JSON commit log) and re-injects them into later prompts sent to your model provider; the author name is read from ~/.gitconfig; the plugin makes no network calls of its own.

entries.name: colorado-traffic
entries.description: Live Colorado highway events from CDOT COtrip. No API key. Default corridor is I-70 Golden to east Denver. Separates incidents happening now from scheduled work and unverified Waze reports.

entries.name: command-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the slash commands you run in brodification (built-in commands in the CLI, built-in and plugin commands on messaging platforms): /command-log shows how often each command was used, its share, in how many sessions and when last, per command, platform, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /command-log recent lists the newest commands (ten, or up to 100 with /command-log recent 50) with the alias typed. Disclosure — writes command metadata (command name, alias typed, surface, platform, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no arguments, session key or user id) to plugin-data/command-ledger/commands.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot block or change a command; no network

entries.name: command-tray
entries.description: Session command tray — shell commands the brodification agent ran via the terminal tool (success and failure). Desktop pane and /commands. No API keys. Disclosure — records terminal commands with exit code, workdir and a 160-char redacted output preview to $BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/command-tray/state.json; the Desktop pane inserts text through brodification Desktop's internal brodification:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API) with clipboard fallback; no network.

entries.name: commandcode-oauth
entries.description: Command Code CLI-key model provider with a live OAuth catalog property bridge, plan limits and failover classification. Disclosure — uses the CLI-internal api.commandcode.ai/alpha/generate endpoint and CLI client headers, sends the full conversation, tool schemas, cwd path and OS/Python version, and imports a static key from the read-only CLI credential file or a browser hand-off; no OAuth exchange takes place. brodification also bundles commandcode for the documented Provider API.
known_issues: Older cores may incorrectly warn about this provider's vendor/model IDs in brodification doctor; generic profile namespace support is proposed in upstream PR 134900.

entries.name: comment-scraper
entries.title: Comment Scraper
entries.description: Ask about the Reddit and Hacker News threads you exported with the Comment Scraper browser extension: list, read, search and quote them by comment number. Disclosure — starts a local stdio MCP server with npx -y comment-scraper-mcp@0.1.0, which npx downloads from npm on first run; the server only reads JSON exports in ~/Downloads and the folders directly inside it, never writes files, makes no network requests, stores no credentials and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: compartment
entries.description: Encrypted, fully offline memory provider. AEAD-encrypted local vault (vectors included), bundled embedding model, exact hybrid search, no API key and no network at runtime. One vault shared with Claude, Cursor and any other MCP client on the machine. Disclosure — installs the full compartment engine (about 27 Python packages including onnxruntime, tokenizers, mcp and system-tray dependencies) into the brodification venv; the provider's system prompt instructs the model to store passwords and API keys in the encrypted vault.

entries.name: completion-sound
entries.title: Completion Sound
entries.description: Pick the sound brodification Desktop plays when a turn finishes: one of the 14 built-in presets or your own audio file (mp3, wav, ogg), with an optional different sound during night hours. Files stay in the plugin's local storage. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.
known_issues: brodification' own completion sound still plays alongside the plugin's until brodification adds a way to turn it off (PR #140350).

entries.name: composer-modes
entries.description: Cursor-style composer modes (ask / agent / plan / debug) for the brodification desktop — the mode's operating note reaches the model inside the turn's model-facing bytes, never the bubble, transcript or session titles, and ask mode is enforced read-only on the tool side.

entries.name: context-audit
entries.description: Context-window forensics: per-turn input/output token estimates, the single largest tool output of each turn, oversized tool calls (args over 50 KB), and compaction events, recorded as metadata only (tool name, byte length, ids, timestamps — never args or results) in a local SQLite DB under BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/context-audit/. Adds a /context-audit slash command that prints the top 5 context eaters over a window with one mitigation per entry.

entries.name: corpus
entries.description: Hosted Corpus MCP (Streamable HTTP at corpuslaw.us/api/mcp) plus two bundled skills: US law search/get_node/list_coverage over 571k+ provisions, and LLC/nonprofit formation intake (requirements, compare, NAICS lookup, handoff, USDC checkout, payment_status), with account.status for quota. Filing always stays human-gated and USDC pay is email-confirmed. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); no API key needed for anonymous research. The formation skill requires fixed vendor-authored marketing copy in the first reply and before payment, and sends founder PII (name, email, phone, address) to Corpus through links and MCP tools. Intake instructions are vendored; checkout requires exact-amount confirmation from the user in the current turn.

entries.name: cortexlayer
entries.description: CortexLayer memory provider — page-linked long-term memory with link-expansion retrieval, wired into brodification' automatic per-turn recall (prefetch) and persistence (sync_turn), plus a pre-compress checkpoint so evidence brodification' own context compaction would otherwise drop is saved first. Platform mode only: each turn's query and conversational content is sent to the hosted api.cortexlayer.net (HTTPS, API-key authenticated) for storage/retrieval — no local/offline mode. Requires a free CortexLayer account and API key.

entries.name: covision
entries.description: Read-only Covision meeting, assigned-task, and published-knowledge tools through the Covision Streamable HTTP MCP service, plus a workflow skill. Requires a Covision account, organization connector enablement, and browser OAuth consent; no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin.

entries.name: crawl4ai
entries.description: Crawl4ai self-hosted web content extraction. Requires CRAWL4AI_URL and CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN pointing at your instance.

entries.name: crew
entries.description: One /crew message becomes verified work on the kanban board. A coordinator owns every card until its proof command exits 0 - one writer per card, an independent verifier, a hard token budget per card, and a live local dashboard of every card, run and tool call. Disclosure — install.py creates four crew-* profiles cloned from your chat profile (including its .env provider keys and memories), deletes non-crew skills in them, updates crew in other profiles and on Linux starts a loopback dashboard service (127.0.0.1:8799, transcript excerpts; --publish serves it to one tailnet login), restarting it when an upgrade changes the plugin code; on native Windows the service and the optional nightly cron are skipped and the dashboard is started by hand, and proofs run in Git for Windows's bash; a Crew tab in the brodification dashboard and a Crew page in brodification Desktop build that board inside the brodification backend, including its transcript excerpts, each live card's step count and last tool name, and its acknowledge action, under /api/plugins/crew/ to anyone with dashboard access; a detached coordinator makes read-only model decisions and runs card proof commands unattended with a scrubbed env, flagged or changed proofs only after the owner answers /crew-proof; card reports and questions are sent to the originating chat via brodification send; agent-written per-role lessons are injected into later crew turns.

entries.name: cron-bulletin
entries.description: Central brodification Desktop inbox for reports produced by local cron runs.

entries.name: crypto-prices
entries.description: Live crypto price ticker for the desktop status bar — Top 10 by market cap, seamless marquee, custom coins & 60+ display currencies, adjustable width (CoinGecko, no API key).

entries.name: cua-spaces
entries.description: Cua's own plugin: runs brodification's terminal, file and code tools inside a Cua Space, an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine you can watch live, as a terminal backend (`brodification config set terminal.backend cua`). On brodification 0.22.3 and later, Bot Desktop, computer_use and the browser follow the terminal into the Space too (needs the `cua` command). Disclosure — installs the `cua` Python SDK (>=0.5.0,<0.8); every command the agent runs, every file it touches, and (on 0.22.3+) every screen, click and page the agent drives go to the Space: on this machine for a local Space, or on Cua's cloud (cua.ai) or a machine you name, using the sign-in `cua auth login` saved (the plugin never reads or stores a token, and keeps CUA_API_KEY/CUA_DAEMON_TOKEN out of the Space). Windows Spaces run brodification's tools in Git Bash, like brodification on a Windows PC: if the Space lacks Git for Windows or Python, the plugin installs them inside the Space (pinned official installers checked against SHA-256, `winget` fallback) and adds `C:\c`-style drive aliases there. The optional `desktop` setting installs a desktop stack (VNC, Chromium, agent-browser, cua-driver) inside a Linux Space with sudo there. Nothing is installed on this machine. With the default `space: create` it makes a fresh Space per session and deletes it when brodification finishes (`delete_on_exit`); because that Space is a disposable sandbox, brodification skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends. A Space you name is never deleted and keeps the prompts.
entries.title: Cua Spaces

entries.name: cursor-acp
entries.description: Use your Cursor subscription models (Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Composer 2.5, GPT-5.6, Grok) inside brodification via the Cursor CLI's ACP server (`agent acp`). Install with one command (`npx brodification-cursor-acp`) or `brodification plugins install cursor-acp`. The plugin rewrites `.cursor/cli.json` in an empty private workspace every run with a deny-all list (`Read`, `Write`, `Shell`, `WebFetch`, `Mcp`) to prevent Cursor's native CLI tools from accessing host files. It includes a custom extractor that recovers both flat `{"name", "arguments"}` and inline `<tool_call>` blocks that standard regex bridges drop, retries on concurrent `set_model` calls, and reports `usage=None` so brodification proactive context compression functions correctly. Disclosure — sends the full conversation, brodification tool schemas and tool results to Cursor through your locally installed, signed-in Cursor CLI (`agent acp`); Cursor's own tools are fenced by a deny-all `.cursor/cli.json` that the plugin rewrites in a private workspace under `$BRODIFICATION_HOME/cache/cursor-acp-workspace` on every start (a differing existing file is backed up to `cli.json.bak`), and brodification executes every tool call under its own approvals.

entries.name: cursor-provider
entries.description: Cursor model provider using the official proprietary Cursor SDK. Disclosure — uses Cursor's proprietary cursor-sdk (PyPI, bundled binary bridge on loopback) with the user's CURSOR_API_KEY; sends the full conversation, tool schemas/results and images (HTTPS URLs or base64) to Cursor; keeps private per-session SDK workspaces under BRODIFICATION_HOME/cache/cursor-sdk; Cursor built-in tools and MCP are requested off and brodification keeps tool execution and approvals.

entries.name: cursor-sdk
entries.description: Experimental model transport using the official Cursor Agent SDK. Requests go to Cursor through its official SDK. The plugin cannot enforce an included-only spending cap and never changes account spending settings. Instructions use a Cursor project rule, not a native system-role override. Permission and prompt-hierarchy equivalence remain unqualified. The plugin spawns Node and a local SDK agent, runs Git initialization in a plugin-owned workspace, and writes project rules, hooks, and SDK state under its own runtime directory. That state may contain private conversation data and currently remains on disk. Credentials come from brodification's profile-scoped secret accessor. No credential store or vendor token file is read directly by plugin code. Text-only, buffered responses. The bundled model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery. Optional picker hooks require brodification support. This plugin does not patch the desktop. Disclosure — spawns Node and a local Cursor Agent SDK worker per request (`npm ci` in the plugin dir installs Cursor's official native platform binaries from npm); sends the full conversation, system prompt and tool schemas to Cursor with your CURSOR_API_KEY; Cursor-native shell/file tools are denied by a fail-closed project hook and the run is cancelled if one fires, but that enforcement is not proven in every Cursor runtime; each request's workspace and conversation state stay under the plugin's runtime/ directory until you delete them.
known_issues: Experimental: included subscription billing and live permission equivalence are not verified.
Node 22.13 or later and Git are required. Install the pinned npm dependencies in the plugin directory.
Text-only, buffered responses. Model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery.
SDK workspaces and conversation state remain under the installed plugin's runtime directory.
Uses 3 private brodification helper imports, disclosed in the README and entry PR.

entries.name: custodian
entries.description: Autonomous operations monitor for a brodification install: scans gateway logs, cron jobs, skill journals and agent data directories, classifies findings against a 27-fingerprint registry, auto-repairs Tier 1 problems, escalates the rest, and keeps an append-only issue ledger. Ships /custodian (status, scan, issues, repair, verify, schedule, confidence, init, escalation-runner), four scan/health tools and a grid dashboard. Disclosure — reads gateway logs, cron job state and per-skill journal files under BRODIFICATION_HOME to build its findings, and writes repair actions and an issues ledger back there; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — /custodian init registers 3 recurring agent cron jobs (deep scan 4×/day, cron-health 4×/day, escalation runner every 30 min on weekdays).

entries.name: custom-dangerous-patterns
entries.description: Add custom dangerous command patterns to brodification's built-in approval system. Users define regex patterns in YAML; a pre_tool_call hook sends block patterns to brodification's human approval gate and blocks deny patterns immediately. Modifies no brodification internals.

entries.name: darkmoon
entries.description: Triage the findings file of a Darkmoon autonomous pentest scan (JSON or SARIF): filter by severity and proof status, get a severity-sorted summary and a pass/fail gate for a release. Read-only and offline: no network, no subprocess, no credentials, standard library only. Darkmoon is open source (GPL-3.0); its web dashboard and remediation agent are Pro and are not used here. Disclosure — reads a local .json or .sarif file at a model-supplied path (10 MB cap) and returns its findings; no network, subprocess or writes

entries.name: dashboard-auth-feishu
entries.description: Feishu / Lark OAuth sign-in for the web dashboard, admitted by tenant + open_id allow-list. Registers the `feishu` dashboard auth provider once plugins.entries.dashboard-auth-feishu.settings (app_id, tenant_key, owner_open_ids) and an app secret are configured. Disclosure — calls only the fixed Feishu or Lark authorize, token and user_info endpoints; reads BRODIFICATION_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_APP_SECRET or, as a fallback, the Feishu gateway's FEISHU_APP_SECRET, plus BRODIFICATION_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_SESSION_KEY; stores tenant, open_id and display name per sign-in in a 0600 SQLite file under plugin-data (no upstream tokens); a refused sign-in logs the tenant_key and open_id Feishu returned (identifiers only, for first-time setup); every admitted identity gets full dashboard access; upstream PKCE is not used (confidential client with single-use cookie-bound state); pending logins are in memory, so one dashboard worker only; WebSockets opened before logout may stay open until the session key is rotated and the dashboard restarted.
entries.title: Feishu / Lark Dashboard Login
known_issues: Lark endpoints are implemented but not live-tested; Feishu is tested end to end.

entries.name: dashboard-auth-ldap
entries.description: LDAP / Active Directory password login for the web dashboard. Verifies credentials with an LDAP bind (direct or search-then-bind), never stores passwords, requires ldaps:// or StartTLS, and supports group restriction. Registers the `ldap` dashboard auth provider once dashboard.ldap_auth is configured. Disclosure — dashboard logins are verified by binding to your configured LDAP/AD server with the user's password (TLS with certificate validation required unless allow_insecure is set); sessions are stateless HMAC tokens (12h access / 30d refresh by default) signed with BRODIFICATION_DASHBOARD_LDAP_SECRET or a random per-process key, and logout cannot revoke them; group removal and disabled accounts are not re-checked until the refresh token expires; failed logins count toward the directory's account-lockout policy.

entries.name: dashboard-button
entries.description: One-click access to the brodification Web Dashboard (127.0.0.1:9119) from the Desktop app — sidebar row, in-app page that loads itself when the server comes up, and a status-bar chip with a live dot. Front-end only: no agent calls, no tokens, no API keys.

entries.name: dashscope-image
entries.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) image generation -- Wan 2.7 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) and PAYG (sk-ws-*) keys.

entries.name: dashscope-video
entries.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) video generation -- HappyHorse 1.1 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Async task API. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) keys.

entries.name: davinci-resolve
entries.description: Control DaVinci Resolve Studio live, or generate importable interchange files for free DaVinci Resolve.

entries.name: day-panel
entries.title: Today (day panel)
entries.description: A Today page in brodification Desktop, plus brodification day show and check, built from sections you list in a YAML file: any program that prints JSON (your tracker, a script of yours), your open GitHub pull requests and review requests through gh, one read-only tool of an MCP server you already configured, and your AI providers' limit windows from brodification usage. Items can carry a colour, a progress bar and a relative time; the page follows the Desktop theme. Ships a demo page that needs no login or network. Read-only and no model calls; merging a pull request from the page is off by default and needs a preview and a confirmation pinned to the head commit. Disclosure — runs the programs your sources file names (no shell), plus gh and brodification usage, as your user with your existing logins; calls a configured MCP server's tool only when the server marks it readOnlyHint, in a child process that imports three undocumented brodification MCP modules (there is no public seam for this yet); reads only the sources file; writes nothing to disk; logs carry section names and exit statuses, not source output. No credentials stored, no telemetry.
known_issues: The mcp_tool source imports undocumented brodification MCP internals (discover_mcp_tools, _tool_is_read_only, mcp_prefixed_tool_name); a brodification release can break that one source until the plugin is updated. The other sources do not use them.
Under plugins.isolation: host the brodification day terminal command is not available (brodification skips plugin CLI commands in the host); the Desktop page still works.
The Desktop half ships disabled, like every plugin's: turn it on in Capabilities → Plugins.

entries.name: deadbolt
entries.description: Review and approve exact text-artifact writes through a local DeadBolt sidecar. Protects this plugin's commit tool only.
entries.title: DeadBolt — reviewed artifact writes
known_issues: Requires a separately installed DeadBolt 2.0.0 engine and operator-provisioned local sidecar, run, policy and scoped admission credential.
Only this plugin's artifact commit route is gated; other brodification tools, plugins, MCP routes and already-running work are outside its boundary.
New files only, existing parent directories, 32 KiB request limit and five-minute exact approvals. Admitted filesystem failures require operator reconciliation.

entries.name: debug-desk
entries.description: Today's git digest in the current repo, plus the last failed terminal command the brodification agent ran. Desktop pane, status chip, optional local LLM summary. Does not watch OS or editor terminals.

entries.name: deepgram-voice
entries.description: Deepgram Aura text-to-speech and Nova speech-to-text providers for brodification.

entries.name: deepinfra-sandbox
entries.description: Terminal backend running agent commands in isolated DeepInfra cloud sandboxes (deep_sands microVMs). Disclosure — runs agent commands in billable DeepInfra cloud sandboxes and uploads your brodification skills, cache and skill-registered credential files to the sandbox at /workspace/.brodification; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the sandbox.

entries.name: deepseek-search-fetch
entries.description: DeepSeek Search & Fetch as a backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and web_extract URLs to api.deepseek.com with your DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and DeepSeek fetches the pages server-side; billed to your DeepSeek balance per successful request; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access.
entries.title: DeepSeek Search & Fetch
known_issues: Billed by DeepSeek per successful request (list price $0.75 per 1,000; failed calls are free); web_extract calls Fetch one URL at a time, so multi-URL extracts run sequentially to the effective deadline (min(extract_deadline, web.extract_timeout - 1.5s), with bodies aborted at that deadline) and return the pages already fetched; and ori_question is not forwarded, because brodification hands the provider only the query and a result limit.

entries.name: deepseek-whale
entries.description: Live DeepSeek API peak/off-peak pricing whale for the brodification desktop titlebar. Blue x0.5 off-peak, grey PEAK at full price, countdown on click, 30s repaint, no backend or API key.

entries.name: deferred-questions
entries.description: Durable non-blocking questions with exact answer binding and gateway continuation. Disclosure — its pre_gateway_dispatch hook sees every gateway message and consumes only `dq <id> …` answers from the stored recipient; with `enable_tool` on, the model can send questions to any chat the gateway already authorizes, and a question marked continue_agent resumes that chat's agent with the user's answer; questions and answers are stored unencrypted in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/deferred-questions/questions.sqlite3; it calls private gateway and adapter methods, so a brodification update can break delivery until it is re-pinned.

entries.name: degeneracy-guard
entries.description: Asks the user to confirm a tool call whose arguments look like a repetition loop rather than data, through brodification' approval gate (denied or unanswered means refused); replaces flagged degenerate output with a short notice; warns when a session grows long. Disclosure — no network, shell, subprocesses, own threads, telemetry or credentials; writes incident records and a session counter to its plugin data directory; a stream-side record keeps the last 800 characters of flagged output.

entries.name: deja-memory
entries.description: Memory from the coding sessions already on this machine — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, brodification and the other agents deja reads, including history from before it was installed. No model, no API key, no server. Disclosure — runs the separately installed, unpinned deja binary (brew install deja-vu) as a subprocess; deja reads Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, brodification and other agents' local transcript files, keeps its index under ~/.cache/deja, and recalled text from those agents is injected into brodification turns; nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: desensitize
entries.description: Chinese-context desensitization for brodification chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. Also rewrites inbound user messages and outbound assistant replies, so transcript content differs from what you typed; placeholders are code-generated and may over-match (18-digit ID-card-shaped strings, names that collide with the public-entity allowlist); company names are matched greedily and a modifier such as 原北京某某有限公司 is absorbed into the placeholder; magnitude masking drops the numeric value and only fires on the configured trigger words, so a domain term absent from that list is left unmasked without warning; the placeholder mapping is held in memory only and never written to disk.

entries.name: deskrpg
entries.description: brodification gateway integration for DeskRPG virtual offices, with profiles, kanban, cron, artifacts and NPC skill management. Install it through the DeskRPG setup wizard. Optional (off by default): when enabled by the operator, links the plugin into every profile so kanban workers and cron runs can save artifacts. Disclosure — NPC skill management runs brodification skills/curator commands as background subprocesses per profile and edits that profile's skills, config.yaml and memory files; creating new review-policy kanban cards needs a review-policy API that upstream brodification does not ship (the README points at the author's brodification-agent fork for it), and that feature stays inert on upstream.

entries.name: devin
entries.title: brodification Devin
entries.description: Delegate coding tasks to the Devin CLI, on your computer or in Devin Cloud, with live progress cards and change review in brodification Desktop. Every launch goes through brodification approval; Cloud runs need a separate Cloud-managed-permissions confirmation. Disclosure — spawns the vendor devin CLI from PATH or cli_path (devin acp, devin acp --cloud, devin --print, devin auth status, devin models list); the CLI edits files and runs shell commands in a folder the model picks (any folder unless allowed_roots is set) under the configured permission mode (accept-edits/smart auto-allow edits, dangerous auto-allows everything and needs allow_dangerous: true), and talks to Cognition's servers; Devin Cloud runs use Cognition-managed permissions that brodification does not gate. Every model-initiated launch goes through brodification approval; follow-ups typed on a Desktop run card and answers to Devin's prompts on the card start or allow actions on that click without a brodification prompt (unanswered card prompts are denied after 300 s by default). Uses the existing Devin CLI login and stores no credentials; brodification provider, bot and tool secrets are stripped from the child environment (extra_env is passed as set). Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition.

entries.name: devkit
entries.title: Scratchpad (devkit)
entries.description: One managed home for agent drafts: a per-session scratchpad of named buffers the agent edits in place instead of writing a new temp file per revision. Buffers live under plugin-data/devkit/, open in the Desktop code viewer, are promoted to real files only through write_file, and are removed when their chat is deleted. A Scratchpad tab beside Files groups chats by date like the chat sidebar; click a chat to open it, click a file to view or edit it in a workspace tab, and delete or clear drafts. Disclosure — adds a short placement rule (about 120 tokens) to each turn's user message; reads state.db read-only once an hour from a background thread to find deleted chats, and also removes folders idle longer than idle_days (default 90) using its own stamps; deletes only its own folders under plugin-data/devkit/; no network calls, credentials or third-party services.
known_issues: scratchpad action=open needs the Desktop window bridge on the session gateway (brodify-ai/brodification#138917); on v0.22.1 open reports 'The preview pane is only available in the brodification desktop app'. Every other action works.
The agent may not always pick the scratchpad on its own (the model chooses its tools). If it writes a loose file or pastes code instead, ask it to use the scratchpad.

entries.name: dexio
entries.description: Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. Standard library only; no background threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO_API_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step.

entries.name: diaktoros
entries.description: Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two brodification agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended brodification agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files you provide; edits brodification's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one brodification cron job (its migrate command replaces the old brodification-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose, and restore writes one back into the brodification home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the brodification home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices and an optional weekly report to the chat you name; opt-in shadow reviews spend a second profile's model tokens on reviews that are recorded but never posted; its optional Desktop page and local dashboard API read loop state and can re-arm a failed run as `brodification dk retry` would, and doctor compares the installed commit with the plugin's latest GitHub release (read-only); deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force brodification token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only.

entries.name: diff-review
entries.description: Analyze git diffs for common code quality issues — debug prints, hardcoded secrets, bare except clauses, and unresolved TODOs.

entries.name: digital-marketing-pro
entries.description: Open-source marketing toolkit for agencies and in-house teams, one listing with three skill groups and 207 skills registered as brodification skills: Digital Marketing Pro (strategy, SEO/AEO/GEO, paid media, CRM, analytics; 164 skills), ContentForge (fact-checked long-form content with a run auditor; 22 skills) and SocialForge (a content calendar to images, carousels, video and copy; 21 skills). Skills only: no tools, hooks or background processes. Disclosure — Skills only (no tools, hooks or MCP servers). The optional scripts the skills run call third-party APIs (ad, CRM, e-mail, Slack, LLM and image/video providers) only when run, using the user's own keys from environment variables. Live writes need the user's typed yes. For writes the plugin sends itself, the script creates a single-use approval record when it prepares the write, and the agent approves that record after the yes, so brodification does not prompt before those script runs. Writes through MCP tools rely on the typed yes alone. Paid image and video generation is quoted first. refresh_models.py reads your Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and (strategy group) Evolink keys. Keys and data live outside the brodification profile: SocialForge stores API keys in plain text, plus a copy of any Google service-account file, in ~/socialforge-workspace; brand data goes to ~/.claude-marketing; deliverables are copied to ~/Documents/DigitalMarketingPro and ~/Documents/ContentForge. Nothing installs unless the user says yes; installs are exact-pinned pip packages into the Python that runs the script, plus Playwright's Chromium download. See the README and each group's PRIVACY.md.

entries.name: discord-tps
entries.description: Show live tokens-per-second and the active model on your Discord bot's presence. Disclosure — Replaces the Discord bot's public presence with the live tok/s figure and the model name of the most recent API call in this gateway (any platform or chat), visible to anyone who can see the bot; updates at most every interval seconds (minimum 10) over the gateway's existing Discord connection. Reads no credentials and makes no network calls of its own.

entries.name: doc-markdown
entries.description: Convert one local file to Markdown with doc_convert on Linux and macOS, built on Microsoft's MarkItDown. Microsoft and MarkItDown are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Disclosure — the doc_markdown toolset is on by default on every surface, including a gateway, so anyone you allow there can call doc_convert; stop it with brodification tools. It does not fetch pages. Unattended sessions still convert when brodification calls the tool. This plugin creates no cron job. A child process runs MarkItDown with no brodification keys in its environment; on macOS the plugin runs ps about every 10 ms to watch that child's memory. It stops 8 seconds after its converters load, at 60 seconds if loading never finishes, or above 922746880 bytes. It is not a sandbox: after realpath it may read any allowlisted path it can open. Unpublished brodification code locates the brodification home, and a failed check refuses the path. Removal deletes the plugin directory, not the markitdown package. Windows was not tested.

entries.name: doctorpack
entries.description: Local-first diagnostics, safety audit, and incident postmortems for brodification.

entries.name: document-reader
entries.description: Profile-scoped document OCR for brodification Desktop and HUD, with a guarded per-profile Windows service.

entries.name: done-bell
entries.description: Ring when a brodification turn finishes so you can leave the window. OS notification, optional chime, and a busy/done chip. Optional "needs you" when approval is waiting. No API keys.

entries.name: draft-cards
entries.title: Draft Cards
entries.description: Email and chat-message drafts as reviewable cards in the brodification Desktop chat. The agent's draft_card tool stores each draft and its revisions; the card shows recipients, subject and body, highlights the words each revision changed (removed text on demand), supports inline editing, and offers Copy and Open in Mail. The plugin never sends anything: pressing Send records approval of that exact version and posts it to the chat, then the agent sends it with the user's existing mail or messaging tools and reports the outcome with draft_card_status. Disclosure — stores draft text (recipients, subject, body, versions) in the profile's plugin-data/draft-cards/drafts.db (the 500 most recent drafts are kept); the desktop half appends one scoped stylesheet, removed on disable; no network calls, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.
known_issues: After installing, switch on the Draft Cards desktop half in Capabilities → Plugins, then start a new chat so the agent sees the draft_card tools.

entries.name: drag-to-pin-session
entries.description: Pin or unpin sessions from their row with supported desktop SDK actions.

entries.name: duty-board
entries.title: Duty Board
entries.description: Read-only dashboard tab and model-free /duty and brodification duty summaries for waiting conversations, unanswered messages, running turns, undelivered background results and failing cron jobs. Supports all 17 dashboard languages, including right-to-left Arabic. Disclosure — opens BRODIFICATION_HOME/state.db with SQLite mode=ro (sessions, messages, turn leases, async delegations, goals) and reads cron/jobs.json and gateway_state.json; writes only BRODIFICATION_HOME/duty-board/dismissed.json for dashboard dismissals. Chat requires in-process brodification 0.21.7+ and a configured owner; shared-chat summaries default to counts only. No network calls, no model calls, no credentials, no background processes.

entries.name: eatwise
entries.description: Eatwise (外卖营养教练) — local-first Chinese dietary coach: deterministic meal nutrition reviews, personal daily energy/nutrient targets, and consented on-device profile and meal history through 9 MCP tools over a bundled open food database (TFND + USDA FNDDS). No network, no accounts, no payments; profile schema rejects name/phone/ID/medical fields by design. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (cbc08f6) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 22.5+ on PATH. Disclosure — the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first.

entries.name: echarts-in-chat
entries.description: Render a chart inline in the brodification Desktop transcript: the model emits ::echarts{labels=... values=...} and the plugin mounts an interactive SVG chart (dataZoom slider, click-to-filter legend, resize-aware, 280-560px height clamp) in the plugin SDK's transcript-directive slot. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no environment variables, no background processes, and nothing read or written outside the message it renders; the chart is drawn locally as inline SVG with no third-party libraries.
entries.title: ECharts in Chat

entries.name: edit-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the turns in which the agent changed files with write_file or patch: /edit-log shows how many turns changed files, how many files in all, the median per turn, the most changed file type and how long ago the last one was, per model, platform or day, a table of file types (extensions), or the newest turns, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /edit-log recent lists the newest turns (ten, or up to 100 with /edit-log recent 50). A turn another plugin keeps going is counted once. Disclosure — subscribes to pre_verify as an observer only: always returns nothing, so it never keeps the agent going or changes a turn; writes turn metadata (model, platform, file count, files per extension, a 12-digit hash of the session id; never a path, file name or answer text) to plugin-data/edit-ledger/edits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; never opens the changed files; no network

entries.name: effortless-brodification
entries.description: Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt: a fast judge (Jev/TypeSafe, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or any custom API) reads the next message once per turn and rewrites the request's reasoning effort before it ships — easy questions run cheap, hard jobs get high. Port of effortless for Claude Code. Disclosure — sends the next message (≤4000 chars) plus a short recent-conversation excerpt (≤1600 chars) to the configured judge endpoint (default api.typesafe.ai for Jev; a local or custom OpenAI-compatible API otherwise), solely to pick the effort; the optional model_map setting (off by default) also switches the turn's model to the one you map to the verdict; keeps recent per-turn token counts in its own plugin state; no telemetry; secrets resolved only through brodification' secret scope; stdlib-only, no pip dependencies.
entries.title: effortless-brodification

entries.name: empiriolabs-media
entries.title: EmpirioLabs AI Media
entries.description: EmpirioLabs AI backends for brodification' image_generate, video_generate and text_to_speech tools (backend `empiriolabs` for image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider and tts.provider): image generation and editing, text-to-video and image-to-video, and text-to-speech, with models and voices from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure: registers three backends and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); when one is selected and its tool is called, the prompt, source images or text to speak go to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, read through brodification' secret scope, and each call is billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account with no brodification approval prompt; it reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models), polls GET /v1/jobs/{id} while a generation runs (videos up to 15 minutes by default), downloads the generated files from the returned URLs into brodification' cache (the key is never sent to them), and reads a local image file only when the agent asks to edit one.

entries.name: empiriolabs
entries.title: EmpirioLabs AI
entries.description: EmpirioLabs AI as a brodification model provider (provider id `empiriolabs`): chat models with tool calling from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog, each with its context window, image input and reasoning support declared to brodification, a low-cost auxiliary model picked from the same catalog, and `reasoning_effort` sent only when you choose a level and the model accepts it. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests (prompts, tool definitions and tool results) go through brodification' own client to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, which brodification reads, and are billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account; the plugin itself only reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models, kept in memory for an hour), writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: enchanted-composer
entries.title: Enchanted Composer
entries.description: Draft enhancement, reusable prompt libraries, undo/redo, and owner-bound full-duplex voice for brodification Desktop. Disclosure — Derived from brodification-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from brodification-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and brodification task results go to OpenAI. The API lane runs only when COMPOSER_REALTIME_OFFER_URL is set: it posts the SDP offer to that https URL with COMPOSER_OPENAI_API_KEY, or the profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, as a Bearer token (redirects refused). A user-configured wss:// bridge receives microphone audio, chat/profile identifiers and task results. Spoken requests the voice model delegates run as brodification agent turns with tools in the chat where voice started; runs that need approval are stopped, not approved. Settings and usage totals are stored under BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/enchanted-composer/. No telemetry, no self-updater, no Codex OAuth-file reads.
known_issues: Codex subscription authentication is managed with `codex login` outside brodification; the plugin does not read or write Codex OAuth files.
Full two-sided persistent voice history and a phone voice client are not included in version 0.2.7.

entries.name: entropicmem
entries.description: Durable local memory for brodification agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under BRODIFICATION_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to BRODIFICATION_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to BRODIFICATION_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_patch_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not brodification core, and is off by default.

entries.name: epistemic-harness
entries.description: Record a provisional claim or uncertainty before an evidence-gathering step, then link the actual observation to it.

entries.name: error-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of failed provider calls (rate limits, overloads, timeouts, context overflows): /errors shows how many attempts failed per model, provider or cause, how many brodification could retry, and the most common HTTP status, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /errors days puts one day on each line, newest first; /errors recent lists the newest failures (ten, or up to 100 with /errors recent 50) and how long ago each happened. Disclosure — writes failed-attempt metadata (ids, provider, model, HTTP status, brodification's failure class, exception class name, timings; no error message, request or prompt text) to plugin-data/error-ledger/errors.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

entries.name: evalroute
entries.description: Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active brodification model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "brodification evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and brodification shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run brodification -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "brodification evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into BRODIFICATION_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "brodification evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query brodification chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except BRODIFICATION_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "brodification evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under. Disclosure — "brodification evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "brodification evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "brodification evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute (>=0.9.2,<0.10), declared as a Python dependency that brodification installs on your confirmation.

entries.name: event-read
entries.description: Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your brodification gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with brodification tools. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with brodification cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run brodification cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch relies on private parts of brodification, so an update can stop it. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.

entries.name: excel_line
entries.description: Excel-backed hierarchical long-term memory tree (10-row cap per workbook, dynamic branching, leaf pointers). Classifier defaults to the host model; third-party keyless rotation is opt-in.

entries.name: field-academy
entries.title: Field Academy
entries.description: Learn brodification by doing real work. Four paths (Messenger, Traveler, Crossroads, Boundary Keeper) climb Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced to a capstone on a problem of your own, and a fifth, Guide, covers setting brodification up for a client: practice labs built from made-up data, a proposal, one real service run by a scheduled job for several days, a recovery drill, and a review signed by a reviewer you choose. Every mission ends with a check on something you made; your own brodification scores your written answers in a new chat; passed missions come back for short spaced reviews; and at the end of a path you can create a Field Record, your own self-issued learning record. Field Academy is an independent community plugin. It is not made, issued or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure — no network calls (a source link opens in your browser only when you click it); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill: pre_llm_call may add one sentence offering a practice to the user message, only in interactive desktop, TUI and CLI sessions, and post_tool_call records which tool was used; pressing Try it or a scoring button opens a new chat and sends the practice or scoring prompt there (on an older brodification it goes to the clipboard instead); the Desktop page calls gateway list methods only (session.list, cron.manage list, skills.manage list, tools.list, mcp.catalog, commands.catalog, setup.runtime_check); stores progress, pasted documents, practice labs, review packets and saved Field Records in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/; reads a file you name (UTF-8 text, max 5 MiB) and hashes a recording you name without copying it; Guide labs write and check made-up .env and auth.json files inside its own labs folder (refusing to build in a real brodification home) and never read brodification's real ones; on the Guide path reads brodification's run-history database read-only, jobs.json and up to 25 log files (2 MiB each), keeping only timestamps for the job you name, and reads install-stamp.json for the brodification version; no private brodification imports.

entries.name: file-tray
entries.description: Session file tray — paths the brodification agent touched via read_file, write_file, or patch. Desktop pane and /files. No API keys.

entries.name: filebox
entries.description: Dual-panel commander file browser for brodification Desktop — whitelist-guarded file CRUD, copy/move/symlink, media preview, multi-select, rename, and trash. No network I/O, no model tokens.

entries.name: financial-datasets
entries.description: Stock market data from Financial Datasets - financial statements, prices, SEC filings, insider and institutional ownership, KPIs, news, macro data, and a stock screener.

entries.name: fish-audio
entries.title: Fish Audio
entries.description: Lifelike voices for your agent: Fish Audio's expressive text-to-speech in 80+ languages, plus transcription, voice cloning and a voice library. The official Fish Audio plugin: Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in brodification Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a brodification speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop, and live dictation captions on brodification 0.21.6+ (stt.streaming: true). Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices and fish_transcribe tools, /fish and brodification fish commands, and four skills. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to api.fish.audio's realtime speech-to-text endpoint while you speak, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model (free through 30 November 2026), whose requests Fish may use to improve its models. The key comes from the profile's secret scope (brodification stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to brodification's audio cache; clone samples and recordings it uploads must be regular audio files, and brodification config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through brodification's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the brodification dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through brodification's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page and /fish alias can set or reset the profile's Fish model and voice and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this plugin's repository as a public GitHub issue or comment with your gh login only after you approve the exact text; reports leave out keys, credit amounts and your own voice ids, and security problems go to the repository's private advisory form instead. No telemetry.
known_issues: brodification's text normaliser alters <|speaker:N|> markup and Drama 3 closing tags such as </whisper> on the plain text_to_speech path; use fish_speak for multi-speaker speech and Drama 3 word tags (brodify-ai/brodification#133131).
In the dark theme an empty API key field in Settings is very hard to see; a fix is proposed (brodify-ai/brodification#138994).
Under plugins.isolation: host the brodification fish terminal command is unavailable and voice replies use whole-file speech instead of streaming; /fish, the tools and both providers still work.

entries.name: fleet-policy
entries.description: For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`brodification fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). Ships two skills (managed-scope admin, recurring tasks). Disclosure — records only model, reasoning effort and service tier per role (no message content, headers or keys) via the pre_api_request and pre_auxiliary_call hooks and a pass-through llm_execution middleware, stored in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/fleet-policy/observed.json; crons --cost opens cron/executions.db and state.db read-only and checks each cron run's final reply locally for silence; watch is an operator CLI command that calls one MCP tool at the config's server_url (or the admin-pinned watch_server_url) with config headers in which ${VAR} env values are expanded, follows redirects, and writes seen ids to a state file at the config-chosen path; the recurring-tasks skill has the agent write watch configs under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/watches, a script under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/scripts and a cron job; no other network access, no telemetry.

entries.name: fluxer-platform
entries.description: Fluxer gateway adapter for brodification. Native Fluxer integration using Fluxer's bot REST API for outbound messages, Gateway WebSocket events for inbound dispatches, message edits, agent-requested reactions, pins, reply references, media delivery, and channel-directory enumeration. Component button

entries.name: fmsg-platform
entries.description: fmsg platform adapter for brodification. Real-time inbound over the fmsg-webapi WebSocket (/fmsg/ws), outbound via its JSON REST routes. Authenticates with an fmsg API key (fmsgk_...) exchanged for a short-lived JWT — run the agent as a derived sub-account such as @alice_brodification@example.com. Only http

entries.name: foresee
entries.title: Foresee
entries.description: Let AI assistants shop for home and auto insurance: compare instant quotes across every carrier. Connects to the hosted Foresee MCP server (Streamable HTTP at agents.go-foresee.com), with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package (hosted MCP server plus three skills), no Python and nothing runs locally; the vendor is Foresee Insurance Services, LLC (go-foresee.com). Every quote request sends the profile the user gives in chat (ZIP, age or date of birth, vehicles, drivers, driving record, home details) to agents.go-foresee.com with no account or API key. The live_carrier_quotes tool additionally sends the user's identity (name, date of birth, street address, email, optionally phone and driver's licence number) and, after the user's in-chat consent recorded verbatim, Foresee's agents submit those details to the selected insurance carriers, who may run a soft credit-based insurance score pull and contact the user. Foresee does not take payment or bind policies.

entries.name: freight-reconciliation
entries.description: Payer-side freight reconciliation: import carrier bills and trip ledgers into a deterministic local core (SQLite, WAL, no cloud), re-calculate against contracted rates and produce evidence-linked difference lists for human review — 14 MCP tools over uvx stdio (engine pinned to the immutable commit e8cd259c, release v0.4.1), with 3 bilingual workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs uv on PATH. Never approves payments, sends messages or writes back to ERP/TMS; final confirmations route through a local admin page the model cannot reach. Disclosure — the optional freight-admin page listens on 127.0.0.1 and is where a human confirms mappings, rules, matches and exports; nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: freshdesk
entries.description: Generic Freshdesk API v2 tools for brodification. Unaffiliated community connector, not a Freshworks product. Disclosure: calls the account's native Freshdesk HTTPS origin with profile-scoped secrets FRESHDESK_DOMAIN and FRESHDESK_API_KEY; downloads an attachment into the brodification cache only from that ticket's own attachment hosts; the two write tools escalate to brodification human approval and fail closed when no person is present. No third-party dependencies, shell commands, telemetry, or self-updater.

entries.name: frihet
entries.description: Official brodification integration for Frihet — discoverability, setup, diagnostics, and operating guidance for the Frihet MCP. Zero duplicated tools; the canonical 158-operation Frihet surface stays in @frihet/mcp-server and the remote endpoint https://mcp.frihet.io/mcp. Disclosure — /frihet setup and /frihet doctor send an unauthenticated MCP initialize to mcp.frihet.io (or FRIHET_MCP_URL); /frihet doctor also makes one read-only list_invoices call through brodification's MCP client once you grant plugins.entries.frihet.mcp_allowlist; reads ~/.brodification/config.yaml only to check that an mcp_servers.frihet block exists; the pre_tool_call hook prompts before Frihet MCP calls it classifies as irreversible or unknown, but reads and draft-first creates pass without a prompt unless the server sets trust: untrusted.

entries.name: fusion
entries.description: Multi-model fusion router for brodification: detects the model fleet your harnesses (brodification, Codex, Claude, Grok) actually have installed and builds a Frontier -> Middle Manager -> Frontier routing structure with pinned models and provenance from execution records. `brodification fusion teams|validate|plan|run|index|report|status`.

entries.name: fxmacrodata
entries.description: FXMacroData macro and FX research: official-source economic releases, indicator history, release calendars, policy rates, yield curves, FX, commodities and COT positioning, with source citations. Native tools for 23 REST operations and 49 hosted MCP tools, plus a /fxmacrodata USD brief command. Disclosure — tool calls send their arguments over HTTPS to api.fxmacrodata.com and mcp.fxmacrodata.com only, with FXMACRODATA_API_KEY in a request header when it is set. The key is optional: without it the data catalogue, the USD release calendar and recent USD releases (15-minute delay) work, and other data answers with a subscribe message. No files written, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry. It also adds a short research-guidance section to the system prompt and 72 tools in the fxmacrodata toolset; MCP tool behaviour is served remotely and not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: gadget
entries.title: brodification Gadget
entries.description: Talk to your brodification from small ESP32 devices with a screen, microphone and speaker: hold a button, ask, and hear the answer. Adds a gateway platform where each device is a chat, plus tools to list devices, show a card on a screen and run device actions (LEDs, relays). Disclosure — the gateway listens for devices on a WebSocket port (8765, all interfaces by default; plain ws:// unless tls_cert/tls_key are set). New devices need a brodification pairing code unless listed in GADGET_ALLOWED_USERS; GADGET_ALLOW_ALL_USERS skips pairing (development only). A paired device answers the agent's command approvals for its own chat (allow once or deny). The first approved device becomes the platform's home channel by default. Spoken replies that are not WAV are converted with the local ffmpeg. `brodification gadget update --latest` downloads firmware from this repository's GitHub releases, checks size and SHA-256 against the release manifest (files carry build provenance attestations) and sends it to the device. Writes only under plugin-data/gadget/. Uses brodification's own STT, TTS and image cache; no telemetry. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: game-dev
entries.title: Game Dev
entries.description: Read-only project inspection and asset audits with playable-slice, asset-production, and verification skills. Disclosure — lists file names and sizes under any absolute project path the agent supplies (skipping hidden, symlinked and credential-named entries), reads that project's project.godot/export_presets.cfg and, on request, hashes asset files; no writes, no shell commands, no network calls.

entries.name: gbrain-plugin
entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin wiring GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT) into brodification as a local memory layer over MCP: /gbrain status command, desktop starter, and per-profile Postgres setup/update/maintenance scripts. Not affiliated with upstream. Disclosure — the plugin itself only adds a /gbrain status command and a Desktop pane; GBrain is installed by the user via scripts/setup.sh, which installs bun (curl|bash), an unpinned gbrain from GitHub HEAD, and provisions PostgreSQL with sudo.

entries.name: gbrain-pointer
entries.title: GBrain Pointer
entries.description: Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.

entries.name: gbrain-retrieval-reflex
entries.description: pre_llm_call hook plugin, enabled with `brodification plugins enable`: injects ambient context from a GBrain instance before each turn (volunteer_context, then a hybrid-query fallback). Not a `memory.provider`. Silent no-op when GBrain is unreachable or no token is set. Disclosure — before each non-trivial turn the last six user and assistant messages (truncated) and the current message are sent with a GBRAIN_TOKEN bearer token to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp), and returned brain-page text is injected into the turn.

entries.name: gemini-live-bridge
entries.description: Realtime duplex voice chat with the Gemini Live API — a status-bar minibar for the brodification desktop app (transcript, model catalog, thinking level, session token meter, auto-redial via session resumption). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost and receives single-use ephemeral tokens. No agent tools; desktop-focused, dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory.

entries.name: genealogy-research-recipes
entries.title: Kinprove Genealogy Research Recipes
entries.description: Fact-checked genealogy instructions for DNA evidence, record searches and proof judgment. Native read-only skill bundle with recipe sources and an offline given-name lookup helper. Disclosure — optional third-party services and commands described by recipes require separately authorized tools and credentials; the adapter itself makes no service calls and registers no tools, hooks or MCP server.

entries.name: gh-ref
entries.description: @gh:owner/repo#123 context references: attach a public GitHub issue or pull request to a message (title, state, labels, description, the latest comments; for pull requests also the branches, merge state and change size). Disclosure — sends anonymous HTTPS GET requests to api.github.com only (the referenced owner/repo and number leave the machine; no token, public repositories only, 60 requests an hour per IP address); no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @gh: reference provider.

entries.name: gigamail
entries.description: Email and calendar through an existing local GigaMail MCP server, with a workflow skill and stdio launcher. Requires Python and a separately configured backend; no automatic backend installation or updates. Reads real mail and attachments; sending, deletion and calendar writes use GigaMail's out-of-band human approval. Disclosure — a thin stdio launcher for the separately installed GigaMail MCP server from Adecubed inc. (gigamail.ai, github.com/adecubed/gigamail, same author as this plugin); the plugin holds no mail logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but it starts that third-party executable from PATH or a configured path, points it at GigaMail's own data directory under your user profile (%APPDATA%\ADE or ~/.ade), and send, delete and calendar writes are gated by that backend's out-of-band approval rather than by brodification.

entries.name: git-autosave
entries.title: Git Autosave
entries.description: Lightweight local alternative to directory checkpoints for Git projects. Before a mutating tool call it saves the affected repository's working state to a private local shadow ref (refs/brodification-autosave/<branch>, with reflog) through a private index, or copies the single existing file outside Git; `brodification autosave find` and `restore` recover a pre-edit version. Disclosure — runs local git subprocesses in repositories the agent touches (hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor and lazy fetch disabled); writes shadow refs/reflogs into those repositories' .git and unencrypted file copies into its plugin-data directory; never changes HEAD, branches, the real index or the working tree and never pushes; skips credential stores (.env, auth.json, .ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and dependency directories; `brodification autosave sweep` reads the session database read-only and is scheduled by the user; no network, no background processes; it observes only and never blocks or approves a tool call.
known_issues: One V4A patch that moves a symlink and then updates the moved path can miss the edited file on case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems; commit first or send the Move and the Update as separate calls.

entries.name: git-hook
entries.description: Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree brodification touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once.

entries.name: git-review
entries.title: Git Review
entries.description: Read-only Git review pane for brodification Desktop: shows what the agent's last turn, uncommitted, staged or unstaged work, or any selection of commits changed, in unified or split layout, and cites changed lines into the composer as @line: references. It never fetches, stages, commits or checks out. Disclosure — the backend runs read-only git subprocesses (rev-parse, status, diff, log, show, cat-file, ls-files, for-each-ref, branch, remote, rev-list, hash-object) with timeouts and output caps, external diff and textconv drivers disabled; the only network use is the optional PR/MR badge, which runs the user's own gh or glab CLI for the checked-out branch (the plugin itself makes no network requests); it reads files and history inside authorized repositories only (the focused workspace, configured repos/roots and the latest agent selection), this profile's config.yaml, and the cwd column of the sessions table in state.db (read-only); it writes only $BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/git-review/select.sqlite3 (agent selection requests) and Desktop plugin storage (display settings, turn baselines), never into a repository; while the pane is open it polls the local backend every 3 s (agent selections) and 5 s (live diffs); no background processes, credentials or telemetry.

entries.name: git-tasks
