entries.description: Multi-repo GitHub issues & PRs in an Orca-style Tasks view for brodification Desktop. Disclosure — runs your logged-in `gh` CLI and `git` through brodification Desktop's shell bridge and scans your configured clone folders for GitHub repos; approve, close and reopen act on GitHub in one click; creates git worktrees and opens seeded brodification sessions from the detail view.

entries.name: gitbrodification
entries.description: GitHub PRs and issues as a right workspace pane in brodification Desktop, via the connected gh CLI. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI; the in-pane update pill only runs `brodification plugins update gitbrodification` (no fetch-and-replace) and currently compares against upstream main rather than the pinned sha.

entries.name: github_app
entries.description: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise tools with bot-first attribution and approval-gated issue/PR writes. Disclosure — authenticates as a GitHub App from GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID and a private key in GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY or GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH/_FILE (read from the profile env or BRODIFICATION_HOME/.env, held in memory only, never written or logged), falling back to GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token` when no App variables are set, and reports which identity acted in every result. Talks only to https://api.github.com or the operator-configured GITHUB_API_URL / settings.api_url (HTTPS, no redirects; no tool argument can change the host). Issue/comment/review/merge writes stay disabled until settings.allow_write_actions is true and each one additionally goes through brodification's human-approval prompt via its pre_tool_call hook (an 'always' answer does not persist).

entries.name: glasser
entries.description: Glasser's hosted MCP: search, inspect and run 1,000+ paid data endpoints (people and company enrichment, SEO, web, social media, US property, stock quotes) with one key, pay per call. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: a stdio bridge through mcp-remote (browser sign-in, no key in the package) plus a bundled skill for setup and the spending rules. Requires Node.js 18+. Disclosure — paid data broker: each run tool call charges your Glasser balance per the endpoint's published price with no in-brodification confirm step; runs npx mcp-remote@0.14.3 as a local stdio bridge to https://api.glasser.ai/mcp; the sign-in token is cached by mcp-remote under ~/.mcp-auth/.
entries.title: Glasser

entries.name: gmail
entries.title: Gmail
entries.description: brodification Desktop Gmail mailbox UI for search, reading, and thread inspection, with preview-confirmed send, reply, archive, trash, and label changes. Uses the active profile's existing Google Workspace OAuth setup; email is sensitive external content. Gmail actions and data access require user review and configuration. Disclosure — reads the active profile's brodification Google Workspace token (google_token.json, refreshed in memory only) and calls the Gmail API; opening an unread message marks it read, other send/trash/label changes go through a confirm step (one setting can skip every review dialog, and then the prepare ticket, account/profile binding, exact snapshot validation and readback verification still run); remote email images load only after the user allows them. Attachment metadata listing and bounded read-only attachment download (25 MB cap) are profile/account-scoped.

entries.name: go-whatsapp
entries.title: Go WhatsApp
entries.description: Outbound WhatsApp tools through GOWA: registers GOWA's native MCP server and adds device listing, pairing, and removal. Setup can connect an existing server or explicitly install pinned GOWA v9.5.0 as a loopback-only authenticated native user service on Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, or Windows x86_64. Disclosure — agents can send messages and mutate WhatsApp state through the linked account; session databases grant account access. The plugin does not ingest incoming messages or configure webhooks.

entries.name: gondola-provider
entries.description: Gondola, a USDC-settled marketplace API for Venice AI inference

entries.name: gonogo
entries.description: Turn a pilot-scale eval score into a deployment decision — Wilson intervals, a confidence threshold that routes uncertain cases to a human, and an honest INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE verdict when the sample cannot support the claim. Disclosure — gonogo_report writes report JSON/HTML to the path the model supplies.

entries.name: good-student
entries.description: Wrong-question diagnosis and study-action loop for parents and students — deterministic local core (SQLite, no cloud), host-model recognition gated by parent confirmation. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); good-student MCP server pinned to immutable commit 2469cbb over uvx, with the good-student workflow skill bundled. Needs Python 3.10+ via uv. No credentials required; all data stays on-device and nothing is uploaded.

entries.name: govee
entries.description: Discover and control Govee lights (power, brightness, color, white temperature, scenes) through Govee's developer API. Every command is checked against the model's advertised capabilities and ranges, then confirmed by a state read-back. Disclosure — sends device IDs and control commands to openapi.api.govee.com with your Govee API key; the model can change light state; stores nothing on disk.

entries.name: greyridge-token-safety
entries.description: Skill that runs a pre-trade safety check on Base ERC-20 tokens (honeypot/sellability, measured transfer tax, owner/mint/pause flags, liquidity, SAFE/CAUTION/AVOID verdict) by curling the Grey Ridge x402 API's free preview endpoint. Skill-only: no tools, hooks or env vars. Disclosure — the skill has the agent run `curl` against Grey Ridge Signals Group LLC's API (api.greyridgesignals.ai) with the token address and, for the swap gate, trade side and USD size; it mentions a paid x402 route ($0.01 USDC per call on Base) and an unpinned `pip install git+https://github.com/rezearcher/greyridge-x402-tools` helper that the user installs themselves. Its verdict is a heuristic, not financial advice.
known_issues: Base chain only; DEX buy/sell tax is not measured (only transferTaxBps). Free preview is rate-limited; unattended use needs the paid x402 route ($0.01/call).

entries.name: grok-acp
entries.description: xAI Grok subscription as a brodification model provider, driven over ACP stdio. Disclosure — spawns the vendor grok CLI found on PATH (grok agent over ACP stdio, plus grok models / grok login during setup) and drives your existing Grok subscription login; no API key is stored and brodification provider secrets are stripped from the child environment.

entries.name: groq-provider
entries.description: Groq as a brodification model provider (`--provider groq`, or Groq in `brodification model`): reasoning effort is sent in the form each Groq model accepts, so gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b work (through a custom endpoint, brodification 0.21.5 sends them a value Groq rejects with HTTP 400), and the model list leaves out Groq's speech-to-text, text-to-speech, prompt-guard and 4K-context models that brodification cannot run. Not affiliated with Groq. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through brodification' own client with GROQ_API_KEY, which brodification reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: gurusup-brain
entries.title: Gurusup
entries.description: Your company's memory in brodification: search decisions, people, customers and projects across every source your team connected to Gurusup (Slack, HubSpot, Notion, uploaded documents and more), with the sources behind each answer. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1, no local code and no API keys. Disclosure — hosted-only MCP connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Gurusup's server at mcp.brain.gurusup.com under the signed-in Gurusup account (OAuth via `brodification mcp add gurusup-brain --url https://mcp.brain.gurusup.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401), and answers are limited to what that account can see; write tools save knowledge to the company's Gurusup workspace (add_company_knowledge, skills_publish) and send issue reports or feedback to Gurusup (report_issue, send_feedback), and request_human_info can message a teammate on Slack or phone them when its dispatch flag is set.

entries.name: health-data
entries.description: Local health and daily-context data store for brodification.

entries.name: health-insights
entries.description: Deterministic, local-first analysis of your own Apple Health data - weekly trends, rule-based concern checks, nutrition versus Dietary Reference Intakes, an IOM energy target, lab results and opt-in modules (GLP-1 monitoring, medication adherence; all off by default). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package of ten skills that drive the separately installed health-insights command line tool (installed from the plugin's own pinned copy); the plugin itself contains no executable. Works on a self-hosted HealthRelay or Health Bridge receiver database. Disclosure - it handles sensitive health data, so use a local model or one you trust; personal integrations (medication counts, model wording) are off by default. Disclosure — the skills run a separately installed health-insights CLI that reads your HealthRelay or Health Bridge SQLite database read-only and keeps imported lab and ECG results under ~/.local/share/health-insights; the health values it prints are sent to whichever model provider your brodification session uses.

entries.name: healthcare
entries.description: Local-first personal health records: encrypted on-device Vault (AES-GCM) for vitals, medications, activities, emotions, sleep, encounters, diagnosis mentions, medication plans and reminders, served through a Keychain-paired local daemon with 24 scoped MCP tools. Zero-config first run: the plugin bootstraps Vault + daemon + agent pairing automatically under PLUGIN_DATA. Engine pinned to an immutable PyPI release (healthcare-mcp==0.2.1) over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), macOS only, Python 3.11+. Zero network by default; the optional LLM report-import endpoint stays off unless the user configures it. Approval-gated deletes, tamper-evident audit chain. Disclosure — personal health record-keeping, not medical advice (the skill forbids diagnoses and dosage changes); first run has uvx fetch healthcare-mcp==0.2.1 from PyPI; the optional report-import path posts report images to Alibaba DashScope (qwen-vl-max) unless HEALTHCARE_LLM_ENDPOINT points elsewhere, and only when HEALTHCARE_LLM_API_KEY is set.

entries.name: healthrelay
entries.description: Read-only access to your own Apple Health data through a self-hosted HealthRelay receiver. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one stdio MCP server (ten read-only tools, including intake evidence; no raw SQL, no write tools) and three skills for setup, review and troubleshooting. Requires your own HealthRelay receiver (health-bridge) and an iPhone app you sign yourself; the plugin ships neither. Disclosure — exposes your Apple Health data, read-only, from your own receiver database to whichever model you run, so use a local model or one you trust with health data; runs the separately installed health-bridge binary from PATH; the setup skill can install the receiver from the author's git tag with uv tool install.

entries.name: heartbeat2
entries.title: HeartBeat 2.0
entries.description: Your agent follows up on its own: timed check-ins, recurring checks and watchers that wake it in the same chat when something changes. You (with /pulse) or your agent (with the pulse tool) arm follow-ups at a time, recurring checks, a check-in after a long silence, or deterministic watchers on a file, process, URL, read-only command or brodification event (kanban, subagent, API error, reactions). A wake is a turn in the same messaging DM that armed it, on that chat's own model: no side model, cron session or subagent. Watchers decide without a model call; the agent answers each wake with a structured verdict (notify or stay silent, never a typed sentinel); a no-op governor slows, then pauses pointless wakes and asks once. Every guardrail is a user setting (quiet hours, daily caps, unanswered mute, floors, lifetimes) that the agent works inside and can never widen. A one-time reminder you ask for in chat bypasses the unanswered mute and daily caps; HeartBeat 2.0 grants that only in a turn that carries your message. Arming returns a one-line receipt saying when the wake will really fire, and a wake that could never fire before it expires is refused. It delivers to messaging-gateway DMs only and needs plugins.entries.heartbeat2.allow_gateway_injection: true. Ships the plugin skill `heartbeat2:heartbeat2-report-problem`, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — wakes and watchers run full turns on the conversation's own model, billed like any message, at your conversation's context size, with the conversation's normal tools and approval prompts; the agent can arm wakes and watchers itself unless you set agent_can_create to ask_first or no; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and `git ls-remote <url>` / `gh -R` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url_allow_private is on; file watchers refuse paths brodification blocks from reading; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.
known_issues: A wake turn that fails at the provider shows brodification's own failure notice; the plugin cannot suppress it (brodify-ai/brodification#136749). HeartBeat 2.0 backs all wakes off until a model call on the profile succeeds.

notify=false silences the final reply; platforms that show tool progress by default (Discord, WhatsApp, Matrix) still show a progress bubble per wake turn unless display.platforms.

.tool_progress is off (quiet injection requested upstream: brodify-ai/brodification#136825).
Delivers only to messaging-gateway DMs by default (dm_only); CLI, TUI, Desktop, API-server and cron arming are refused until brodification core supports silent injected turns there.
When brodification falls back to another model during a wake turn, its model-fallback notice is posted to the chat, even for a wake that stays silent (brodify-ai/brodification#137738).

entries.name: hermetic
entries.description: Status-bar popover for brodification Desktop with three views: Costs (spend, cache, pricing drift, OpenRouter provider routing), AAI (skill changes, ratings, tests and replays) and HDR (posture, destinations, sensitive paths, what runs on its own). Disclosure — reads this profile's sessions (and other profiles' when you pick them) to audit tool calls, paths and hosts; can edit and save config.yaml and rewrite skill files when you ship or revert a version; AAI replays and judge runs resend conversation context and tool definitions to OpenRouter with your OpenRouter key and incur cost; HDR lists listening TCP ports via ps/lsof.

entries.name: hicortex
entries.description: Shared fleet memory for brodification agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation.

entries.name: hindsight
entries.description: Hindsight long-term memory provider — knowledge graph, entity resolution and multi-strategy retrieval (recall/reflect/retain tools plus automatic per-turn capture). Maintained by Vectorize; cloud, local external and local embedded modes are available. `brodification memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main). Disclosure — in cloud mode (and local external) every turn's conversation, and every entry the agent adds or replaces in brodification's built-in MEMORY/USER stores, is sent to api.hindsight.vectorize.io or the URL you configure, into every bank it writes to; local embedded mode starts a background Hindsight daemon (fetched with uvx, version-pinned, on first run when hindsight-api is not installed) and keeps its LLM settings in ~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env; setup writes the keys you enter to the profile .env; repositories under folders you list in trusted_project_dirs may choose their bank with .hindsight/config.toml; `brodification memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main).

entries.name: holographic
entries.title: Holographic
entries.description: Local fact-store memory provider: SQLite with FTS5 keyword search (word forms in English, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Indonesian, German, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali, Italian, Turkish, Polish and Dutch; Russian and English words of the same root at a lower weight, from bundled DerivBase.Ru (Apache-2.0) and Open English Wordnet (CC BY 4.0) pairs; German compounds and German and Spanish irregular verb forms from bundled Wikidata Lexemes tables (CC0); Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai by character n-grams, Chinese also split into words with jieba's dictionary (MIT), Traditional and Simplified Chinese compared as one through a bundled OpenCC table (Apache-2.0), Japanese spelling variants through SudachiDict's (Apache-2.0); synonyms through keywords the agent gives when it stores a fact), trust scores, entities with aliases and HRR (holographic reduced representation) recall, with no API key, network or model calls unless the optional search by meaning (embeddings: on, off by default) is switched on. The provider that shipped in-tree as plugins/memory/holographic, with the same provider name, config (plugins.brodification-memory-store) and memory_store.db, so `brodification update` moves existing users onto it; the schema change is additive and older versions keep working on the file. Taken over from Nous Research's handoff copy (NousResearch/brodification-plugin-holographic) and maintained by itpartypattaya; since 0.1.1 it fixes probe/reason/related/contradict, non-atomic writes and the never-written retrieval_count, gates recall by relevance without repeats, flags duplicates and conflicts when a fact is added, and honours the provider contract (read-only subagent contexts, brodification_home, mirror metadata, backup_paths); since 0.8.0 it keeps the history of every fact (change / end / correct / revert, search and list as_of a date) and `forget` erases a fact with all its versions from the file; since 0.16.0 a name guessed from a fact's text must be shaped like one and stays provisional until a second fact or a person confirms it, and entities can be renamed or deleted (the facts stay). Disclosure — local only unless the optional search by meaning is switched on: reads and writes one SQLite file per profile ($BRODIFICATION_HOME/memory_store.db unless db_path says otherwise), or with scope: user / chat / thread one file per user or chat in holographic-users/ or holographic-chats/ next to it; each fact version records where it was written (platform, chat type, chat and thread id, session id, the turn author's id and display name, and whether the person said it or the agent inferred it; never chat titles), shown in full by list, history and export and not in recall unless recall_source: short (date, display name, this or another chat); each confirmation of a fact by a person keeps its time, session id and that person's id (no text); forget deletes that and the confirmations with the fact and keeps only an HMAC of the text, keyed by a random key stored in the same file, as a tombstone; delete_entity removes a name, its aliases and links from the entity index (never a fact) and keeps an HMAC of each name the same way (not of an alias only a fact's text gave, which goes without one), and both rewrite the file so freed pages keep no copy; the first writable open after an upgrade that changes the extraction rules relinks the facts to their entities under the new rules (stores up to 2,000 facts and 500,000 characters; larger ones on fact_store rebuild_entities), changing only the names it guessed and their links, never a fact, a declared name or an alias someone gave; subagents never write, but a cron job's explicit fact_store / fact_feedback calls do unless cron_writes: false (on by default); no subprocesses or telemetry, and no network calls or credentials unless embeddings: on (off by default): then the text of facts, and of messages and fact_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron_writes is on (embedding_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding_key_env, OPENAI_API_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored.
known_issues: Word forms are matched by stems, not a dictionary: an irregular form can miss (ponies / pony). A synonym is found only if the fact's keywords name it, unless the optional online search by meaning is on; facts stored without keywords (older ones, auto_extract) need `enrich`.

Arabic, Indic scripts, Indonesian, German, Turkish, Polish and Dutch are matched by scanning the facts' text: the first such search after start analyses every fact (about 1-1.5 s at 5,000 facts, 4-6 s at 20,000); stores without such facts never scan. The bundled dictionaries load on the first word of their language (Chinese about 0.2 s and 30 MB).

forget cleans the database file only: brodification session history, `brodification backup` archives and copies other tools made are not rewritten (tools can read the `forgotten` table and clean their own copies by fact id).

entries.name: honcho
entries.description: Honcho is memory infrastructure for building stateful agents that understand changing people, agents, groups, projects, and ideas over time. Store messages and events, let Honcho reason in the background, then query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any model or framework. Use it managed at api.honcho.dev, run a local stack with the honcho CLI, or self-host the server yourself. Maintained by Plastic Labs; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns, derived conclusions and peer/session ids are sent to the Honcho API (api.honcho.dev by default, or the self-hosted base_url you configure) under your HONCHO_API_KEY; every request also carries X-Honcho-Host (brodification version and OS platform) and X-Honcho-Plugin (plugin version) headers that Honcho records for usage attribution.

entries.description: Add and manage custom OpenRouter models in brodification without modifying the core catalog.

entries.name: hud-teach
entries.description: Click-through numbered marks on any live Mac window — chess, games, Photoshop, Settings — so brodification can teach on the real UI without clicking for the user.

entries.name: huddo
entries.description: Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, edit or unsend your own messages, react, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.9.8, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, huddo_transfer (and huddo_leave with to) hands room ownership to another member, and huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar with operator: true change your paired human's display name or avatar; brodification does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_edit/huddo_unsend/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download/huddo_transfer/huddo_leave/huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skill tells the agent to get confirmation in your own brodification chat before anything sensitive.

entries.name: hwiki
entries.description: Markdown wiki as brodification long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside BRODIFICATION_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to brodification's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at BRODIFICATION_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in BRODIFICATION_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to brodification backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

entries.name: hyatlas
entries.title: HyAtlas Memory
entries.description: HyAtlas 5 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories are kept locally. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `brodification hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings are computed locally; stored memories leave the machine only in the LLM calls described below. Extraction is opt-in and uses an LLM you choose: `brodification memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in brodification's .env as HYATLAS_LLM_KEY. The plugin reads that key only through brodification's get_secret and reads no brodification credential. A plain key file named by HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE also works; the server reads it on every call, so do not point it at another program's credentials such as brodification auth.json. The server has no default endpoint and makes no LLM call until the endpoint, the model and a key are all present; while the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, /api/v1/status reports llm "awaiting_key". `brodification memory setup`, the repo installer and the sample launcher pre-fill a free Nous Portal endpoint and model (and setup defaults to ultra mode), but nothing is sent until a key is supplied. A server the plugin starts gets that key in its environment; for a server started another way (the launcher, a service) that reports "awaiting_key", the plugin (at most every 10 minutes) and `brodification hyatlas doctor` POST the key over plain HTTP to /api/v1/llm/key, only when the configured server host is this machine; the server accepts it only from a loopback address and keeps it in memory only, never on disk. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters), together with up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions of that owner so the model can update them instead of duplicating them. In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). Once a day per owner (HYATLAS_CROSS_SCHEMA_EVERY; off disables it) ultra also sends up to 40 of that owner's stored patterns to find up to 3 that hold across topics. In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions, recent summaries and newest facts to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY), and, after a 30-minute pause in an owner's writes (HYATLAS_EPISODE_GAP; off disables it), up to 40 of that stretch's facts to write one episode summary. HYATLAS_RECONCILE=on (off by default) adds a second LLM call per write that sends the new facts together with similar stored ones (including those under user IDs grouped with the owner by HYATLAS_USER_ALIASES) so the model can update, replace or link them; it is meant for a local model. An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. Turns written while the endpoint was unreachable or before a key arrived are extracted later by a catch-up pass (every 10 minutes by default, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_EVERY; rows up to 7 days old, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_MAX_AGE), sending the same text a write would have sent. `brodification hyatlas doctor` sends one short test prompt ("Reply with the single word OK.") to the endpoint and writes, finds and deletes one test memory. When you replace or remove an entry with brodification's memory tool, the plugin asks the local server to retire the matching memory (reversible); nothing leaves the machine. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, brodification starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `brodification hyatlas start` keeps running after brodification exits until `brodification hyatlas stop`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `brodification hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads no credentials (since 4.8.0 it no longer reads brodification auth.json). No telemetry.
known_issues: After enabling, select the provider with `brodification memory setup` (memory.provider: hyatlas) — installing and enabling alone does not activate memory.
The agent tools and hooks arrive through the MemoryProvider interface, not ctx.register_tool, so they do not appear in the plugin tool list.
Requires the separate hyatlas-go server binary (installed by the user); without a reachable server the provider reports unavailable and memory features degrade rather than fail.

Updating the plugin does not update the server: install hyatlas-go v5.0.0 too. A store written by an earlier version can be cleaned with the server's maintenance endpoints (see after-install.md, 'Upgrading a store written before 4.5.0').
5.0 removed share_llm_key: the plugin no longer uses brodification's Nous sign-in. Set your own extraction key (llm_key) with `brodification memory setup`; `brodification hyatlas doctor` checks it.

entries.name: hydradb
entries.description: Long-term memory for brodification, backed by HydraDB. Relevant context is recalled before each turn, and completed turns are saved in the background. Disclosure — when selected as the memory provider, each turn's user message (as the recall query) and every completed user/assistant turn are sent over HTTPS to the HydraDB API (api.hydradb.com, or HYDRADB_BASE_URL) under HYDRADB_API_KEY.

entries.name: identity
