Without trusted_users every direct chat counts as the owner: whoever can message the agent directly may add facts to the owner profile and correct them (not delete them) until the owner's id is listed.
Spotting USER.md and MEMORY.md edits made through terminal and execute_code is best effort: a path built some other way, or a command run from a script file, can get through.

terminal and execute_code calls are read up to 16,384 characters. A longer call that contains the word memories, USER.md or MEMORY.md (any case, quotes ignored) is refused even when it only reads them; a longer call that contains none of them passes without being read.

entries.name: memory-zvec
entries.description: Community Zvec memory backend for brodification - in-process HNSW + RocksDB FTS store with native hybrid retrieval and session-safe lock governance; embeddings via any Ollama-compatible endpoint (local Ollama bge-m3 by default).

entries.name: memtomem
entries.description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from brodification, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.6.8) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks. At startup the server also reads the nearest .env found upward from its installed location inside uv's cache (normally ~/.env), setting variables not already present, outside brodification's MCP environment filtering.

entries.name: mermail
entries.description: Privacy-first agent email inboxes and workspace automation through hosted Mermail MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, seventeen skills bundled); authenticate with OAuth via `brodification mcp login mermail`. No credentials are stored in mcp.json. Disclosure — the bundled skills also expose Mermail's paybox wallet tools over the hosted MCP (x402 payments, xStocks trading, standing grants); the skills allow the agent to move funds without a same-turn confirmation when your message already states exact terms, so spending controls live on your Mermail account, not in brodification.

entries.name: meshy
entries.title: Meshy
entries.description: Meshy AI's own MCP server (pinned @meshy-ai/meshy-mcp-server@0.6.5) for text, image and multi-image to 3D, texturing, remeshing, rigging, animation, concept images and 3D-print prep, with a bundled meshy-3d workflow skill. In brodification Desktop: inline 3D cards with a download and convert menu, a gallery of recent generations and saved models (with a "Made from" history), image sets, and a credit chip in the status bar. Every credit-spending call goes through brodification's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a 200-credit limit per chat makes it ask again. Needs MESHY_API_KEY and Node.js 18+. Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned server from npm through npx; it sends prompts and the images or models you or the agent name to Meshy's API (api.meshy.ai) under your key, gets only MESHY_API_KEY from your profile, and sends no analytics (its User-Agent names brodification and its version). Downloads go to the plugin's data folder or the folder the agent names (never over an existing file); the Desktop backend fetches only from Meshy's asset hosts. The skill's helper scripts (model stats, preview render, optional Blender hand-off) run locally through the terminal tool.

entries.name: metamask-wallet
entries.description: MetaMask Agent Wallet for brodification — chat-only setup, reads, and approval-gated transfers/swaps/signatures, a gated Guard Mode policy editor, and a background 2FA watcher. Keys stay in MetaMask.

entries.name: metronix
entries.description: Metronix memory provider for brodification with prefetch recall and built-in memory write-through.

entries.name: microsoft365
entries.description: Pre-release Microsoft 365 Graph tools for Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Calendar, Teams, To Do, and Planner.

entries.name: mindgraph
entries.description: MindGraph — semantic graph memory with hybrid retrieval, goal/decision tracking, and cross-document synthesis.

entries.name: minecraft-platform
entries.description: Minecraft gateway adapter for brodification. Spawns a Mineflayer bot that joins a Minecraft server, wanders around, and relays chat messages between players and the brodification agent. Supports offline and Microsoft-authenticated accounts.

entries.name: minimax-image
entries.description: MiniMax image generation -- Image-01 models via MiniMax platform. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image with subject reference.

entries.name: minimax-search
entries.description: MiniMax web search via the Token Plan API — keyed, no CAPTCHA

entries.name: minimax-video
entries.description: MiniMax (Hailuo) video generation -- Hailuo 2.3/02 and S2V-01 models via MiniMax platform. Async task API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and subject-reference-to-video.

entries.name: mistral-vibe
entries.description: Direct Mistral Vibe subscription access — browser PKCE login, dedicated credential pool, account-visible catalog discovery, relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models. Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "brodification auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the brodification credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Prompts and model listing go only to api.mistral.ai/v1. Vibe subscription coverage of API use is not guaranteed and may bill as pay-as-you-go. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely.

entries.name: mnemostack
entries.description: Persistent agent memory over a mnemostack service or a local Qdrant — hybrid recall (vector + lexical + graph), verbatim capture with self-echo suppression, and soft retraction. Multi-tenant when pointed at a shared authenticated service; the tenant is resolved server-side from the service key. Disclosure — the pinned directory is a discovery shim; the provider code installs from PyPI at the version pinned in plugin.yaml pip_dependencies (brodification-mnemostack==1.0.3) into the brodification venv. Configured via MNEMOSTACK_* env vars; no key is required for a purely local Qdrant setup.

entries.name: mnemosyne-dashboard
entries.description: Local-only web dashboard for browsing and visualising Mnemosyne memories, triples, stats, and consolidation history.

entries.name: mnemosyne
entries.description: Local-first memory layer for brodification — SQLite with vector + FTS5 hybrid recall, episodic consolidation, temporal knowledge graph. Zero cloud. Disclosure — the mnemosyne_remember_media tool refuses local file paths unless MNEMOSYNE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_PATHS is set and sends media only to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint when modality_enabled is on; video uses ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

entries.name: mnemoverse
entries.description: Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms (beta) let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the two bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; brodification runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context. OAuth tokens are held and refreshed by brodification, never by the package. No telemetry, background process or self-update code.

entries.name: model-drift-watch
entries.description: Scheduled check that the model you use in brodification has not quietly got worse: 34 fixed, exactly graded questions (reasoning, instruction following, Japanese, plus your own) run through brodification cron, each run tested against the same model's own baseline with an exact per-question test and a same-day confirmation run, and a message only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model or a failed measurement. Not yet tried against a real LLM API (checked with a local mock model and real brodification cron). Disclosure — each check calls your own model through ctx.llm on your bill, capped per check by the plugin (default 120,000 tokens / $0.50, no daily cap; the agent can start checks itself via the model_drift tool, and the scheduled agent turn is extra); price lookup goes through brodification's pricing code (may fetch OpenRouter/models.dev prices); 10 optional code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child process (not a hostile-code sandbox) including in unattended cron runs when enabled; `schedule` creates one brodification cron job that survives plugin removal (run `unschedule` first); writes run history to plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry.

entries.name: model-picker
entries.description: Per-turn cost classifier across three model tiers (Quick / Standard / Expert): rates each user turn from configurable best_for lists and rewrites the outgoing request's model through the llm_request middleware, biased to keep the previous tier unless the turn changes shape, with escalate_model for tool failures. Disclosure — the plugin rewrites the model field of every outgoing request for a classified session, picking between three configured model ids that must all belong to the session's own provider (a foreign-provider tier is refused and the session model stands); it makes one bounded auxiliary classifier call through the host's plugin LLM route on each classified turn (up to about 12,000 characters of recent conversation plus the prompt), reading its model ids from config.json next to the plugin, MODEL_PICKER_CONFIG, or MODEL_PICKER_* env, and falls back to the host's primary model; routing decisions, with the first 120 characters of each classified prompt, are logged to $BRODIFICATION_HOME/logs/model-picker.log; a classifier-driven tier change can ask the context engine to compact the transcript before the switch, and escalate_model replaces the next request's context with a model-written handoff summary plus the recent tail; that engine registers only when the host config sets context.engine: model-picker.

entries.name: model-router
entries.title: Model Router
entries.description: Profile model settings, opt-in Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads brodification profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background brodification children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — once you enable routing for a profile, the model-callable `coding_route` tool starts detached background brodification agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless `approvals.single_query_mode: approve`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' `skills/` folders. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs.
known_issues: Small bounded changes stay with Main. Ordinary implementation delegation requires two substantive independent workstreams with net parallel benefit; explicit delegation and required Heavy/independent review remain exceptions. This is guidance, not an API two-job minimum.

Preferences now live under Settings > Plugins. The main-sidebar settings row is removed; legacy /model-router bookmarks remain supported. A host supporting the public plugin-settings area is needed; no private-core or sidebar fallback is added.
The Desktop UI is Korean-first. Windows runtime/SDK/Desktop behavior has been tested; full Linux/macOS runtime support is not claimed.
Requires a brodification build with unified Python/Desktop packages and request/tool middleware; new Python tools may require a new session.
Fast and fallback can increase API charges or subscription-credit use. Transports bypassing the request middleware, including codex_app_server, are outside Fast inheritance coverage.
The native scanner can report CAUTION for the manual source-repair helper; routing-disabled capability probes can warn that coding_route was not registered.
Default-profile mid-run activation was not confirmed on the developer's shared backend; package installation is distinct from existing-session activation.

entries.name: model-usage-status
entries.description: Provider-native Claude and Codex remaining allowance windows in the brodification Desktop status bar. Disclosure — spawns the local `codex app-server` and `claude auth status` CLIs and reads the Claude OAuth token read-only through brodification core; the optional install.sh (not part of the catalog install) edits the statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json; macOS only.

entries.name: monid
entries.description: Connect your agent to third-party tools and APIs (web search and scraping, people and company data, social media, media generation, email and phone) through one integration. The agent discovers, compares and runs tools at runtime, paid per call from one Monid balance. Disclosure — Monid (monid.ai, by Monid / monid-ai) is a paid third-party marketplace: the agent installs the @monid-ai/cli npm package or connects to mcp.monid.ai, sends your requests and any uploaded files to Monid and on to its providers, and each run spends your prepaid Monid workspace balance. The "confirm the price first" step is an instruction to the model in the bundled skill, not a brodification approval prompt, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.monid`.

entries.name: morning-briefing
entries.description: Personal daily newspaper for brodification: gathers weather, calendar, AQI, curated 36-hour news (timestamped Reddit RSS + X + web search, per-story QR codes), and newsletter digests, renders one 8.5x11 newsprint page, and prints it every morning via a cron job.

entries.name: mrscraper
entries.description: MrScraper web search, rendered extraction, crawling, and scraper tools. Disclosure — every tool call is a paid MrScraper API request billed to your account; URLs, prompts and schemas you pass are sent to mrscraper.com.

entries.name: ms-decision-provider
entries.description: Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Reference implementation of the typed decision-provider runtime in #113008. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to brodification's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.

entries.name: my-github
entries.description: Desktop and dashboard plugin: statusbar chip, palette command, and dashboard tab listing your GitHub repos (public + private) via the gh CLI.

entries.name: mybot-farm
entries.description: Search mybot.farm, plant/reinstall brodification packs (Desktop Recruit + CLI), and post GAF listings. Disclosure — plants third-party brodification profiles (config, SOUL, skills, memories) from mybot.farm sellers with no hash pinning; force/clean delete profiles.

entries.name: myswarm
entries.title: MySwarm
entries.description: Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via brodification default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file brodification loads into every session's system prompt) after a brodification approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Adds a ~2.8k-character MySwarm guidance section to every session's system prompt. Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

entries.name: nachos
entries.description: Durable memory and context compression for brodification with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under /nachos/.

entries.name: needs-you
entries.description: brodification is waiting — full Desktop page for pending approvals. Queue, chip, OS notify. Redacted previews only. No API keys.

entries.name: nerve
entries.description: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for brodification with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, and OpenJev Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya and OpenJev can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local brodificationContextBus checkout into BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugins/brodification-context-bus and runs brodification plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger this.

entries.name: netmind-provider
entries.title: NetMind
entries.description: NetMind OpenAI-compatible model provider with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://api.netmind.ai/inference-api/v1 through brodification' own client with NETMIND_API_KEY, which brodification reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: next-prompt
entries.description: Suggests your next message after each turn as a pill under the Desktop composer: your likely answer when the agent asks you something, or the natural next step.

entries.name: next-steps
entries.description: Next-step suggestions under the brodification Desktop composer after each turn: local Ollama inference, per-session state, target routing (session, new tab, bots, kanban), tiny-model capacity profiles, EN/DE UI. No API keys. Disclosure — after every agent turn, sends the last 8 messages (each cut to 200 chars) plus the working directory to Ollama on localhost; clicking a suggestion immediately submits it as a prompt in the current session, a new session, or another profile's session, or creates a kanban card, and for non-current targets also attaches the working directory and the last 6 messages (on by default, can be turned off under Targets).

entries.name: nextcloud-talk
entries.title: Nextcloud Talk
entries.description: Signed Nextcloud Talk bot webhooks and text replies for brodification, with JSON/XML OCS support. Disclosure — runs an HTTP webhook listener (default 0.0.0.0:8788, HMAC-verified with the bot secret) and sends messages and optional Basic-auth room lookups to your Nextcloud server; registers the `nextcloud_talk` gateway platform.
known_issues: Text only; attachments, reactions and inbound reply-context reconstruction are not implemented.
Dedupe is in-memory and does not survive restart; uncertain sends are not automatically retried.
Valid empty OCS acknowledgements confirm delivery without returning a message ID.

entries.name: nextdns
entries.description: Read-only NextDNS tools - DNS query logs, blocked queries with the blocklist that matched, and aggregate analytics by domain, device, blocklist or protocol. For triaging DNS problems and answering "was this blocked, and by what". Uses the official NextDNS API; makes no configuration changes.

entries.name: nexus
entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; brodification and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when brodification cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from brodification config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to a cloud model; reads ~/.brodification/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when brodification cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS_EMBED_IN_HOST=1), the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon whose default model is a cloud model that receives memory text), and the service keeps running after brodification exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in brodification config.yaml; reads ~/.brodification/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt.

entries.name: ngrok-ai-gateway
entries.title: ngrok AI Gateway
entries.description: The ngrok AI Gateway as a brodification model provider (`--provider ngrok`, or ngrok AI Gateway in `brodification model`): one access key for all your model providers, with failover. The model list comes live from your gateway, and gateway errors (unrouted model, access-policy and upstream-key failures, out of credit) map onto brodification' fallback instead of a generic error. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1 (or NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) through brodification' own client with NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_KEY, which brodification reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: nine-balance-widget
entries.title: Nine-Balance Widget
entries.description: Nine AI provider balances in one desktop widget — live balance/usage and quota reads, token-based spend estimates with off-peak price windows, drop alerts, and an anime mascot per provider with rotating flavour lines (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok). Fully English UI. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Keys are entered in the widget's settings page and stored in plugin-scoped storage; the widget only calls those providers' official APIs. Ported from MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget (MIT). Disclosure — API keys you enter in the widget's settings are stored in plaintext in Desktop plugin storage (not brodification' secret store); while the widget is on, the Desktop renderer polls the balance/usage endpoint of the provider matching your current model every 60 s with that provider's key (api.deepseek.com, api.minimaxi.com / api.minimax.io, open.bigmodel.cn / api.z.ai, api.moonshot.cn / api.moonshot.ai, api.kimi.com, token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the key in the URL, api.x.ai); each key goes only to its own provider; draws a floating widget over the app window.

entries.name: node-search
entries.description: Bounded Markdown metadata+graph prefilter for configured local roots

entries.name: nowstamp
entries.description: Give the agent a clock. Appends the current date and time, plus the real gap since the previous message, to every user turn. Optional spaced-out timestamps on tool results for long runs.

entries.name: ntfy-approval
entries.description: Answer brodification' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes brodification' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: nvidia-app
entries.description: NVIDIA App control through its local MCP server: overlay capture and state, driver status and release notes, game optimization, and app launch. Requires NVIDIA App 11.0 or newer on Windows; the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while the app's service is running. The plugin reads the endpoint and token NVIDIA App publishes in its own McpServer server.json on every connection, so a changed port or token needs no reconfiguration. Disclosure: the tools read and change NVIDIA App settings on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.
entries.title: NVIDIA App

entries.name: nvidia-broadcast
entries.description: NVIDIA Broadcast control through its local MCP gateway: camera, microphone and speaker effects, Studio Voice profiles, device selection, camera resolution, and effects on local media files. Requires NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 or newer on Windows (2.2 and older have no gateway); the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while NVIDIA Broadcast is running in the user's desktop session. Disclosure: the tools change live audio and video effects on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.
entries.title: NVIDIA Broadcast

entries.name: obsidian-memory
entries.description: Browse, search, and edit Obsidian vault notes from the brodification dashboard. Features force-directed graph visualization, multi-vault support, markdown rendering with wikilinks, and inline note editing.

entries.name: oc-free-provider
entries.description: Unofficial OpenCode Zen free-model transport for brodification. Discovers live zero-cost tool-capable models by intersecting OpenCode Zen and models.dev over HTTPS, persists only the last successful intersection for restart fallback, and bidirectionally translates compatible OpenCode and brodification tool schemas, calls, choices, and replayed history while brodification executes tools locally. No OpenCode CLI, Node.js, npm, or npx dependency. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results, and other conversation content leave the machine for OpenCode and the selected model provider; model availability, retention, data use, and permission are governed by their current terms.

entries.name: office-desk
entries.title: Office Desk
entries.description: Guarded Word, PowerPoint and Excel editing: tracked Word changes and comments, slide and deck edits, and Excel edits with LibreOffice recalc. Every write gets a backup and a revertible receipt, and you review it all on a Desk page in the Desktop app. Settings are in Settings > Plugins. Disclosure: reads any Office file the agent is pointed at but writes only inside folders the user puts on the Desk (backups and receipts live in the plugin's own data dir). xlsx_recalc runs the user's installed LibreOffice (soffice, headless) on a temporary copy. The Desk page reads the session store read-only to show a workstream's chat. No network calls, telemetry, credentials or background processes. Depends on the paper-docx, paper-pptx and paper-xlsx forks. They provide the docx, pptx and openpyxl import names, so they must not share an environment with python-docx, python-pptx or openpyxl.

entries.name: offpeak-bekci
entries.title: Off-Peak Watch (offpeak-bekci)
entries.description: Makes Ollama Cloud's off-peak window visible and actionable in brodification: a desktop status-bar chip shows the countdown and the queue item counts (Ollama off-peak hours: weekdays 18:00-12:00 UTC, weekends one block), a one-shot notice fires 30 minutes before the window opens, and approval is taken only from the user (`/offpeak-onayla <id,id>`) — work runs only if approved, and items never enter the queue by themselves. `/offpeak-durum` prints a readable report by default (machine-readable JSON with `/offpeak-durum json`), and `/offpeak-kur` prints the cron job it would install in full plus a `plan_hash`; nothing is installed without a hash-bound approval typed by the user, and the plugin never writes the cron store. One `llm_execution` middleware measures the call rate for Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window and ships measure-only (`kuru_kosu: true`): it records what it would delay and never delays. No network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads; the only local files it touches are the queue ledger and its own JSONL measurement log. Output language is English by default; `dil: tr` selects Turkish. Auto-delivery is host-dependent: in a classic CLI session the request enters the agent queue; on the Ink TUI / desktop-panel host the core asks for a persistent `session_key`, which the command handler does not receive, so the command prints the parameters as a single line of JSON. Injecting into a gateway additionally requires `plugins.entries.offpeak-bekci.allow_gateway_injection: true` (default off); the only in-process way to read that key is the private `gateway.session_context` module (rule 9 -> not used). Requires brodification >= 0.22.2. Disclosure — the llm_execution middleware can sleep Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window once `kuru_kosu: false` is set (default is measure-only); it writes a JSONL measurement log and, on `/offpeak-onayla`, rewrites the user's queue file; `/offpeak-kur` and `/offpeak-kaldir` leave cron install/removal requests in the session (or, with `allow_gateway_injection: true`, inject them into the gateway) for the agent's own cron tool to act on; no network calls, no credential reads, never writes the cron store.

entries.name: omh
entries.description: Oh My brodification (OMH) bridge: routing hints and role context for OMH workflow skills, per-task delegation model routing, plan todos and a status tool, a brodification Desktop status pane (off until enabled), bounded evidence probes that keep prepared work apart from observed results, and a file-backed memory provider. Disclosure — omh_delegate_route writes delegation.model/provider/reasoning_effort in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/config.yaml and the session hooks restore them; omh_gather_evidence runs allowlisted checks (python -m unittest with reporting flags only, python -m compileall, git diff --check, omh doctor/probe/docs/release checks) via subprocess on the host, outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without brodification' terminal approval, in the agent working directory or below it, so it runs whatever test code that directory holds; omh_team (only with the separate OMH core package installed) asks once through the brodification approval prompt for an exact list of up to 8 check commands from an accepted plan, then runs them on the host as each helper returns; omh_jev_ask posts model-supplied state and questions to api.typesafe.ai (openrouter.ai only when the operator opts in via ~/.omh/jev/settings.json) with the user's own TYPESAFE_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY, only in a turn where the user names Jev; opt-in egress_attempts (re-registers chosen core tools, needs the operator's tool-override grant) and browser_adapter (vetoes core browser_* tools) settings; reads session and cost metadata from state.db read-only; state lives under ~/.omh and <project>/.omh.

entries.name: omnivoice
entries.description: OmniVoice TTS provider for brodification

entries.name: opaque-composer
entries.description: Keep the desktop composer solid while scrolling so conversation text stays readable.

entries.name: openai-compatible
entries.description: GPT Image through CLIProxyAPI, New API, or any OpenAI Images-compatible gateway, with gateway-aware errors and requested-vs-returned size reporting. Disclosure — sends image prompts and any source images (local files, data URLs or public HTTPS URLs) to the OpenAI-compatible gateway base_url you configure, authenticated with OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_API_KEY.

entries.name: openalex
entries.description: Scholarly search, citation traversal, grouped counts, and fulltext access through OpenAlex with session spending limits.

entries.name: opencode-shepherd
entries.description: Watch over opencode sessions from anywhere: alerts for stopped turns, questions and permissions, plus a dependency-free CLI to reply. Disclosure — the skill has the agent install the ocshepherd CLI from GitHub at a pinned commit and, after asking you, add a cron entry or systemd unit that polls your opencode server; the CLI talks to that server with the password you provide, can reply to its questions and permission prompts, and optionally sends alerts to Telegram or runs a notify command you configure.

entries.name: openinvest
entries.description: Self-hosted AI investment committee — skills for portfolio review, a decision ledger, and a 4-role LLM committee (macro / quant / risk / CIO) that debates a symbol. Disclosure — the skills run the openinvest backend from PyPI via uvx (pinned in run.sh) and keep portfolio, ledger, committee records and any keys you add in plaintext under ~/openInvest (or $INVEST_HOME); it fetches public market data and RSS news, and on the Direct path / daily report sends your portfolio and wealth context to the LLM you configure (default api.deepseek.com) and, if installed, to the agy or gemini CLI for a second opinion; news ingestion can trigger extra committee runs (LLM spend). The MCP tools are a server you add to config.yaml yourself (the printed snippet runs the plugin's pinned run.sh with `trust: untrusted`, so brodification asks before ledger writes); buy/sell/deposit/withdraw only edit the local ledger — it never connects to a broker or places orders.
entries.title: openInvest

entries.name: openltm
entries.description: Long-term memory for brodification agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in BRODIFICATION_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)

entries.name: openmail
entries.description: Gives a brodification agent its own email address. Inbound mail wakes the agent over a websocket, replies go out in-thread, plus tools for sending, reading and provisioning inboxes.

entries.name: openrouter-picker
entries.description: One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, brodification secret store or BRODIFICATION_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).

entries.name: openrouter-spend
entries.title: OpenRouter Spend
entries.description: OpenRouter API-key spend and recorded chat costs in USD/INR. Disclosure — sends the configured OpenRouter key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or the variable named in api_key_env) only to openrouter.ai's read-only key and generation accounting endpoints, and fetches public USD/INR rates from api.frankfurter.dev unless a manual rate is set; middleware on every LLM request records ids, model, token counts and reported cost (no prompt or reply text) to its own ledger; the dashboard reads accounting metadata (session ids, token counts, billing provider) read-only from the state.db and OpenRouter Spend ledger of every profile under the brodification root.

entries.name: openrouter-voice
entries.description: OpenRouter speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers for brodification (stt.provider / tts.provider = openrouter).

entries.name: openspec
entries.description: OpenSpec CLI tools for spec-driven development workflows

entries.name: openviking
entries.title: OpenViking
entries.description: Long-term memory for brodification. Capture conversations, recall useful facts across sessions and search your knowledge. Choose Quick Local, OpenViking Service (managed cloud) or your own server. Disclosure — conversation turns, tool results and MEMORY.md / USER.md edits are sent to the configured OpenViking server. Quick Local setup installs the newest OpenViking 0.4.x server release from PyPI at setup time (checked against PyPI's hash, not the version reviewed here; re-running setup upgrades it) plus a hash-pinned llama-cpp-python wheel and a local embedding model. It copies the active brodification static LLM API key into a private file under the profile for extraction, and its localhost server keeps running after brodification exits and after plugin removal (stop it with `brodification openviking local stop`). Extraction can use a remote LLM. Custom localhost connections can start openviking-server from PATH with the profile environment minus brodification bot, gateway, GitHub and dashboard secrets; model and tool API keys still pass.

entries.name: operations
entries.title: Operations
entries.description: A brodification Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads brodification-metrics-dash's <brodification root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <brodification root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through brodification send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task.
known_issues: Request, error, host and conformance results come from brodification-metrics-dash's metrics.db; without it those sections show "unavailable".
Merge requests and the GitLab conformance standard need the GitLab host and token set in the plugin's settings (or GITLAB_HOST and GITLAB_TOKEN).

entries.name: optchat
entries.description: OptChat-style endless memory for brodification: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after brodification's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.

entries.name: optmem-brodification
entries.description: Independent brodification integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under BRODIFICATION_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables brodification' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

entries.name: orbit-desktop
entries.description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by brodification. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working brodification provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the brodification tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current brodification conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local brodification session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: orcaslicer
entries.title: OrcaSlicer for brodification
entries.description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Nous Research. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/BRODIFICATION_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.brodification-orca (BRODIFICATION_ORCA_HOME), outside BRODIFICATION_HOME.

entries.name: orquehelx
entries.description: Per-call delegation across your own subscriptions. The model sends each subagent to a named route with delegate_to(route, goal, context); each route pins a provider brodification already knows (Claude, Codex or Antigravity subscription plugins, ACP provider plugins) and a model. delegate_task, by contrast, uses the one target in config.yaml. Subagents launch through ctx.subagent_lifecycle. A child counts as out of quota only on an unambiguous provider error or a measured window at 100 %, and the route never switches on its own: a policy decides whether the parent asks you, picks another route, or waits. Disclosure: a pre_tool_call hook blocks delegate_task spawns while routes are configured (list/steer/stop pass); an api_request_error hook records quota errors in memory. Quota is read with brodification' fetch_account_usage (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex) on /ohx quota and after a provider error. No other network egress, no files written.

entries.name: osv-ref
entries.description: @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

entries.name: parallel-search
entries.description: Free web search and page fetching through Parallel's hosted MCP, with a setup skill bundled. No account or API key required. Queries and requested URLs are sent to Parallel. Adds direct MCP tools alongside brodification's native web providers.

entries.name: parcel-deliveries
entries.description: Track package deliveries with the Parcel app (parcelapp.net). List what's on the way, add tracking numbers and look up carrier codes, with a built-in guard for Parcel's strict rate limits. Disclosure — sends tracking numbers, descriptions and optional postcode/order email to api.parcel.app (Parcel Premium API key); the model can add deliveries to the user's Parcel account (add-only, capped at 20/day); caches delivery lists in plugin-data.

entries.name: parlor
entries.title: Parlor.sh
entries.description: Rooms where AI agents of any vendor talk to each other. A room is a URL; agents join, read and post over plain HTTP, with no accounts and no sign-in. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: the parlor skill plus the hosted parlor MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, 8 tools). Disclosure — hosted unauthenticated MCP connector at parlor.sh/mcp (tool set is server-controlled, not pinned) plus a curl fallback; messages the agent writes go to parlor.sh or the server in a given room URL and rooms are public to anyone with the link; room tokens are stored under ~/.local/state/parlor; the skill may keep background wait loops running.

entries.name: parrotnotes
entries.description: Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `brodification mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: pass-secrets
entries.description: pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Stdlib-only (subprocess + pathlib), no Python deps, no network — ever. Config: secrets.pass.{enabled,store_path,subdirs,override_existing,timeout_seconds}. Disclosure — when enabled, shells out to the local pass binary (10 s per entry) for every .gpg entry under the configured store subdirs and injects each as an env var that by default overrides .env and shell values; when enabled, also adds a ~900-char system-prompt note about secret resolution; no network.

entries.name: pastdotdev
entries.description: past.dev memory provider: recall before each turn from source-traced memory of past conversations, with sessions sent to past.dev when they end. Maintained by past.dev. Disclosure — the user's message (as the recall query) and each session's user and assistant text, with common secret shapes redacted, are sent to the past.dev API (api.past.dev by default, or the address you configure) under your past project key, with a past-brodification/<version> User-Agent; the key and identity are read from PAST_API_KEY or ~/.past/config.json, which past.dev's other connectors share; off by default on messaging-gateway sessions.

entries.name: pay-cli
entries.title: Pay CLI
entries.description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins from a wallet on this machine, through the local `pay mcp` stdio server of the official Pay CLI, with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; the user installs the `pay` CLI (brew or npm) and runs `pay setup` first, and the server is offered only while `pay` is on PATH. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: brodification starts `pay mcp` as a long-running local process; the curl tool spends the local wallet's stablecoin balance; each payment is confirmed by the user through MCP elicitation (PAY_FORCE_ELICITATION=1, declined when nobody can answer) and the server is marked untrusted; every profile using the plugin shares the same local wallet.

entries.name: pay
entries.title: Pay
entries.description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins through the official hosted Pay MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://connect.pay.sh/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys or local wallet), with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: the curl tool spends the hosted Pay account's stablecoin balance; hosted Pay enforces the account's spending limits (none move until the user sets them) and confirms each payment through MCP elicitation, declined when nobody can answer; the plugin marks its server untrusted, but the documented OAuth setup (`brodification mcp add pay`) replaces that entry with a native one that runs at `trust: full` unless the user sets `mcp_servers.pay.trust: untrusted`; chats sharing a brodification profile share its Pay account; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: pcs-security-tls-posture
entries.description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

entries.name: pdf-surgeon
entries.description: Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which brodification installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from.

entries.name: pending-queue-monitor
entries.description: Desktop-only, read-only monitor for pending memory and skill write approvals. Disclosure — the pane's API reads pending/memory/*.json and pending/skills/*.json under the default brodification root and every named profile directory beneath it (all profiles, not only the active one), and returns only counts, age buckets, oldest age, and per-item profile/subsystem/id/action/origin/created_at/age_seconds. It never returns or displays summaries, payloads, or record content; it exposes no approve, reject, or delete actions; it registers no tools, hooks, or middleware, performs no network I/O, and holds no credentials.

entries.name: penny
entries.description: Penny core memory and private notes for brodification. Disclosure — automatic recall sends the first 4,000 characters of each nontrivial local prompt to app.mypenny.ai as a search query, and the agent can save notes there through penny_remember without a brodification approval prompt; works only in local CLI/TUI conversations (cron, subagents and gateways are refused); login is a manual command that registers its own OAuth client with clerk.mypenny.ai and briefly listens on 127.0.0.1 for the callback; tokens are kept in <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/penny/auth.json (owner-only) and are not removed on uninstall; no raw transcript upload, telemetry or other-client credential reuse.
entries.title: Penny

entries.name: pep-ref
entries.description: @pep:<number> context references: attach a Python Enhancement Proposal to a message (status, type, authors, Python version and its first section, usually the Abstract), or one section with @pep:<number>#<section>, with PEP number and title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

entries.name: personae
entries.description: A messenger-style roster for brodification Desktop: one row per profile with its live sessions, per-profile colour, status lights, search, groups, multi-select and an Apropos beta that starts a new session already knowing the ones you picked. Disclosure — a Desktop pane over all your local profiles: it reads each profile's sessions, cron jobs and settings through the app's own requests and, only when you click, deletes or archives sessions (deletes ask first), changes cron jobs or edits profile settings; Apropos starts a new session with a hidden pointer message naming the sessions you picked; no network calls or telemetry.

entries.name: phone-harness
entries.title: Phone Harness
entries.description: Drive a real phone from brodification with one phone_exec tool: an iPhone via iPhone Mirroring on a Mac, an Android over adb, or a cloud phone from Phone Harness Cloud. Disclosure — runs model-written Python on this computer with your user's permissions through the phone-harness package (installed from PyPI); every phone_exec call goes to brodification's approval prompt unless you opt in to classifier auto-run, a heuristic, bypassable check that decides which scripts ask first; taps and types into your real phone and its apps and accounts; screenshots go to the system temp folder and are attached to the tool result for vision models; a cloud phone streams its screen to Phone Harness Cloud, bills by the minute, and uses phone-harness's own cloud sign-in (~/.config/phone-harness/auth.json); phone-harness's PostHog telemetry (script text, script output, helper arguments) is off under brodification unless you opt in.

entries.name: photofresco
entries.title: PhotoFresco
entries.description: Edit images in a PhotoFresco window you approve: layers, masks, selections, adjustment layers, previews and PNG/PSD export. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/) with a local stdio MCP server and bundled skill; needs Node.js 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium 120+. Disclosure — opens https://photofresco.com/app/ (remote web editor, live code not covered by this pin) in a separate Chrome/Edge/Chromium profile under ~/.local/share/photofresco-connector (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/PhotoFresco Connector), with cookies/sign-in/autosave kept there; previews and document state the agent requests go to your model provider; with the Send/Spend permissions granted in the PhotoFresco window, AI ops spend PhotoFresco credits up to the budget you set and cloud/feedback ops send document data to PhotoFresco, and brodification does not prompt before those calls; with Export granted, quick-export ops save to the browser's download folder; no local folders are readable or writable unless you add --read/--write yourself.
known_issues: Needs a desktop session and an installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium; the user approves the connection and each permission in the PhotoFresco window.

entries.name: pinned-folders
entries.description: A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

entries.name: pixel-worlds
entries.description: Watch your agents inhabit pixel-art realms in brodification Desktop, with imported scenes and a minimal PW Agents display.

entries.name: plan-mode
entries.title: Plan mode
entries.description: Claude Code-style plan mode for brodification: the agent explores and writes a plan, and edits nothing else until you approve it. It works on every interactive brodification surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating brodification tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .brodification/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent shows the complete plan, submits it with plan_mode(submit) and one approval card asks: approve and auto-accept edits, approve and review each file edit (when brodification approvals are on, every write_file and patch then gets brodification' approval prompt with its path and a preview), or keep planning; Other sends feedback, and the revised plan says what changed since the last revision. Once approved, it implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress. To change the plan yourself, keep planning, run /planmode edit, save, then /planmode show and /planmode approve; the text you were shown is saved as an approved snapshot, so later edits to the file do not change the approval. The classic profile (plan_profile: classic), approval_card: false and surfaces without a card use brodification' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve). When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks through clarify instead, so a person still decides. By default plans are compact and decision-complete, the lean profile asks at most three targeted questions, and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, plan_profile, allow_commits and plan_skill settings). Classic CLI enforced on every supported brodification; gateway, TUI and Desktop from brodification v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds; 0.21.6 recommended. On the interactive classic CLI, brodification' inline diff shows a new plan file in full, so the agent does not retype it (write_once). A report-a-problem skill drafts a bug report and files it with gh only after you approve the draft. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. A plan is approved only on its approval card (a clarify question only the plugin issues and checks), through brodification' own approval prompt, or with /planmode approve. It reads nine groups of internal brodification seams for session identity, workspace, profile, skills.inline_shell and the classic CLI's inline diff, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .brodification/plans under the session working directory, reads plan files there, saves the approved text of an edited plan as a new file under .brodification/plans/approved, and keeps per-session state in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. When a turn ends while a submitted plan still awaits approval and no approval card was answered, it adds one line to that reply on any surface, whatever its length, saying how to approve (unless footer is off). When you pick "Always" on a plan approval or a per-edit review, brodification core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml; each entry is keyed to one plan revision, so it cannot approve another plan. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and brodification serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file. On the interactive classic CLI (lean, write_once) it checks that brodification printed a newly written plan file in full, then tells the agent not to retype it. Its report-a-problem skill has the agent file to the plugin repository with gh only after the user approves the exact saved draft. The plugin itself makes no network calls, launches no subprocesses and has no self-updater.

entries.name: pocket-watch
entries.description: Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under BRODIFICATION_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.

entries.name: post-cortex
entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory through a post-cortex daemon (https://github.com/julymetodiev/post-cortex): typed records (decisions, fixed problems, code changes) in an entity graph with local semantic search. Recalls related records from the profile's workspace before each turn, puts the user card and the workspace's project card in the system prompt, mirrors built-in memory writes as records, and adds post_cortex_search, post_cortex_record and post_cortex_context (graph neighbours and reverse dependencies of named components) plus the post-cortex:memory skill. Records and captured turns carry the author brodification:<profile>. Profiles are mapped to shared workspaces by name glob, so a team of profiles recalls each other's records. Disclosure — talks only to the post-cortex daemon at the configured URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3737; a remote daemon over plain HTTP should sit on a private network or behind TLS): each non-trivial user prompt (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as a search query, and built-in memory writes and post_cortex_record calls are sent as records; with the opt-in capture setting (off by default) each completed turn of the primary agent is sent too: the user's message (with the sender's display name when brodification knows it), the final reply, tool names and file paths, never tool output; nothing goes to third parties. Disclosure — the daemon stores records (and captured turns, deleted after its message_retention_days) in its own database and redacts credentials, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and public IPv4 addresses on write. Disclosure — PCX_TOKEN (and optionally PCX_URL) is read through the brodification secret scope; the only local state is $BRODIFICATION_HOME/post-cortex.json (0600, never holds the token). No threads or processes of its own (capture runs on brodification' sync worker), no shell commands, no deletes in post-cortex; cron and subagent runs never write automatically.
known_issues: Requires a post-cortex daemon 0.4.0 or newer; cards, authorship, capture and derived_from need 0.5.0 and are skipped on an older daemon. A daemon bound to 0.0.0.0 must list the host in the plugin URL in its allowed_hosts, or every request gets 403.

entries.name: pricewin
entries.description: Live hotel and flight prices from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.price.win, no account or key), with the pricewin-travel-search skill and inline hotel/flight cards for the Desktop transcript bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Booking is a request the hotel confirms; nothing is ever charged. Disclosure — connects to the hosted PriceWin MCP server at mcp.price.win (no key); search arguments including a verbatim excerpt of the user's request go to it, and four of its twelve tools act on bookings (request_booking sends guest details to the hotel, cancellation needs a token emailed to the guest); nothing is charged.

entries.name: print-job-watch
entries.description: Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel ask for brodification approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, and when those checks cannot run. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your brodification gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running brodification tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" adds one unused line to config.yaml, and that line does not approve the next move. The optional watch is a cron job you create from the CLI (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. The watch needs plugins.isolation: in_process; under host it only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam.

entries.name: prism
entries.description: Prism OpenAI-compatible inference with long-context DeepSeek models.

entries.name: privacy-gateway
entries.description: Local Presidio-based PII pseudonymization for brodification model requests and tool results with an encrypted profile-scoped alias vault. Disclosure — PII detection runs locally with Presidio and the spaCy en_core_web_lg model, which you install manually; alias mappings are stored encrypted in the brodification plugin DB under BRODIFICATION_PRIVACY_GATEWAY_KEY; requests are blocked when the engine cannot load; tools outside rehydrate_tool_allowlist receive alias tokens, not plaintext.

entries.name: profile-models
entries.title: Profile Models

Disclosure — reads the selected profile's full config.yaml through the host's `config.get` (the response includes any credential fields it holds); only model-routing fields are kept and nothing is stored or sent off the machine.

entries.name: profile-pane
entries.description: Disclosure — copies .env key values (and opt-in auth.json backups) between profiles; rewrites other profiles' SOUL, memory and config.yaml. Cross-profile config pane with copy+manifest reconcile and per-group scope.

Other text written between redraws, CRLF line endings and output without a carriage return are left as they are. Disclosure — register() adds one transform_terminal_output hook that rewrites the output string in memory; no tools, network access, subprocesses, files, settings or environment variables.

entries.name: promoat
entries.title: AI Clone Videos
entries.description: Make realistic AI videos of yourself, with your own face and voice, from inside brodification. Powered by Promoat Disclosure — sends your scripts, prompts and the public media URLs you supply to Promoat's hosted API (promoat-platform-plugins.vercel.app) with your PROMOAT_KEY; video, character, voice-clone and speech tools spend paid Promoat credits; clone_voice and create_character build a reusable voice or face from the samples you pass; delete_character and delete_voice permanently remove account assets.

entries.name: prompt-enhance
entries.description: Rewrite a composer draft outside the chat and put the finished prompt back in the field. A prompt library keeps saved prompts, and a one-call model pick does not change the session.

entries.name: prompt-enhancer
entries.description: A composer button for brodification Desktop that rewrites a rough draft into a structured prompt (task / scope / constraints / output shape) and restores the original on a second click. One stateless gateway call, preserves @file and /command chips, per-session state. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體.

entries.name: prompt-optimizer
entries.description: Model-aware prompt rewriting with quality scoring, analytics, and coaching. Disclosure — the default auto mode rewrites every user message of 5+ words through your configured model (one extra LLM call per turn) before the agent sees it.

entries.name: prompt-pocket
entries.description: Local prompt library for brodification Desktop. Save, edit, search, and copy named prompts for manual use, with validated JSON import/export and IndexedDB storage. Does not read or modify composer drafts, send messages, or make network requests.

entries.name: prompt-queue
entries.description: Kanban-style prompt queue for the desktop: Play drains cards one at a time into per-card target modes — new session, existing session, project, or a profile's canonical Bot Chat — gated on the global model slot, background-review completion, and context compaction. Queue/Done/Skipped/ Failed tabs, two-row target picker, markdown ingest (Windows), and a trust-aware ::enqueue directive (ask-first by default). Disclosure — Desktop pane that runs queued prompts as full agent turns (all tools the session allows) in new or chosen existing sessions, projects it can create, or a hidden per-profile "Bot Chat" session while Play is on; reads recent agent.log lines to detect background reviews and context compaction; on Windows the markdown-ingest menu runs local shell commands (mkdir, dir, certutil, explorer, and python on a small bundled reader script it writes into the chosen folder) through brodification's shell.exec; an opt-in Auto-add setting lets ::enqueue directives in a live assistant reply queue prompts that run without a click.

entries.name: prompt-snippets
entries.description: Prompt snippet library for the brodification Desktop composer: a quick-pick overlay styled after the app's own slash menu (own shortcut), plus a management view with drag reordering, group tags and import/export. Inserts into the focused session, not the active one.
