UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體. v1.8.0 is fully SDK-only: the quick-pick overlay renders as an official Popover anchored to the plugin's own contributed node and all draft writes go through the host composer draft API. No local network; v1.6.0+ adds local JSON import/export via the system clipboard.

entries.name: prompt-studio
entries.description: Step-by-step prompt builder for brodification Desktop (F4): option cards per step with AI suggestions, then an AI-written final prompt sent to or placed in the composer through host.composer (brodification Desktop 0.21.5+). Tuned for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. AI calls go through its own auxiliary task (auxiliary.prompt_studio) via the dashboard plugin API; sends no temperature. No external network beyond the configured provider; preferences in ctx.storage. Disclosure — on opening in an existing chat (default on, toggle in Studio Settings) it reads the last 8 user/assistant turns (plus any compaction summary) of that session from state.db, redacts secrets and sends up to 8k chars to the configured auxiliary model for a short summary used in step suggestions; draft and form answers go to the same auxiliary model; no other network.

entries.name: prompt-tray
entries.description: Saved chat prompts — click a tray item to insert it into the brodification composer. Review / Plan / Explain defaults, then your own. No API keys. Disclosure — inserts prompts through brodification Desktop's internal brodification:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API); stores prompts in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/prompt-tray/prompts.json; no network.

entries.name: proofable-mcp
entries.title: Proofable
entries.description: Context and control for any AI. Agent identity, scoped access, and proof across tools. Disclosure — skills-only package: its workflow skills steer the agent to Proofable's hosted MCP server at mcp.proofable.me (which you add yourself with `brodification mcp add … --auth oauth`) to check identity proofs and agent permissions, create wallet-signed proofs, and store, list or revoke secrets in Proofable's hosted vault, so secrets you store and proof/agent data go to Proofable; brodification does not prompt before those MCP tools run unless you give the server a trust setting; the skills also suggest Proofable's own optional `proofable` CLI, which edits MCP/project config.

entries.name: protean-model-sync
entries.description: Fleet-wide provider and model presets with CLI and brodification Desktop support. Disclosure — writes model/provider keys into the config.yaml of the profiles you select (backup taken first).

entries.name: protean-ordaprompt
entries.description: Jev-style comparative classifier for OrdaPilot. It compares all topic labels and session choices in one batch, including new-topic, ambiguous, and new-session options. It uses calibrated score and margin gates, weighs continuity against context cost and contamination, and abstains when uncertain. OpenRouter is optional for provisional new-label proposals and disabled by default.

entries.name: protean-subagent-viewer
entries.description: Read-only brodification Desktop pane for live and past delegated subagent workers.

entries.name: protonpass
entries.description: Proton Pass secret source: resolves pass://vault/item/field references (mapped source "protonpass") or every env-var-titled item of one vault (bulk source "protonpass_vault") into environment variables at startup through the user's own pass-cli, beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources, with a brodification protonpass setup/status/token/set/remove/sync/disable CLI. Stdlib-only, no Python deps. Disclosure — when enabled, runs the user-installed pass-cli (argv only, allowlisted env, 30 s per call), which talks to Proton's API; a personal access token or AI-agent token is read from brodification' env and passed only to the pass-cli login child's environment (never argv); writes a 0700 session dir under cache/protonpass and a 0600 value cache (cache_ttl_seconds: 0 disables); no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry, no background process.

entries.name: provenance-gate
entries.title: Provenance Gate
entries.description: Flags memory and skill_manage writes that state a user decision ("the user decided ...", "用户决定 ...") without the user's own words: each such sentence needs a quote that appears verbatim in text the user typed in this session, shares key words with the decision and does not drop a negation. A patch is checked by the text it produces. Observe mode (the default) records flagged writes and `brodification provenance-gate report` lists them; block mode refuses them and tells the model how to fix the write. Measured on an independent blind set of 133 lines: precision 1.000, recall 0.694. Disclosure — two hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call); keeps a local copy of the text the user types, with its sender_id and session link, and an evidence log of checked claims under plugin-data/provenance-gate (30-day default retention, `brodification provenance-gate purge`); reads MEMORY.md, USER.md and skill files to reproduce what a patch produces; no network, no credentials, never asks for approval.

entries.name: provider-copy
entries.description: Copy provider API keys (and provider base-URL overrides) from one profile onto other profiles — a one-time, explicit copy from a desktop page. Per-profile missing/present badges, fill-missing by default with an explicit overwrite opt-in. OAuth sign-ins and messaging bot tokens never travel; values never cross back in responses.

entries.name: provider-status
entries.description: Status-bar quota tracking for 17 providers: Tavily, OpenCode Go, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), OpenRouter, Grok (xAI), Codex (OpenAI), OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Cerebras, Moonshot Kimi, MiniMax, Google Gemini, Hugging Face, Mistral, and Qwen. DeepSeek and GLM show peak/off-peak gauges and countdowns. Includes OAuth and multi-key pools. This edition does not rotate brodification environment keys on exhaust. Codex and Grok checks use their CLI client identity and user-agent.

entries.name: provider-usage
entries.description: Per-provider quota and balance readout in the brodification desktop status bar. Per-provider chips with eye toggles, a popover with every quota window, reset times, balance and key-cap amounts, near-limit amber tint, a desktop notification per threshold crossing, and burn-rate projections (ETA to reset or depletion). Providers: OpenCode Go, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, plus Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Nous, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek when configured. Disclosure — resolves provider credentials read-only (brodification account-usage helpers and profile secrets, else the profile's .env and the vendor CLI login files ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json) and sends each only to that provider's usage endpoint; the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity. No subprocesses, no telemetry.

entries.name: pstack
entries.description: Engineering rigor stack: poteto-mode orchestrator with 7 playbooks (new-feature, bugfix, refactor, testing, one-shot, migrate, explore), plus how, architect, interrogate, swarm, and unslop skills.

entries.name: public-holidays
entries.description: Public holidays for 200+ countries and their regions, plus workday checks, workday counts and deadline math (N working days after a date), computed in code instead of by the model. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to date.nager.at (Nager.Date, free, no key) carrying only a country code and a year; no redirects, 10 s timeout, responses cached in memory only. No credentials, no files written, no shell commands, no hooks, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: pushary
entries.description: Phone notifications, questions and approvals through Pushary's native brodification approval transport, with optional per-tool gates. Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account (fails closed); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions and wait in ~/.pushary/run/brodification-commands; sends session events with a machine id (~/.pushary/machine-id when present, else a hashed hostname) on every turn, the redacted command and description of each approval it carries, the redacted reason when brodification marks a turn failed (max 200 characters), redacted gated-tool arguments and pushary_remind reminder text to pushary.com; reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through brodification.
known_issues: Updating from 0.5.9: this release reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through brodification. If Pushary setup or the Pushary app gave the old copy its key, save it once with: brodification config set PUSHARY_API_KEY <your key>

entries.name: pushover-brodification-plugin
entries.description: Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers, brodification's sudo password prompt) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests to api.pushover.net only, carrying your Pushover app token, user key and notification text (when lifecycle notifications are enabled, excerpts of agent replies, clarify questions, approval commands, the command waiting on the sudo password prompt (redacted by brodification; never the password) and kanban block reasons; PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_QUESTION=minimal suppresses all but kanban reasons); send_message can address any Pushover user or group key; runs notify-send (argv, no shell) when native notifications are enabled; writes an unrotated log under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/logs and settings.json under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data, and $BRODIFICATION_HOME/.env only from the interactive setup wizard. Outbound-only, no inbound or approval path, no telemetry, no background processes.

entries.name: qdrant-memory
entries.description: Durable native memory for brodification with LLM fact extraction. Conversations are distilled by the brodification-configured LLM into searchable memories — facts, preferences and decisions with deduplication and importance — instead of storing turns verbatim, and are kept in Qdrant (embedded, self-hosted Server, or Qdrant Cloud) with configurable embeddings (default: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b at 2560 dimensions). The plugin registers a native MemoryProvider plus four scoped tools: qdrant_memory_search, qdrant_memory_add, qdrant_memory_update and qdrant_memory_delete. A SQLite WAL admission ledger makes every write idempotent and replayable across restarts with fail-closed recovery; scoped inventory, portable export and scope-aware deletion (list/export/delete-all with explicit single-agent vs all-agents semantics) ship in the same CLI, and `migrate mem0` imports existing Mem0 exports with resumable, verifiable runs. Disclosure — memory text is stored in the configured Qdrant store (embedded files under <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/qdrant-memory/qdrant by default, or the Server/Cloud URL you set), and memory text plus each turn's recall query are sent as plain text to the configured embedding endpoint (default local Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434; an OpenAI-compatible remote endpoint can be configured, and keyed endpoints must use HTTPS). Disclosure — after each primary-agent turn, at session end and before context compression, conversation text goes to the LLM configured in brodification through the brodification plugin LLM facade (a provider/model override needs the plugin's brodification trust grant) to extract facts and to compare near-duplicate memories; that LLM may be a remote provider. Disclosure — the provider is selected with memory.provider: qdrant-memory; its settings live in <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/qdrant-memory.json (0600, secrets stripped on save). QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_API_KEY and EMBEDDING_API_KEY are read through the brodification secret scope, but an api_key written by hand into qdrant-memory.json takes precedence, and `migrate mem0` reads the source Qdrant endpoint and any api_key from <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/mem0.json or --source-config. Disclosure — state lives under <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/qdrant-memory/ (embedded store, SQLite WAL ledger, lock files); the ledger holds raw turn text and pre-compression transcripts until they are processed, and failed items until retried, then scrubs the bodies. Disclosure — single-writer design: a local ownership lock excludes a second writer to the same profile destination, and Server/Cloud deployments expect one active writer per scope. Disclosure — deletion removes records and fences pending operations, but is not a forensic secure erase (SQLite WAL pages and backups may retain content).
known_issues: Preview scope: multi-writer Server/Cloud deployments, hybrid retrieval and a web UI are not supported.
Deletion removes records and fences pending operations but is not a forensic secure erase; storage-level remnants (WAL, backups) may persist.
Embedded mode is single-writer: a second process fails closed on the ownership lock instead of sharing the store.
Extraction adds LLM latency after a turn; memory admission is not guaranteed before the host admits the provider, and pending operations replay on the next start.

entries.name: qdrant
entries.description: Dense semantic memory for brodification, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional recall-indicator display, display.level (off | summary | verbose, default off), adds latency and collection to the chat indicator at summary and one numeric line per operation to the log at verbose — numbers and identifiers only, never recalled message text or search-result snippets (the md_search line also echoes the query you searched — your own input, not recalled content); it is separate from the older top-level progress knob (off | minimal | verbose), which gates status events. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Optional hybrid dense+sparse RRF search (default off): one config key enables dense+BM25 RRF fusion. A fresh collection declares the sparse vector at creation and an existing dense-only store gets it added in place (Qdrant >= 1.18) with one bundled backfill command; measured +0.024 recall@10 on the LongMemEval 1,000-example benchmark. INT8 quantization is not implemented. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the brodification secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights (plus the 10 MB Qdrant/bm25 sparse model when hybrid is on) from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding runs on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials) and last-operation status in <BRODIFICATION_HOME>/qdrant-status.json. Disclosure — md_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.brodification/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/brodification_default, ~/.brodification/brodification-agent/website and any path in the md_docs_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md_ingest.py and lives in <base brodification home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md_ingest.py --semantic, and md_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate brodification_md_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every brodification process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process). Disclosure — the bundled scripts/backfill_memory.py (run by hand; a dry run unless --yes) reads a profile's brodification session database (<profile>/state.db, read-only) and copies every stored user, assistant and tool message from every session source (cli, cron, subagent, gateway), in 2,000-character chunks, into the collection at the url in qdrant.json (default http://localhost:6333); nothing reads state.db unless you run it.
known_issues: Windows on ARM is unsupported: grpcio, pulled in by qdrant-client, has no win_arm64 wheel. Linux and macOS on x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 are supported.
Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported — the provider is REST-only and requires a reachable server.

md_search returns 'no markdown index yet' until you run the bundled ingest script once (python scripts/md_ingest.py, lexical only and fast; add --semantic for the embedding tier, which takes about 7 minutes for 5500 chunks on a 5-core CPU). No background process does this for you.

Running the plugin's pytest suite inside an installed copy still changes the PM dependency stamp (the .pytest_cache directory is hashed as a build input); only an upstream core change can exclude gitignored state.

entries.name: quota
entries.description: Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint using the brodification-quota-plugin User-Agent; optional additional Claude accounts read access tokens only from explicitly configured Claude Code credentials files and send them only to Anthropic's fixed OAuth usage endpoint (read-only, no refresh-token exchange or credential write-back; tokens and paths excluded from the quota cache). Linux extra accounts verified; Windows experimental, extra macOS Keychain accounts unsupported. The openai-codex check reads every saved Codex account from brodification' own auth.json credential pool (read-only, never refreshed; expired accounts show reauth-required) and queries the Codex usage endpoint with the codex-cli User-Agent; the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json, brodification' auth.json pool and OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY_N variables (read-only). The cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check reads local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux or the macOS Keychain for the browser's Safe Storage key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or brodification' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek, openrouter, ollama (which may read OLLAMA_API_KEY from ~/.brodification/.env and calls ollama.com/api/usage and /api/me) and experientiallabs send keys from brodification' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints.

entries.name: quote-ask
entries.title: Quote & Ask
entries.description: Codex-style ask-about-selection for brodification Desktop: select text anywhere in a conversation, and a small pill appears above the selection offering Quote & ask — the selection lands in the message composer as a Markdown quote with the caret on the line below, ready for your question — or Copy, which puts the same Markdown quote on the clipboard. A command-palette entry does the same without the pill. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars, nothing written to disk, nothing persisted. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; serializes the selection to Markdown (fenced code with its language, nested lists, bold/italic, links), cut at 4000 characters; writes the draft through host.composer (getDraft/setDraft, falling back to insertText, then ctx.os.writeClipboard) and focuses the composer; ignores selections made inside the composer itself and hides on collapse, scroll or Escape. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: quotum
entries.description: A quotum seat's Venice key as a provider. Private and anonymized models, with the seat's daily cap, spend and the 20:00 UTC bell in /usage, and a Seals tab in brodification dashboard with the seat's record. Disclosure — prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY go to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage and the Seals tab send a 16-hex sha256 handle of the key to quotum.org, then the Seals tab reads the seat's public record from quotum.org (the key itself is never sent there); QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 swaps in its own client that drops brodification web_search for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token
known_issues: The optional QUOTUM_X_SEARCH mode supplies its own client through create_client, so it works with plugins.isolation in_process (the default) only; under host isolation leave it off.
brodification' bundled Achievements page has no hook for outside achievements, so the seat's seals live in the plugin's own Seals tab.

entries.name: rea-captcha
entries.description: Inspect captured browser verification evidence locally when an agent task is interrupted by a CAPTCHA. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (pinned stateless mcp.json + skill); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ with npx on PATH. Disclosure — on first start brodification runs `npx rea-captcha@0.3.1`, which downloads that exact npm package and its dependencies (incl. Playwright) from the npm registry; the catalog config is stateless, so only the read-only, local captcha_analyze works and the browser-session tools fail closed until you configure a separate stateful server; no telemetry, hosted solver, browser-profile copying, or cookie/token transfer.

entries.name: rea
entries.description: Reverse engineer programs with REA (rea.tools): native binaries, .NET assemblies, Electron/JavaScript apps, Android packages, firmware and browser/process activity, through REA's MCP server (pinned rea-agents@6.7.0 over npx stdio) with REA's reverse-engineer-anything skill adapted for brodification. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ on PATH, plus your own Ghidra, Hopper or IDA for native decompilation. Disclosure — a few REA tools run a command under a PTY, launch or drive an application, change a connected Android device or overwrite a chosen file, and brodification does not prompt before them; the bundled skill tells the agent to ask first and to skip them in unattended runs.

entries.name: reaction-feedback
entries.description: Lets the agent see the emoji reactions you leave on its Telegram messages: react 👍 or 👎 to a reply and the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the message it followed. Disclosure — registers pre_gateway_dispatch (always returns None, so dispatch is never changed), pre_llm_call and gateway_platform_event hooks; keeps a bounded in-memory record of private-chat message ids, 60-character excerpts and reactions; writes nothing to disk, makes no network requests, starts no processes and reads no secrets.

entries.name: reaction-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the emoji reactions people leave on messages in your Telegram chats with brodification: /reaction-log counts each message once, with the reactions it has now, and shows per emoji how many messages carry it, in how many chats and how long ago it was last set, or per day with the day's most used emoji, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, or everything recorded; /reaction-log recent lists the newest reaction changes (ten, or up to 100 with /reaction-log recent 50). Only reactions the gateway authorizes reach it. Disclosure — subscribes to gateway_platform_event as an observer only and ignores every event but a reaction change; writes the emoji a message has after the change, a count of custom emoji and 12-digit hashes of the chat and message ids (never a user id, user name or message text) to plugin-data/reaction-ledger/reactions.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

entries.name: reading-buddy
entries.description: Local-first WeRead (微信读书) reading companion: syncs bookshelf, reading stats and notes to the local machine and turns them into private reading cards and weekly/monthly reviews through 8 MCP tools, with a built-in fictional demo mode for previews. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (e5f6673) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 20+ on PATH. All data stays in PLUGIN_DATA; never posts to WeRead — cards and reviews are local files saved only after user confirmation. Disclosure — live mode sends your WEREAD_API_KEY as a Bearer token plus book ids and paging cursors to i.weread.qq.com (Tencent's WeRead agent gateway) and nothing else; the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first; the engine's npm dependencies resolve as caret ranges at first launch.

entries.name: reasoning-switch
entries.description: Rotate the focused session reasoning effort from the status bar. A dialog sets the levels, colors, and per-level prompt limits. Disclosure — changes the focused session's reasoning effort through the gateway config.set API (core may fall back to writing the global config.yaml when the session id is stale) and auto-demotes the level after the configured number of prompts.

entries.name: recency-anchor
entries.description: Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop

entries.name: redaction-pack
entries.description: Teaches brodification's built-in secret redactor 71 more vendor credential formats (HashiCorp Vault, Doppler, Amazon Bedrock, Atlassian, Cloudflare, Supabase, Tailscale, Docker Hub, JFrog Artifactory, CircleCI, HubSpot, PostHog, Grafana, Sentry, Shopify and others) through register_redaction_patterns, so those tokens are masked in logs, tool output and model-bound text like the built-in ones. Disclosure — register() makes one call, ctx.register_redaction_patterns; no tools, hooks, network access, subprocesses, files or environment variables; the patterns can only add masks, and security.redact_secrets: false still turns redaction off.

entries.name: redline
entries.description: Guided Markdown and source-code review in brodification Desktop — annotate passages or line-numbered code in a docked pane and send comment/question/change-request batches back to the agent; cards are offered automatically on delivered Markdown. Disclosure — reads any user-selected local .md/.markdown or source-code path (.py .sh .js .ts .tsx .c .h .cpp .go .rs .rb .yaml .yml .json .toml .sql, so config files such as config.yaml or auth.json are shown if you open them) up to 1 MB (symlink-resolved), writes only a <file>.redline.json sidecar beside it, and in brodification Desktop chats the transform_llm_output hook appends a ::redline directive line to qualifying final agent responses; syntax highlighting uses Pygments in the local gateway host with plain-text fallback; no network beyond the local gateway, no credentials, no telemetry, no subprocesses; the pane polls the local backend every 3 s while open.

entries.name: remarkable
entries.description: Unofficial reMarkable cloud transfers, library management, backups, typed text, and bounded native notebook rendering. Disclosure — talks to reMarkable cloud with a device token under ~/.brodification/credentials/remarkable/; remarkable_upload sends model-chosen local PDF/EPUB files to your account; the cloud sidecar (Node 22+) and renderer venv are installed only by the human-run setup commands; USB/SSH off by default.

entries.name: reme
entries.description: Local-first, file-native long-term memory with HTTP and embedded ReMe backends. Disclosure — search queries and full user/assistant turns are sent to the configured ReMe endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:2333; a non-loopback http:// endpoint receives them in plaintext) or handled by the in-process ReMe SDK; no API keys are forwarded.

entries.name: render-platform
entries.title: Render
entries.description: Deploy, debug and manage Render applications with 20 unchanged skills from render-oss/skills and Render's hosted MCP connection. Disclosure — connects brodification to Render's hosted MCP server (mcp.render.com) with your RENDER_API_KEY; the server is marked untrusted so tools without a read-only annotation need approval; account permissions apply and changes can incur Render charges; bundled skills guide shell commands, file edits and Render CLI installs (including the vendor's curl | sh installer).
known_issues: render-docker is excluded because its upstream Dockerfile cleanup example triggers a critical scanner rule.
Render's list_workspaces lacks a read-only annotation and requires approval; unattended calls are denied.
An existing native mcp_servers.render configuration overrides the package connection and trust setting.

entries.name: replaid
entries.description: Connect Replaid with OAuth to read, triage, and draft replies in your social inbox.

entries.name: requesty
entries.title: Requesty
entries.description: Requesty LLM gateway as a brodification model provider (`--provider requesty`, alias `rq`, or Requesty in `brodification model`). The picker lists Requesty's managed routing policies (curated routes with failover, `@eu` variants for EU-only hosting); any Requesty model id or org policy also works. `/reasoning` maps onto Requesty's `reasoning_effort` for reasoning-capable models, the brodification session id is sent as `requesty.trace_id`, and context windows and estimated cost come from the Requesty catalog. Prompt caching is done server-side by Requesty. Disclosure — chat requests go to https://router.requesty.ai/v1 (or REQUESTY_BASE_URL) through brodification' own client with REQUESTY_API_KEY, which brodification reads; the plugin itself only fetches Requesty's public model catalogs (/v1/models/managed and /v1/models, no credentials), once per process, sometimes on a short-lived background thread. No attribution headers, telemetry, file access or processes. Supersedes #27908.

entries.name: rfc-ref
entries.description: @rfc:<number> context references: attach an IETF RFC's record from the RFC Editor to a message (title, status, date, authors, abstract, what it obsoletes and updates and what obsoletes or updates it, errata link). Disclosure — sends one HTTPS GET per reference to www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc<number>.json only (the referenced RFC number leaves the machine); no API key, no caching, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @rfc: reference provider.

entries.name: rocketchat-platform
entries.description: Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for brodification. Connects to a self-hosted Rocket.Chat instance via the REST API v1 for outbound traffic and the Realtime (DDP) WebSocket for inbound messages. Uses aiohttp (already a brodification dependency) — no extra packages needed.

entries.name: rply-platform
entries.title: rply
entries.description: rply gateway platform: talk to brodification from the rply inbox on your phone and laptop, with web push. Messages and files both ways, seen/working/done with a live activity note, clarify questions and command approvals as tappable questions, cron delivery, a pinned table of scheduled jobs, a dashboard app with run/pause/resume, and an rply_request_secret tool that saves API keys to the profile's .env without the value passing through the chat. Each profile joins the channel as its own agent. Disclosure — keeps a long-polling connection to the configured rply server only (RPLY_SERVER, default https://app.rply.sh; self-hostable, AGPL server); messages the channel's members send reach brodification as user instructions and members answer its approval and clarify prompts; the dashboard sends the server brodification' cron job list, the titles and previews of the 10 most recent sessions from every platform, token and cost totals and the default model, and runs, pauses or resumes jobs when its buttons are pressed; stores the agent token in the profile's .env, an X25519 keypair in <profile>/rply/secret-key.json (0600) and secrets the human provides in the profile's .env under a variable name the agent picks (core's env denylist applies; the .env path is sent to the server with the request); the secret tool waits up to 15 minutes for the human and refuses under cron; adds a `brodification rply` setup command; credentials read through brodification' profile-scoped route; no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: rss-reader
entries.description: Desktop RSS reader with reader-mode capture, drag-reorder subscriptions, mute rules, saved searches, AI summaries, keyboard shortcuts, and an optional headline ticker. Disclosure — optional YouTube cookies you paste in Settings are sent with YouTube feed requests; selectable User-Agent presets (incl. a ChatGPT-User string) are sent to feed hosts; YouTube videos render as youtube-nocookie.com embed iframes inside the reader.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite-docker
entries.description: Community plugin that rewrites brodification terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local), so a Docker or remote backend without rtk never receives an rtk command. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the brodification host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite
entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites brodification terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands. Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/brodification/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).

entries.name: runbox
entries.title: runbox
entries.description: Build, run and test Python in an offline container per chat, with results as a plain file:line issue list. The agent syncs files or folders in as copies, then runs run (a shell command), check (ruff error rules) and test (pytest); fixes stay in the box until the user asks for export, which writes changed files back through write_file and reports host files changed since the sync as conflicts. In brodification Desktop a VS Code-style editor opens beside the chat: file tabs with in-place editing, Run / Check / Test / Stop, and PROBLEMS / OUTPUT / RUNS panels that follow the agent live. Ships the runbox:dev-loop starting-point skill. Disclosure — needs Docker (on macOS a dedicated colima profile 'runbox', started on demand with --activate=false and its own Docker config); pulls the container image pinned by digest and installs a hash-pinned checker toolchain (ruff 0.16.9, pytest 9.1.1 and deps) from PyPI once per image; the work container has no network, hardened flags, and runs commands without brodification' dangerous-command approval like brodification' Docker backend; install (PyPI) always asks for approval in a separate installer container; a write_file/patch on an imported original asks for approval (guard_imports); export reads each existing target through read_file before replacing it; a background thread removes idle containers (15 min), stops the VM, and removes boxes of deleted or long-idle chats (reads state.db read-only hourly); adds a short per-turn note (about 80 tokens); no credentials or telemetry.
known_issues: Needs Docker: on macOS install colima and the docker CLI (brew install colima docker); on Linux a running Docker daemon. The first start on macOS downloads the VM image and takes a few minutes.
The brodification data folder must be under your home folder on macOS (colima shares only that).
The agent may not always pick runbox on its own (the model chooses its tools). Ask it to use runbox.

entries.name: s3
entries.description: Generic S3-compatible backup and restore operations for brodification

entries.name: sabi-metadata
entries.description: Fail-closed attribution middleware for Sabi's local adaptive routing lane (sabi-code). Adds opaque session/turn headers on loopback only; ignores all other models. Verified on brodification 0.21.3.

entries.name: safeailabs-provider
entries.title: Safe AI Labs
entries.description: Safe AI Labs as a brodification model provider (`--provider safeailabs`, or Safe AI Labs in `brodification model`): an OpenAI-compatible API with one endpoint per region, the model list from its /v1/models and the context window of its fallback model declared. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://us.api.safeailabs.ai/v1 (or SAFE_AI_BASE_URL) through brodification' own client with SAFE_AI_KEY, which brodification reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: salesforce-chatter
entries.title: Salesforce Chatter
entries.description: Talk to brodification from Salesforce Chatter: @mention the bot user in a post or comment, it Likes the message as an acknowledgement and replies in the same thread, keeping the thread as one session. Images and files on the post are passed to the model; MEDIA files are attached back. Community plugin, not affiliated with Salesforce. Disclosure — authenticates as a dedicated bot user with the OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer flow, reading the private key file at SF_CHATTER_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH; talks to the configured Salesforce login host and the org instance (attachment downloads follow Salesforce redirects); image URLs in the agent's replies are fetched from the gateway host over HTTPS (any public host; private, loopback and metadata addresses are refused) and uploaded to Chatter; polls the To Me feed every 60 s and, for allowlisted groups, runs a SOQL probe every 5 s by default (counts against the org API quota); writes Likes, comments, files in the bot user's Files and optional home-channel posts; keeps its ledger in plugin-data/salesforce-chatter/inbox.sqlite. dry_run defaults to true (no Salesforce writes, no outbound image fetch); with SF_CHATTER_ALLOWED_USERS unset nobody is answered. Optional, off by default: html_preview renders model-generated HTML to PNG with Chromium in a network-isolated Docker container (digest-pinned image, pulled if missing). No telemetry.

entries.name: scalekit
entries.title: Scalekit
entries.description: Call any Scalekit connector from brodification: 500+ connectors and 20,000+ tools. Disclosure — HTTP calls go to the Scalekit environment URL you paste; the three Scalekit values are read with get_secret; one person id is stored at plugin-data/scalekit/identifier; the model can request an approval link, run a named tool, or proxy one HTTP request. Provider tokens stay in Scalekit; no shell, no background process, no telemetry.

entries.name: scamgate
entries.description: Offline scam gate. Blocks known-bad links and payments before a tool runs, and asks a human when it cannot see the destination. Disclosure — blocks agent tool calls that would edit brodification config/profiles/plugins/hooks or turn approvals off, and with approvals off turns its "ask" into a block (setting when_approvals_off: allow restores asks); keeps its signing key and ask log under ~/.local/state/scamgate and phishing feeds under ~/.cache/scamgate (not per-profile); feeds download only when you run `scamgate update-feeds` (openphish.com, Phishing-Database on GitHub, optional urlhaus); optional SCAMGATE_RDAP=live sends each checked link's domain to its RDAP registry.

entries.name: search1api
entries.description: Live web search, news, Ask, page crawl, sitemap, and trending via Search1API

entries.name: secret-drop
entries.description: Store a secret on the gateway host without showing it to the model. Disclosure — stores the value in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600) and adds the name to terminal.env_passthrough, so $NAME is available to the terminal tool; the model can still read the value with its own tools (cat .env, echo $NAME). Keeps secrets out of chat/prompt context and redacts verbatim output of credential-shaped values; it is not a boundary against a model that deliberately reads it. Adds a static system-prompt section and a /secret command. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_brodification_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK).

entries.name: secret-handoff
entries.description: Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. Disclosure — the reply is typed into the focused field of the page whose origin matches the requested service, over the endpoint from BROWSER_CDP_URL or SECRET_HANDOFF_CDP_URL; the answer is visible in the CLI scrollback or the chat history of the surface that asked, and the value is never written to disk, the tool result, or the session transcript.

entries.name: secure-env-ingress
entries.description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys and payment cards, protected hosted payment-field filling, nested HTTPS verification codes/passcodes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre_gateway_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. In interactive Telegram sessions, secure_env_vault saves logins or fills a code field through the captured browser supervisor without explicitly submitting the site form. Explicit parent payment/nested-code targeting requires compatible host task/profile ownership and browser-generation evidence and fails closed without it; this is not a general fix for native Vault named-tab selection. Payment filling requires separate native consent and exact document/control guards; explicit resume requires existing nonempty values to match Vault. Site input callbacks, especially 3-D Secure, may authorize or auto-submit an operation. Unknown outcomes require external verification before retry. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer.

entries.name: sem-weave
entries.description: CLI-backed skills for local code discovery and entity-diff review with Sem, plus optional Weave branch-merge previews. Requires user-installed CLIs; does not apply edits or merges, install binaries, or change Git configuration.
known_issues: Requires Ataraxy Sem on the host terminal's PATH; Weave is optional for merge previews.
Tested with Sem 0.27.0 and Weave 0.5.4 on macOS; Windows shell instructions are not included.

entries.name: sendblue
entries.description: Sendblue iMessage / SMS integration. Provides typing indicators, async daemon routing, and Active LLM Tools for SMS dispatch.

entries.name: senler-io-user
entries.title: Senler.io
entries.description: Get task-specific guidance for Senler agents, automations and knowledge, connect your account through MCP OAuth, and automate selected webhook events with an outbound Relay connection. Disclosure — brodification installs the declared `python-socks[asyncio]` dependency for native SOCKS proxy support. First activation of the enabled plugin adds a `senler-io-user` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by brodification) to the profile's config.yaml and records completion through plugin settings, which native uninstall clears. Reinstalling and enabling the plugin prepares a missing MCP again. The old durable marker from 0.5.2–0.5.3 is ignored, so upgrading restores a missing entry once, including an entry manually removed before this upgrade. Existing compatible and disabled connections are preserved; later loads in the same installation respect manual removal. Explicit chat setup can restore a removed connection. Relay setup enables a `senler-io` gateway platform in the same profile. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is `trusted_inbound`, so these events bypass brodification allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook allows the Senler MCP and native tool discovery and pins customer replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a brodification approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in `<BRODIFICATION_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. Configured monitoring also stores notification recipients, queued texts and delivery receipts in that database; the selected native brodification messaging adapter sends summaries and delivery-test messages to the saved recipient.
known_issues: After updating, restart the backend used by Desktop and the gateway; a new chat alone may still use older loaded plugin code.
Preview: Windows Desktop sign-in was previously confirmed; automatic MCP appearance still needs a Desktop UI check, and a real Senler Relay workflow needs end-to-end verification.
Requires current brodification with native MCP OAuth and Relay transport; gateway proxy mode and multiplexed profiles are unsupported.
Monitoring notifications require a connected messaging channel; arbitrary Desktop/TUI chats are unsupported.

entries.name: serpapi
entries.description: SerpApi web, Maps, News, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, and Travel Explore for brodification.
entries.title: SerpApi

entries.name: session-dashboard
entries.description: Session Analyzer — per-session analytics for the brodification desktop app: full page at /session-dashboard with token/cache/cost aggregates, tool-call breakdown, file changes, failure groups, and Ask AI (copies a ready-to-run analysis prompt into a fresh draft chat). Read-only over state.db.

entries.name: session-flow
entries.description: Session pane for brodification Desktop: Firefox-style session groups with project grouping, list/grid views, Ctrl+Scroll session cycling with a HUD, session-row styling and a built-in settings page. All timers are ctx-owned intervals disposed on unload (live-session poll ~30 s, session refresh ~45 s, project cache 60 s, activity expiry 30 s). The standalone full build in this repo (full/plugin.js, install.sh) is not part of this catalog entry. Contact: info@agantila.com. Disclosure — SDK-only Desktop plugin: reads the local brodification gateway through public RPCs (projects.tree, projects.list, session.list, session.active_list, session.context_breakdown) and, on your actions, writes through public RPCs (projects.create/update/add_folder/remove_folder/set_primary/set_active/delete, session.create, session.cwd.set, session.title, session.branch_stored, session.archive, session.close, session.delete); captures Ctrl+mouse-wheel across the app (browser zoom suppressed except over canvases, editors and zoomable images) to cycle sessions; settings and groups stay in the app's local plugin storage; no outbound network, no shell commands, no credentials, no self-update.

entries.name: session-lens
entries.title: brodification Session Lens
entries.description: Read-only observability for brodification Desktop: what each session cost and why, its full trace, recurring tool failures, every profile at a glance, provider quotas and service balances, model comparison with cheaper-route evidence, and instruction-rule grading. Disclosure — reads every profile's state.db read-only plus agent logs, cron/gateway state, config.yaml and .env (key names, and the values of keys an adapter uses); with the credentials brodification' own resolvers return, calls only each configured vendor's usage or balance endpoint (hosts listed in the README), sending Grok CLI client headers to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and a Claude Code user-agent to api.anthropic.com; brodification' resolvers may renew brodification' Codex, Nous and xAI logins and, when brodification holds no other Anthropic credential, Claude Code's login; runs the local monid CLI when installed; an Anthropic one-token Claude Haiku probe is off by default; writes no brodification state itself and sends no session content anywhere.

entries.name: session-mirror
entries.description: Mirrors brodification Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post_llm_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after brodification's redact_for_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $BRODIFICATION_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `brodification session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $BRODIFICATION_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread.

entries.name: session-ref
entries.description: Reference another brodification session in the Desktop composer with @session — type @ and pick from live session suggestions. Inserts a compact @session:"<title>" reference; nothing is injected into context, the agent resolves it with its own session-search. No more copying session IDs.

entries.name: session-token-counter
entries.description: Accumulated input/output token totals and context-window occupancy for the focused session, in the brodification Desktop status bar.

entries.name: shodan
entries.description: Shodan tools with complete capability declarations.

entries.name: showly
entries.title: Showly
entries.description: Preview, publish, and manage websites hosted on Showly from brodification, through the hosted Showly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — tool calls go to Showly's hosted MCP server at mcp.showly.ai. The bundled showly-hosting skill makes Showly the default for any deploy, preview or share request that names no provider, and new links default to public (anyone with the link). The showly-reports skill runs a bundled local Node.js renderer (vendored answer-me-with-html 0.4.14, upstream self-update check removed) through the shell and uploads the report directory to Showly when sharing is requested. Sign-in is out of band: `npx @showly/mcp-server login --to brodification` (unpinned) writes MCP_SHOWLY_API_KEY into ~/.brodification/config.yaml.
known_issues: Sign-in needs one command after install, because a portable mcp.json cannot carry a credential: npx @showly/mcp-server login --to brodification

entries.name: sidebar-cycle
entries.description: Step through brodification Desktop sidebar sessions in on-screen order with Ctrl+Cmd+] / Ctrl+Cmd+[ (rebindable), wrapping at both ends. SDK-only: session-row slot markers for order, host.state for the focused session, host.openSession for navigation.

entries.name: sidebar-manager
entries.description: Hide and reorder core sidebar navigation rows from a statusbar dialog.

entries.name: sigrex
entries.description: Build, run and manage sigrex.io trading automation (code and AI strategies, trading bots, webhooks and signals across crypto exchanges, DEXs and prediction markets) through the official Sigrex MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sigrex.io, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with the sigrex workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a free Sigrex account. The connection has full account access, including actions that can place live trades. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill instructs the agent to confirm before any action that moves money or changes data.

entries.name: singularity
entries.description: Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend: brodification's terminal, file and code tools run inside a hardened, rootless container on this machine (--containall --no-home), with CPU/memory limits and an optional per-session persistent overlay (`brodification config set terminal.backend singularity`; image from `terminal.singularity_image`). Formerly built into brodification core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it drives the `apptainer` (or `singularity`) CLI you install, which pulls the configured image (default `docker://nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop`) and caches a SIF under your scratch directory. Your skills and registered credential files are bind-mounted read-only into the container, and because the container is a disposable sandbox brodification skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as for its other container backends.

entries.name: sketch-pad
entries.description: Draw a shape on a Desktop pad and attach the PNG to the next brodification chat message. For "what is this shape" when you have no photo.

entries.name: skill-integrity
entries.description: Rug-pull detection for installed agent skills — fingerprints every file in every skill directory (SHA-256), keeps a profile-local snapshot, and reports exactly which skill files changed, appeared, or vanished since; a skill that mutates after install without the user touching it is the rug-pull signal. A skill directory made unreadable is reported as a finding, never treated as clean. Read-only observer, stdlib-only, zero network calls; blind spots (oversize files, symlinks, permission-denied) are counted and printed, never silent. The wrapper registers an hourly pre_llm_call hook that injects findings into the agent context, plus a /skill-integrity slash command (snapshot | check | show) that creates the baseline snapshot and shows the file-level diff. The CLI supports --state-dir to target the plugin's manifest directly. Skill dirs and state derive from get_brodification_home(), covering non-default profiles. Disclosure — reads (hash-only, read-only) every file under the active profile's skills directory and ~/.claude/skills, stores a mode-0600 snapshot in BRODIFICATION_HOME/plugin-data/skill-integrity, and at most hourly injects the names of changed skills into the agent's context.

entries.name: skill-retrieval
entries.description: BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $BRODIFICATION_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.

entries.name: skill-router
entries.description: Evidence-based, session-safe skill routing with auditable decisions and opt-in learning

entries.name: snag-shelf
entries.description: Everything that snagged - cross-session shelf of failed tool calls. Full Desktop page, chip, pin, fix-prompt insert. No API keys. Disclosure — stores failed tool-call metadata (tool, truncated args with key-name redaction, error snippet) locally in plugin-data; no network.

entries.name: snyk
entries.description: Scan code (SAST), dependencies, container images, IaC and SBOMs with Snyk through its first-party MCP server (pinned snyk@1.1306.0 over npx stdio, CLI analytics disabled), with the snyk-security-scan workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH and a free Snyk account (browser login via the snyk_auth tool).

entries.name: source-tray
entries.description: Session source tray — URLs the brodification agent opened via web_search, web_extract, or browser_navigate. Desktop pane and /sources. No search backend of its own and no API keys.

entries.name: specstream
entries.description: SpecStream gives brodification finished lists from the live web: describe the list in plain words and get every matching row with the page it was read from, priced per match with a maximum you approve before anything runs. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and four skills (compile, review-work, approve-work, continue-work); no Python, no executables, no stored credentials. Disclosure — your request text and your answers to the price are sent to api.specstream.ai; approving a price spends your SpecStream balance (new accounts get $10 free) and the plugin marks its server `untrusted`, so brodification asks before every call that is not read-only and refuses those calls in unattended runs; a `specstream` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.
entries.title: SpecStream

entries.name: spectator
entries.description: Harness-neutral live session sharing, summaries, and branch queries. Disclosure — reads state.db read-only and exposes masked transcripts to invite-token guests on the dashboard; host-approved guest suggestions are injected via ctx.inject_message.

entries.name: speechify
entries.title: Speechify
entries.description: The official Speechify text-to-speech provider (tts.provider: speechify), maintained by Speechify. Simba 3 voices with low-latency streaming in voice mode, Opus voice notes for messaging platforms, and a brodification speechify command to list voices and hear a test line. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice and model, the plugin's name and version (Speechify-Caller attribution headers), and your SPEECHIFY_API_KEY to api.speechify.ai (or the base_url / SPEECHIFY_BASE_URL you configure); synthesis is billed to your Speechify workspace; generated audio is written to brodification's audio cache; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry.
known_issues: Streaming in voice mode needs brodification 0.21.6 or newer; 0.21.5 speaks whole sentences instead.

entries.name: spotify-desktop
entries.description: Spotify Connect remote for brodification Desktop — status-bar mini player (now playing, transport, volume, devices, search, playlists, queue) reusing the brodification Spotify login (Spotify Premium required for playback control). Unified agent+desktop package: Electron status-bar player plus a dashboard-API backend (desktop-focused, no web UI). No agent tools; config via plugins.entries.spotify-desktop.settings (poll intervals).
known_issues: On brodification releases where Spotify moved to the `spotify` plugin, the player needs spotify-desktop with cruzlxyz/brodification-spotify-desktop#2 plus `brodification plugins install spotify` (login: `brodification spotify login`); this pin predates that change.

entries.name: spotify
entries.description: Spotify for brodification: seven tools (playback, devices, queue, search, playlists, albums, library) over the Spotify Web API, plus `brodification spotify login|status|logout` (loopback PKCE with your own Spotify developer app; Premium needed for playback control). Formerly built into brodification core; existing users are migrated automatically.

entries.name: stack
entries.description: Git-backed Markdown memory with background curation and model-based recall. Disclosure — runs a background curation agent with terminal, file-read and patch tools on your configured auxiliary model, fed raw conversation turns; it commits and pushes the memory store to whatever git remotes you configure, and pulls shared submodules at session start; the engine runs via uv run, which fetches pyyaml==6.0.2 from PyPI; an optional dataset file (memory.stack.dataset_enabled, off by default) stores full transcripts locally with no rotation.

entries.name: stalkchain
entries.title: StalkChain
entries.description: Crypto research in plain English through the official StalkChain Data MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://data.stalkchain.com/mcp/directory, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check a coin before you buy, vet a trader before you copy them, see what smart money is buying, review a wallet and set price alerts, across Solana, Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Monad, Hyperliquid and Robinhood Chain, plus the StonkFun launchpad. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + 18 skills), no Python or executables; needs a StalkChain account with credits. Read-only: never trades, moves funds or signs anything; the only write is the user's own price alerts, after they confirm. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; each tool call sends the tool name and its inputs to data.stalkchain.com and spends the account's credits; price alerts are stored by StalkChain with their destination (account email or a user-given Discord, Slack or Telegram webhook URL, which can embed a bot token) until deleted or fired.

entries.name: sticky-notes
entries.description: In-window sticky notes for brodification Desktop.

entries.name: stop-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the turns you stopped while brodification was still working (/stop, or /new and /reset during a running turn, on messaging platforms, the TUI and the desktop app): /stop-log shows how many running turns were stopped, how many by /stop and by /new, in how many sessions and how long ago the last one was, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /stop-log recent lists the newest stops (ten, or up to 100 with /stop-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes stop metadata (platform, /stop or /new, brodification's label for the stop, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no session key or chat content) to plugin-data/stop-ledger/stops.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay or undo a stop; no network

entries.name: storm-fusion-research
entries.description: Human-gated perspective-panel research. One question, several seats, one judge, one human. Solo, native subagent panel, or per-seat MoA/Fusion fanout via the storm_run_panel tool. Disclosure — every seat/judge call runs through brodification's plugin LLM lane on your own credentials; with llm.allow_provider_override / allow_model_override enabled the agent picks provider and model per seat and spend follows that choice. The human gates are skill instructions to the agent, not enforced by the tool.

entries.name: stream-speed
entries.description: How fast each model starts answering and how fast it writes: /speed shows the median and p90 time to first text and the median characters per second per model, provider or day, or lists the newest streams (ten, or up to 100 with /speed recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded, from the streaming hooks. Disclosure — writes per-response stream timings (ids, model, timings, character count, no text) to plugin-data/stream-speed/streams.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; atexit waits up to 1 s; no network

entries.name: stt-vocab
entries.description: Puts the names a speech-to-text model mis-hears into the transcription prompt brodification sends with each voice message: terms you list (globally or per surface) and names found in this profile's memories/USER.md and MEMORY.md, most important last, within the 896 characters brodification keeps for Whisper-family backends; your stt.prompt stays in front. Notes written in German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese or Turkish can be named in the languages setting. Disclosure — register() adds one pre_transcription hook that returns a new prompt string; memory-derived names go only to local backends (faster-whisper, local_command) unless allow_remote is set, and the memory files are not read otherwise; reads at most 256 KB per memory file; no tools, network access, subprocesses or writes; brodification uploads the prompt with the audio to the configured STT provider.

entries.name: sugar
entries.description: Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: sunshine-moonlight
entries.description: Set up and diagnose Moonlight game streaming (Sunshine host <-> Moonlight client) between machines that run brodification. One tool, action-based: discover hosts on the tailnet/LAN, preflight ports, install+start Sunshine, pair clients, verify encoders, and launch a stream. Writes to remote machines only over SSH and only when the action says so. Disclosure — runs shell commands as your user on this machine and, over SSH, on hosts you name (BatchMode, your existing keys); `install` runs `sudo` with your package manager to install `sunshine` or `moonlight-qt` without a brodification approval prompt; `configure`/`start` rewrite Sunshine's config (with a backup) and restart its user service; `discover` reads `tailscale status` and port-probes your tailnet peers; `launch` starts a Moonlight process. No credentials stored, no telemetry.
entries.title: Sunshine / Moonlight

entries.name: superlocalmemory
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory for brodification, kept on your own computer: recall before each turn, tool-outcome logging, opt-in turn capture, 16 skills and /slm commands. Disclosure — talks only to the `superlocalmemory` MCP server you configure and grant in `plugins.entries.superlocalmemory.mcp_allowlist` (on this computer, or on another one with `connection: remote`): each turn's user message (redacted) is sent for recall and every tool call's arguments and result (redacted, up to 2,000 characters each) are logged to it, and with `capture_turns` on every turn is saved; `/slm` commands run the local `slm` CLI, including ones that change SLM and host settings (`/slm upgrade-hosts --apply` writes the plugin's grant into brodification config.yaml); `slm_agent` starts a child agent that inherits the parent session's tools.
entries.title: SuperLocalMemory
known_issues: Grant the plugin its memory server after install: slm upgrade-hosts --host brodification --apply (adds mcp_allowlist: [superlocalmemory]).

entries.name: supermemory
entries.description: Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.

entries.name: switchbot-control
entries.description: SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. No Plug Mini on/off. Locks off unless enabled. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Each call reads SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. Every command asks for brodification approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your brodification gateway can request a command and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. Not tested on real devices. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

entries.name: t3-code-theme
entries.title: T3 Code Theme
entries.description: Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for brodification Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.

entries.name: tabella
entries.description: Document lifecycle for agents in one package: create .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.pdf/.odt/.ods/.odp from structured JSON or raw HTML/CSS, convert between formats via pandoc + LaTeX, and read any document — anydoc (Rust, office formats and text PDFs to Markdown, in-process) with LiteParse + Tesseract OCR fallback for scanned PDFs and images, plus PDF text editing with output-directory guards. Ships as an Agent Plugins v1 package (auto-discovered plugin.json + mcp.json declaring a stdio MCP server — the client spawns it per the v1 lifecycle, PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA injected — plus an optional self-host streamable-HTTP server; first run of either bootstraps the dependency venv). The HTTP lane binds to 127.0.0.1 only and requires Bearer auth out of the box: a random token is generated into PLUGIN_DATA on first run (TABELLA_TOKEN overrides); requests with an Origin header or a non-JSON body are rejected, and model-supplied HTML cannot fetch network or local-file resources (data: URIs only — the same fetcher now also guards CSS input, not just HTML). Pandoc invocations are argument-safe: extra_args is allowlisted (--toc, --number-sections, -V key=value) and from_format/to_format are validated against the built-in format-name grammar (^[a-z0-9_]+([+-][a-z0-9_]+)*$), closing pandoc's *.lua reader/writer code-exec path; both servers re-exec into the dependency venv after bootstrap. Disclosure — Python deps (python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx, weasyprint, odfpy, Pillow, lxml, PyMuPDF, firecrawl-anydoc, liteparse — 10 direct packages, transitives included in a 25-package closure) are pinned to exact versions with sha256 hashes in requirements-pinned.txt and installed by scripts/setup.sh with --require-hashes into a venv under PLUGIN_DATA or ~/.venvs/docs; system packages pandoc and texlive-xetex are required for PDF conversion (weasyprint for HTML->PDF); OCR needs the tesseract binary; all conversion, reading, OCR and PDF editing run locally with no network or telemetry; nothing is uploaded; read, convert, and PDF-edit tools access exactly the filesystem paths you pass; doc_create_document additionally containment-checks its output paths against the configured output directory (escape warns). Linux is the tested platform.

entries.name: tailgate
entries.description: Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs brodification hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.

entries.name: talaria-webui
entries.description: Extends brodification API capabilities to deliver a richer chat interface with Talaria WebUI. Disclosure — adds API_SERVER_KEY-authenticated /talaria/v1 routes to the brodification API server (cross-session history search, rewind/branch/compress of API sessions, runs with the profile's instructions and prefill); stores response metadata (no message bodies) in $BRODIFICATION_HOME/talaria/observations.db; relies on private api_server/AIAgent internals behind feature detection.

entries.name: tam
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment that carries no credentials: brodification provider keys (including HF_TOKEN and OLLAMA_API_KEY), TAM_API_TOKEN and any *_TOKEN / *_API_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variable are withheld, and of HF_* / OLLAMA_* only non-secret settings pass (OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL, HF_HOME, HF_HUB_OFFLINE); it stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside BRODIFICATION_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; brodification memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.

entries.name: tamabrodification
entries.description: Grow a local Tamabrodification pet from real brodification agent activity. Disclosure — hooks write a pet ledger and sprite atlas under $BRODIFICATION_HOME only; the optional python -m tamabrodification CLI additionally reads/writes ~/.codex, ~/.petdex and ~/.evopet, runs an unauthenticated loopback preview server (127.0.0.1:8765) and on macOS compiles a Swift overlay and installs a RunAtLoad+KeepAlive LaunchAgent with no uninstall command. No network egress, no credential reads.

entries.name: tameru
entries.title: Tameru
entries.description: Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_expand tool brings back the exact original. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Subclasses brodification's built-in ContextCompressor and overrides its private prune/demote methods (checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens brodification's re-prune runway. Adds a model-callable tameru_expand tool that returns pruned tool output from memory or from this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process. No network calls; the render log is off by default.
known_issues: Full archive recovery requires plugins.isolation to be in_process; host mode limits recovery.
Overrides private ContextCompressor signatures and falls back when the host contract changes.

entries.name: teamorouter
entries.title: TeamoRouter
entries.description: TeamoRouter as brodification model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so brodification' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads).
